rules.statement: Some item powers spend charges, regain a stated amount at dawn, and cannot be used again until a specified time; single-use objects may lose their magic when activated.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 216–225, item descriptions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to finite charges with the stated recovery schedule; a world can adjust reserves or recharge rates, with scarcity controlling repeated use.

rules.statement: An item can summon a creature that follows commands for a limited duration, then disappears or returns to its object; some summoned creatures act independently or may disobey.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 220–223, Efreeti Bottle; Elemental Gem; Figurine of Wondrous Power (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a commanded companion with a duration and dismissal condition; a world can alter obedience, duration, or recovery, with risk and upkeep limiting the bond.

rules.statement: Some items impose a condition or control effect on a creature after a failed saving throw; the effect may allow repeat saves, end on a specified event, or persist while a cursed item is worn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 218–220, Dragon Orb; Dust of Sneezing and Choking (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a bounded condition with its stated escape route; a world can change the save or duration, with loss of agency as the cost.

rules.statement: A number of effects alter space: they can bar extradimensional movement, place a target elsewhere, or open a route between planes; these effects differ in which routes they block or permit.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 218, 220, 224–225, Dimensional Shackles; Cubic Gate; Energy Bow; Handy Haversack (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the specific routes or storage limits listed for each effect; a world can broaden access, with confinement, capacity, or dangerous destinations as constraints.

rules.statement: An illusion can conceal or misrepresent a creature or object, but physical interaction or close examination may reveal it; some illusions end when their source moves or is dismissed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 217–218, Cloak of Displacement; Deck of Illusions; page 224, Glamoured Studded Leather (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concealment that fails under the stated inspection or interaction; a world can make detection harder or easier, with exposure to scrutiny as the limitation.

rules.statement: A creature can be transformed into another form by an item, sometimes retaining selected mental abilities; such transformations have a fixed duration or end when the item is no longer used.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 216, Cloak of the Bat; pages 222–223, Figurine of Wondrous Power (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a temporary form with only expressly retained traits; a world can vary duration or retained abilities, with dependence on the item as the cost.

rules.statement: An item can create a bounded area or barrier, or change conditions within an area, with its size and duration set by the item’s effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 216–221, Web; Cube of Force; Eversmoking Bottle; Feather Tokens (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed area and duration; a world can turn the area or persistence dial, with charges, visibility, or environmental conditions limiting use.

rules.statement: Some item effects end when the user takes a specified action, stops meeting a condition, takes damage, or reaches a stated time limit.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 216–225, item descriptions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated ending trigger; a world can make effects more stable or fragile, with damage, movement, or time serving as the balancing cost.

rules.statement: An Ioun Stone activated by tossing it into orbit grants its benefit while orbiting 1d3 feet from the user; no more than three stones can orbit one user at once. The stones count as worn objects and evade collisions and attempts to grab or strike them.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ioun Stone, p. 227 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a limit of three orbiting stones; a world can raise or lower the cap, with greater capacity making stacked benefits easier to obtain.

rules.statement: A Mysterious Deck user declares how many cards to draw, then draws them randomly, no more than 1 hour apart. Undrawn declared cards fly out and take effect together; each drawn card vanishes, then returns to the deck except the Fool and Jester.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mysterious Deck, p. 231 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to declared, random draws with a one-hour interval; a world can alter the interval or how many cards return, changing the risk of repeated effects.

rules.statement: When an Iron Flask captures a qualifying creature, it holds that creature alone until someone releases it; the captive does not age or need air, food, or drink. Release makes the creature obey the releaser for 1 hour, subject to the stated exception for commands likely to cause its death or imprisonment.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Iron Flask, p. 228 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one captive per flask and one hour of compelled service; a world can change either limit, with stronger control increasing the danger of capture.

rules.statement: A creature confined in a closed Portable Hole can force its way out with a successful DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check. The hole contains enough air for 1 hour of breathing, divided among the breathing creatures inside.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Portable Hole, pp. 234–235 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a break-out check and shared one-hour air supply; a world can adjust the check or air duration, making storage more or less survivable.

rules.statement: A Spell Scroll can be read to cast its single spell without material components if the spell is on the reader’s spell list; the scroll is consumed after a completed casting, but not if casting is interrupted. A spell above the reader’s normal casting level requires an ability check against DC 10 plus the spell’s level, and failure consumes the scroll without effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Scroll, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the scroll is single-use and accessible only to an eligible spellcaster; a world could relax the list restriction, at the cost of making stored magic easier to use.

rules.statement: A Ring of Spell Storing holds at most 5 levels of spells. A creature can store a level 1–5 spell by casting it while touching the ring; its attuned wearer can later cast a stored spell using the original caster’s spell parameters, after which that spell’s capacity is freed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Spell Storing, p. 239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: stored spells take up capacity measured in spell levels and retain the original caster’s parameters; a world could change capacity, with fewer or more reusable spells as the tradeoff.

rules.statement: A Rod of Absorption can cancel a spell targeting only its holder if it creates no area, storing the spell’s level as energy instead; it can accumulate at most 50 levels over its lifetime. A spellcaster holding the rod may spend stored levels to create spell slots of level 5 or lower, never exceeding their own maximum slot level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rod of Absorption, p. 241 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the rod converts eligible incoming spells into a finite, reusable reserve; a world could raise the 50-level cap, increasing defensive and casting power.

rules.statement: The Rod of Security transports its user and up to 199 willing creatures to a chosen demiplane, where an hour restores Hit Points as if a Hit Point Die were spent and visitors do not age. Visitors can stay up to 200 days divided by their number; ending the effect or reaching the limit returns them to their original location or the nearest unoccupied space, and the rod cannot be used again for 10 days.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rod of Security, p. 242 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the refuge is safe, temporary, and has a 10-day reuse delay; a world could alter the visitor limit or duration, trading greater shelter for weaker separation from danger.

rules.statement: A Sphere of Annihilation destroys matter that passes through it, except for Artifacts not susceptible to its damage; partial contact deals 8d10 Force damage. A controlled sphere can be moved up to 5 feet per point of the controller’s Intelligence modifier, minimum 5 feet, and a creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by it is obliterated.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphere of Annihilation, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: passage through the sphere destroys matter and its damage can obliterate a victim; a world could narrow what counts as destructible, with reduced lethality.

rules.statement: If a Sphere of Annihilation touches a planar portal or extradimensional space, roll d100: on 01–50 the sphere is destroyed, on 51–85 it enters the portal or space, and on 86–00 it and creatures and objects within 180 feet go to a random plane.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphere Interactions, p. 245 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: contact produces one of three outcomes by the listed probability bands; a world could change the bands, making spatial collisions more or less hazardous.

rules.statement: A Rope of Climbing has AC 20 and 20 Hit Points, is immune to Poison and Psychic damage, and recovers 1 Hit Point every 5 minutes while it has at least 1 Hit Point; at 0 Hit Points it is destroyed. A Rope of Entanglement has the same durability and recovery limits.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rope of Climbing and Rope of Entanglement, pp. 242–243 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these animated ropes repair themselves slowly but are destroyed at 0 Hit Points; a world could change their repair rate, balancing durability against the need to protect them.

rules.statement: Several charged items recover a stated number of expended charges at dawn, while the Ring of Three Wishes becomes nonmagical after its third charge is spent. Some staves and rods also risk destruction when their last charge is used, as specified in their individual entries.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Items with charges, pp. 237–245 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charge recovery and depletion are item-specific, with dawn as the reset point for many; a world could change recovery or depletion, affecting how often powerful effects can be used.

rules.statement: A charged item spends its listed charges to produce effects and typically restores a specified random number of spent charges each dawn. Several items risk destruction or permanent loss of properties when their final charge is used, with the result determined by a d20 roll.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of Healing; Staff of Power; page 246 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to dawn-based charge recovery with an item-specific last-charge risk; worlds can change recovery or failure odds, balancing repeatable magic against possible loss.

rules.statement: The Staff of Power can absorb a spell that targets only its holder, canceling that spell and gaining charges equal to its level; exceeding its 50-charge capacity triggers its destructive release effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of the Magi; page 246 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cancellation and charge storage up to 50; a world can change capacity or absorption scope, with overflow causing a dangerous explosion.

rules.statement: Breaking the Staff of Power releases an explosion in a 30-foot area: its holder has a 50 percent chance to escape to a random plane, otherwise taking 16 damage per charge; other creatures save at DC 17, taking 6 damage per charge or half on success.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of Power; page 247 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a charge-scaled blast and a coin-flip planar escape; a world can alter the escape chance, with destruction of the staff as the price.

rules.statement: A summoned monster disappears after 1 hour, on death, or when dismissed; a summoned monster is worth the experience listed in its statistics if defeated or otherwise neutralized, unless another rule says otherwise.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Stone of Controlling Earth Elementals; page 248; Experience Points; page 256 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a timed, dismissible summon that still grants its listed reward if neutralized; a world can change duration or reward to limit summoning exploits.

rules.statement: A staff can become a Giant Constrictor Snake under its user’s control; the user can command it mentally within 60 feet, and it can revert to staff form, but cannot be reused for 1 hour. If it dies, the staff is destroyed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of the Python (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a controlled creature-form with a one-hour reuse delay and destruction on death; a world can change the delay or survivability, with the living tool at risk.

rules.statement: A creature summoned by magic is worth the experience shown in its stat block if defeated or otherwise neutralized, unless a rule specifies otherwise.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Experience Points; page 256 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: summoned creatures yield listed xp
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to awarding the creature’s listed reward even when summoned; a world can exclude summoned beings to prevent creating reward through magic.

rules.statement: A monster’s type identifies categories that certain effects can target or treat specially, but the type categories themselves provide no rules; descriptive tags likewise add no rules by themselves.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Creature Type; Descriptive Tags; page 254 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: creature categories have no inherent rules
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to using types and tags only when an effect calls for them; a world can attach additional category rules, defining what those categories change.

rules.statement: Attack descriptions distinguish effects that happen only on a hit, only on a miss, or either way; saving-throw effects specify the save, DC, affected creatures, and outcomes of success and failure. A successful save that grants half damage also prevents every other part of that effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Saving Throw Effect Notation (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to resolving only the outcome named for the hit, miss, or save result; a world can change how much successful saves mitigate, at the cost of making effects more or less dangerous.

rules.statement: For damage shown as both a number and a die expression, use one or the other, never both. A monster spell of level 1 or higher is cast at its lowest listed level unless stated otherwise, and cannot be cast at a higher level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Damage Notation; Spellcasting (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: choose one damage value and spell level
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the fixed damage number and minimum spell level; a world can prefer rolled damage or permit stronger spell levels, trading simplicity or restraint for variation or power.

rules.statement: A monster casting a spell with a casting time of at least 1 minute must use the Magic action on each of its turns and maintain Concentration, unless its action description says otherwise. A legendary action can be taken only after another creature’s turn ends, one at a time; the monster spends a use, regaining all uses at the start of its turn, and cannot use one while incapacitated or unable to act.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spellcasting; Legendary Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: actions require time and uses
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these action, concentration, and use limits; a world can relax them to make monsters more potent, at the cost of reducing opportunities to interrupt them.

rules.statement: A use marked X/Day returns after a Long Rest. A use marked Recharge X–Y can be used once, then returns at the start of a turn when a d6 roll falls in that range; it also returns after a Short or Long Rest. A use marked for a Short or Long Rest returns after either rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Limited Usage (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the printed recovery schedule; a world can shorten or lengthen recovery, balancing frequent access against the strength of the ability.

rules.statement: An aboleth’s underwater mucus can curse creatures in a 5-foot emanation at the end of its turn (DC 14 Constitution save). A failed save lets the target breathe air and water but prevents regaining Hit Points except underwater; outside water, it also takes 6 acid damage every 10 minutes unless its skin is moistened.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Aboleth — Mucus Cloud (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed area, save, and continuing costs; a world can change the curse’s persistence or damage interval, making water dependence more or less perilous.

rules.statement: An aboleth can dominate one visible creature within 30 feet (DC 16 Wisdom save) twice per day. On failure the target is charmed, controlled as an ally while within 60 feet, and can communicate telepathically with the aboleth at any distance; it repeats the save when damaged and after spending 24 hours at least 1 mile away.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Aboleth — Dominate Mind (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated distance, repeat-save triggers, and until-death-or-planar-separation duration; a world can weaken the control or remove escape saves, trading reliability for a harsher effect.

rules.statement: A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by an aboleth’s memory-consuming action yields its memories to the aboleth if it is a Humanoid. The action can target a creature within 30 feet that is charmed or grappled; a successful DC 16 Intelligence save halves its 3d6 psychic damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Aboleth — Consume Memories (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to transferring memories only on the specified lethal result; a world can allow transfer without death, at the cost of making the ability easier to exploit.

rules.statement: When destroyed, an aboleth returns with all its Hit Points in 5d10 days, in the Far Realm or another GM-chosen location. A balor killed outside the Abyss, or a devil killed outside the Nine Hells, instead returns there instantly with all its Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Aboleth — Eldritch Restoration; Balor — Death Throes; Barbed Devil — Diabolical Restoration (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed home-plane revival and delay; a world can change the delay or destination, at the cost of weakening or strengthening the consequences of killing such creatures.

rules.statement: A failed save can be turned into a success a limited number of times: ancient brass dragons do this 4 times per day (5 in their lair), while ancient bronze and copper dragons do it 4 times (5 in a lair). Adult bronze and copper dragons can do so 3 times (4 in a lair).
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ancient Brass Dragon; Adult Bronze Dragon; Ancient Bronze Dragon; Adult Copper Dragon; Ancient Copper Dragon (dnd-srd-5.2.1#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use a small daily pool of save overrides; a world can raise the pool in a lair, reflecting the creature’s home-ground advantage.

rules.statement: A breath weapon that lists Recharge 5–6 becomes usable again when the creature rolls a 5 or 6 at the start of its turn. Its area, save and effect vary by creature; successful saves often halve damage, while failures may impose conditions or movement effects.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dragon stat blocks, pp. 269–277; Chimera; Dragon Turtle (dnd-srd-5.2.1#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow a rechargeable area attack with its printed shape and save; a world can change the recharge range or area, with stronger effects costing more opportunities to act.

rules.statement: A restrained target affected by the chuul’s tentacles repeats a Constitution save at the end of each turn; success ends the effect, and after 1 minute it succeeds automatically. A cockatrice’s bite similarly escalates from restrained to petrified after two failed saves, with petrification lasting 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Chuul; Cockatrice (dnd-srd-5.2.1#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use repeated saves with a timed automatic end; a world can lengthen the buildup or duration, making the danger of remaining affected more severe.

rules.statement: A chain devil’s conjured chain can restrain one visible target within 60 feet on a failed Dexterity save, deal 9 fire damage, and pull a Large or smaller target up to 30 feet toward the devil; the chain ends at the end of the devil’s next turn. On a successful save, it vanishes without restraining the target.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Chain Devil (dnd-srd-5.2.1#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use a short-lived binding attack that can also pull its target; a world can extend its duration or reach, making escape and interruption more important.

rules.statement: The golem heals by an amount equal to acid damage directed at it instead of taking that damage. When it starts its turn Bloodied, a roll of 6 on 1d6 makes it attack the nearest creature it can see until destroyed or no longer Bloodied.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Clay Golem (dnd-srd-5.2.1#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use damage of one type as healing and a low-probability loss of control below half health; a world can alter the trigger or die size, trading resilience against predictability.

rules.statement: A creature attached to a cloaker is blinded, and the cloaker takes half damage, rounded down, while the attached creature takes that same amount. The cloaker can detach by spending 5 feet of movement, or someone adjacent can use an action and succeed on a DC 14 Strength (Athletics) check to detach it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cloaker (dnd-srd-5.2.1#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use attachment to transfer damage and impose blindness, with movement or an adjacent helper able to break it; a world can change the escape cost, shifting the burden between victim and ally.

rules.statement: A death dog’s failed Constitution save poisons its target; the target’s Hit Point maximum then fails to recover after a Long Rest. It repeats the save every 24 hours, ending the effect on a success, but later failures reduce its maximum by 5 (1d10).
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Death Dog (dnd-srd-5.2.1#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use a recurring save to end a lingering affliction, with further failures worsening it; a world can change the interval or loss, making the poison more or less urgent.

rules.statement: A djinni’s whirlwind lasts while its concentration continues and can be moved up to 20 feet at the start of each of its turns. A creature caught in it must save against restraint, takes 21 thunder damage at the start of its turns while restrained, and repeats its save at the end of each turn to escape.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Djinni (dnd-srd-5.2.1#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use a movable, concentration-bound area that restrains and damages its occupants; a world can enlarge or shrink the area, with concentration limiting how long control can be maintained.

rules.statement: A devil or celestial that dies away from its home plane re-forms there: the chain devil and deva return immediately with full Hit Points, while the djinni returns after 1d4 days. The dragon’s legendary actions provide a separate timing limit: it spends a limited pool after another creature’s turn and refreshes the pool at the start of its own turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Chain Devil; Deva; Djinni; Dragon legendary actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use home-plane revival with the stated delay and full recovery; a world can change the delay or restoration, making defeat a displacement rather than a permanent end.

rules.statement: Some creatures climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without checks; sunlight imposes disadvantage on a drider’s ability checks and attack rolls.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Drider, page 282 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to effortless climbing and a sunlight penalty; a world can change which surfaces or light sources trigger these traits to reflect creature biology.

rules.statement: A web walker ignores movement limits imposed by webs and senses the location of creatures touching the same web.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Drider, page 282 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sensing others through a shared web; a world can limit the range or precision to make webs less reliable as an information network.

rules.statement: The efreeti reforms on the Plane of Fire 1d4 days after dying elsewhere, restored to full Hit Points; the erinyes and glabrezu instead reform in their home planes immediately and at full Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Efreeti, page 283; Erinyes, page 283; Glabrezu, page 289 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to death triggering restoration at the listed home plane and delay; a world can change the return time or destination as the cost of planar dependence.

rules.statement: A ghost that possesses a Humanoid within 5 feet on a failed DC 13 Charisma save disappears into the host, incapacitates the host, and controls its body while the host remains aware. The possession ends when the body reaches 0 Hit Points or the ghost leaves as a Bonus Action; afterward the host is immune to that ghost’s possession for 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ghost, page 288 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary bodily control with the listed escape conditions and immunity; a world can turn the save, duration, or host awareness to set the danger of possession.

rules.statement: An erinyes’s magic rope can restrain a visible creature within 120 feet on a failed DC 16 Strength save; the restraint lasts until the rope is destroyed, the erinyes releases the target as a Bonus Action, or it uses the rope again. The rope has AC 20 and 90 Hit Points, and can be restored after a Short or Long Rest if damaged or destroyed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Erinyes, page 283 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a destructible, recoverable rope that restrains at range; a world can adjust its durability or recovery interval to tune how costly the restraint is.

rules.statement: A fire elemental deals 5 fire damage at the end of each of its turns to creatures in its 10-foot Emanation, and ignites creatures and flammable objects there. It also deals 5 fire damage the first time it enters a creature’s space on a turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fire Elemental, page 284 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a persistent damaging aura and contact burn; a world can turn the aura’s size or frequency to reflect how intense the elemental’s heat is.

rules.statement: A flesh golem absorbs lightning damage as healing equal to the damage dealt. When it starts its turn Bloodied, a roll of 6 on a d6 sends it berserk; it attacks the nearest visible creature, or an object if none is reachable, until destroyed or no longer Bloodied.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Flesh Golem, page 285 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting lightning damage into healing and a rare Bloodied-triggered rampage; a world can change the trigger or absorbed amount to tune the golem’s volatility.

rules.statement: A gray ooze corrodes nonmagical weapons cumulatively by −1 to attack rolls each time they damage it, destroying them at −5; its touch similarly reduces nonmagical armor’s AC by 1, destroying it when its AC reaches 10. Mending removes either penalty, and the ooze can eat through 2-inch-thick nonmagical metal or wood in 1 round.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Gray Ooze, page 293 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to accumulating corrosion with repair or destruction thresholds; a world can adjust the rate or materials affected to set the ooze’s environmental cost.

rules.statement: Some creatures return after death: the guardian naga revives in 1d6 days unless a specified dispelling spell is used on its remains; certain fiends return instantly in their home plane, while a lich needs its spirit jar and reforms in 1d10 days in its lair.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to restoring the creature with all Hit Points after its listed delay or at its listed destination; a world can make return conditional on destroying an anchor or using a countermeasure.

rules.statement: The hydra loses one head when it takes at least 25 damage in a turn, but at the end of its turn regrows two heads per head lost since its previous turn and regains 20 Hit Points, unless it took fire damage in that interval; it dies when all heads are dead.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 300, Hydra traits (dnd-srd-5.2.1#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to regrowing heads and restoring 20 Hit Points unless fire interrupts the cycle; a world can vary the damage threshold or recovery amount to tune how costly it is to stop regeneration.

rules.statement: A harpy’s song can charm Humanoids and Giants within 300 feet, incapacitating them and drawing them toward the singer; affected targets save again at turn’s end, after taking outside damage, or before entering hazardous terrain, and success grants 24-hour immunity to that harpy’s song.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 297, Harpy actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to attraction and incapacitation until a successful repeat save; a world can alter the eligible targets or break conditions, with stronger control carrying a greater exposure cost.

rules.statement: A creature swallowed by the kraken is restrained, protected from outside attacks by total cover, and takes 7d6 acid damage at the start of each of its turns; if the kraken dies it can escape using 15 feet of movement, while sufficient internal damage can force the kraken to regurgitate its victims.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 303, Kraken actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to containment with ongoing damage and an escape route on the captor’s death; a world can change capacity or escape requirements, trading secure capture for greater danger to captives.

rules.statement: An incubus’s touch curses a target for 24 hours or until the incubus dies, preventing benefits from Short Rests; its Nightmare knocks a target with 20 Hit Points or fewer unconscious, subject to listed waking and damage conditions.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 301, Incubus actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated curse duration and rest restriction, and to sleep only below the 20-Hit-Point threshold; a world can shorten the curse or change the threshold to adjust how debilitating the effect is.

rules.statement: A homunculus and its master can communicate telepathically while on the same plane; its bite can poison a target, and failure by 5 or more makes the poison last 1 minute and renders the target unconscious until it takes damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 299, Homunculus (dnd-srd-5.2.1#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one master-linked telepathic companion and the listed poison outcomes; a world can extend the bond across planes or limit communication, with distance and vulnerability as the cost.

rules.statement: The archmage’s Mind Blank spell makes it immune to the Charmed condition, and the mage and archmage can use a limited number of reactions to cast Counterspell or Shield in response to their triggers.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 305, Mages (dnd-srd-5.2.1#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to blocking charm for the duration of Mind Blank and allowing three protective reactions per day for these stat blocks; a world can raise or lower reaction capacity to trade defensive coverage against other actions.

rules.statement: The marilith can teleport up to 120 feet to a visible unoccupied space when its teleport is available; a devil or demon listed with restoration returns with all Hit Points in its home plane if killed elsewhere.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 298, 300, 306, Restoration traits and Marilith actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated teleport distance and home-plane return; a world can restrict destinations or make return conditional, balancing mobility and persistence against access to the home plane.

rules.statement: A death-triggered burst affects creatures within a 5-foot emanation; a Dexterity save halves the listed damage. The mephit examples deal 7 (2d6) fire at DC 11 or 5 (2d4) fire at DC 10.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Traits, pages 307–308 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Resolve the burst when the creature dies; a world can vary the radius or damage, with the blast threatening nearby creatures.

rules.statement: Some breath attacks affect creatures in a cone and allow a Dexterity save for half damage; the listed recharge range is 5–6 or 6, depending on the creature. Steam Breath also reduces a failed target’s Speed by 10 feet until the mephit’s next turn ends.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Actions, pages 307–308 and 318–319 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated cone, save, damage, and recharge; a world can tune the cone or recharge, balancing area damage against limited use.

rules.statement: A hit can impose a condition or movement restriction for a stated duration, and some effects allow a save to avoid or end it. For example, the merfolk spear reduces Speed by 10 feet until the end of the attacker’s next turn, while a mummy’s failed glare save frightens its target until then.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Actions, pages 308–310 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply the listed condition and duration after a failed save or hit; a world can adjust duration or resistance, trading control for reliability.

rules.statement: The mummy’s curse prevents healing and reduces the target’s Hit Point maximum by 10 (3d6) every 24 hours; a creature killed by the attack turns to dust. The mummy lord’s version also denies the benefit of a Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rotting Fist, pages 309–310 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Track the curse and its daily maximum loss until its removal or the target’s death; a world can alter the rate, with lasting harm as the cost.

rules.statement: A mummy lord destroyed with its heart intact forms a new body after 24 hours, at full Hit Points, in an unoccupied space in its lair. Its Tiny heart has AC 17 and 10 Hit Points and is immune to damage except fire.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Undead Restoration, page 310 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Revive it after 24 hours if the heart survives; a world can change the anchor’s vulnerability or delay, making the heart the price of permanence.

rules.statement: A hag’s soul bag can hold souls and is required for her once-per-day Nightmare Haunting; destroying the bag releases its stored souls, and she can make another after 7 days. A soul killed by the haunting cannot be raised until released.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Soul Bag and Nightmare Haunting, page 311 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Make the bag a required, destructible soul anchor; a world can change its durability or replacement delay, limiting the hag’s power and trapping souls.

rules.statement: A creature grappled by the purple worm or remorhaz can be swallowed on a failed Strength save. Inside, it is blinded and restrained, is protected from outside effects, and takes acid damage each turn; enough damage from inside may force the creature to regurgitate its victims.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Swallow, pages 317 and 319–320 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated size, capacity, save, and escape conditions; a world can change internal damage or regurgitation thresholds, making capture dangerous but escapable.

rules.statement: Some creatures return to life through a body tied to a specific plane: the nalfeshnee and certain fiends regain a full-health body immediately on their home plane if killed elsewhere. Other restorations require an intact heart and 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Restoration traits, pages 310–311 and 315 and 318 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Return the creature in its linked plane or at its lair, under the stated conditions; a world can make the anchor destructible or the return slower.

rules.statement: A roper’s tentacle can reach 60 feet and, on a hit, grapples a target and poisons it until the grapple ends. The target can escape at DC 14; destroying that tentacle (AC 20, 10 HP) frees it without harming the roper, and the tentacle regrows at the start of the roper’s next turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Roper — Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a separate, destructible restraint with a fixed escape DC; a world can change tentacle durability or recovery time to make escape easier or harder.

rules.statement: A rust monster can damage a worn or carried nonmagical metal weapon or armor on a failed DC 11 Dexterity save. Repeated penalties destroy armor when its offered AC reaches 10 or a weapon when its attack penalty reaches −5; Mending removes the penalty. Its touch also destroys a one-foot cube of unattended nonmagical metal.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rust Monster — Actions [Page 321] (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cumulative, repairable damage to mundane metal; a world can vary which materials resist the effect or how readily repair magic restores them.

rules.statement: A sahuagin can magically control sharks within 120 feet through telepathy. It can breathe air and water, but must submerge at least once every four hours or risk suffocation outside water.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sahuagin Warrior — Traits (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to short-range control of sharks and a four-hour amphibious limit; a world can turn the range, creature type, or submersion interval to change the power’s reach and cost.

rules.statement: A salamander damages creatures of its choice within 5 feet for 2d6 fire damage at the end of each of its turns. Its spear returns to its hand immediately after a ranged attack, whether or not the attack hits.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Salamander — Traits and Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a selective, close-range damage field and a magically returning weapon; a world can vary the field’s radius, damage, or whether the weapon returns.

rules.statement: A shadow’s hit reduces a target’s Strength by 1d4; a target reduced to Strength 0 dies. If a humanoid dies this way, a new shadow rises from its corpse 1d4 hours later.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Shadow — Actions [Page 323] (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to strength loss that can kill and a delayed undead consequence; a world can change the reduction, recovery, or creation delay to tune the danger and aftermath.

rules.statement: A shield guardian is magically linked to an amulet: its wearer can call it across the same plane and knows it can locate the amulet. Within 60 feet, the guardian takes half the wearer’s damage, rounded up; it also regenerates 10 HP each turn while above 0 HP.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Shield Guardian — Traits [Page 323] (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a same-plane amulet bond with nearby damage sharing and steady regeneration; a world can alter the bond’s range, damage share, or healing rate.

rules.statement: Silver dragon paralyzing breath first incapacitates a creature that fails its save; at the end of its next turn it saves again, becoming paralyzed on a second failure. While paralyzed, it repeats the save at each turn’s end and ends the effect on a success; after 1 minute it succeeds automatically.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Silver Dragons — Paralyzing Breath [Pages 324–325] (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an escalating failed-save effect with repeated chances to recover and a one-minute limit; a world can change the number or timing of recovery saves.

rules.statement: The tarrasque can swallow a creature it has grappled on a failed DC 27 Strength save, up to six creatures at once. A swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, cannot teleport, and takes 16d6 acid damage at the start of each of the tarrasque’s turns; sufficient damage from inside can force the tarrasque to regurgitate its swallowed victims.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Tarrasque — Bonus Actions [Page 332] (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a limited-capacity internal prison that causes recurring harm and can be escaped by damaging the captor; a world can change capacity, damage, or the escape threshold.

rules.statement: A treant can animate up to two visible trees within 60 feet once per day. They use its statistics except Intelligence and Charisma are 1, they cannot speak or animate other trees, act immediately after it, and obey it; animation ends after 1 day, when either treant dies, or when a tree is more than 120 feet away, after which it roots if possible.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 333 — Treant, Animate Trees (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to two subordinate tree-creatures for at most one day; a world could alter their number or tether distance, with the treant’s limited daily use constraining this command.

rules.statement: A troll that ends a turn Bloodied after taking at least 15 Slashing damage that turn can lose a limb, up to four times per day. The limb becomes a separate creature; each missing limb gives the troll one Exhaustion level, and replacement limbs grow when it next regains Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 333 — Troll, Loathsome Limbs (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to severed limbs becoming independent creatures under the stated damage and health conditions; a world could change the threshold or daily cap, trading bodily injury and Exhaustion for extra creatures.

rules.statement: Trolls and troll limbs regain 15 and 5 Hit Points, respectively, at the start of their turns. Acid or Fire damage disables that regeneration for the following turn; either dies only if it starts a turn at 0 Hit Points without regenerating.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 333 — Troll and Troll Limb, Regeneration (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to recurring healing that can be interrupted for one turn by Acid or Fire; a world could vary the recovery amount or disabling damage, making those damage types strategically valuable.

rules.statement: A vampire outside its resting place that reaches 0 Hit Points becomes mist without spending an action, unless it cannot shape-shift, in which case it is destroyed. At 0 Hit Points in mist form, it must reach its resting place within 2 hours or be destroyed; there it returns to vampire form, remains Paralyzed until it regains Hit Points, and regains 1 Hit Point after 1 hour.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 335–336 — Vampire, Misty Escape (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a timed retreat-and-recovery route rather than immediate death; a world could change the deadline or recovery time, with the resting place serving as the costly safe haven.

rules.statement: A vampire’s bite reduces a target’s Hit Point maximum by the Necrotic damage dealt and restores the same amount of Hit Points to the vampire. A Humanoid reduced to 0 Hit Points by this bite and then buried rises at the following sunset as a Vampire Spawn under the vampire’s control.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 336 — Vampire, Bite (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to transferring vitality from victim to vampire, with a buried Humanoid’s death creating a controlled spawn; a world could change the conversion or delay, making victim loss the price of the vampire’s gain.

rules.statement: A vampire can change into a Tiny bat or a Medium mist cloud, or back to vampire form, only when it is not in sunlight or running water; its worn items change with it. In mist form it cannot act, speak, or handle objects, but has resistance to all damage except sunlight damage and can pass through any space air can pass through, but not liquid.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 336 — Vampire, Shape-Shift (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to three forms with distinct movement and interaction limits; a world could change the available forms or environmental restriction, balancing infiltration and resilience against lost agency in mist.

rules.statement: A Lycanthrope’s bite or gore can curse a Humanoid that fails a Constitution save; if the cursed target reaches 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes that attacker’s kind under the GM’s control with 10 Hit Points. A successful save grants immunity to that specific lycanthrope’s curse for 24 hours; the save DC is 14 for werebear, 12 for wereboar, 11 for wererat, 13 for weretiger, and 12 for werewolf.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 337–339 — Werebear through Werewolf, Bite or Gore (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a kind-specific curse that converts a Humanoid at the brink of death into a controlled creature; a world could vary save difficulty or conversion conditions, with the risk of transformation as the cost.

rules.statement: A wight’s Life Drain reduces a creature’s Hit Point maximum by the damage dealt. A Humanoid killed by it rises 24 hours later as a Zombie under the wight’s control unless restored to life or its body is destroyed; a wight can control at most twelve zombies this way.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 341 — Wight, Life Drain (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to vitality loss followed by delayed controlled reanimation, capped at twelve servants; a world could adjust the delay or cap, while body destruction or restoration prevents the consequence.

rules.statement: A wisp can turn itself and its light Invisible while concentrating; the effect ends early immediately after it attacks or consumes a life. It can also kill a living creature it can see within 5 feet if that creature has 0 Hit Points and fails a DC 10 Constitution save, restoring 10 Hit Points to the wisp.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 342 — Will-o’-Wisp, Vanish and Consume Life (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concentration-based invisibility that breaks on specified actions, plus a close-range execution that heals the wisp; a world could change the ending triggers or healing, with opportunity and risk limiting the benefits.

rules.statement: Some creatures gain Advantage on attack rolls against a target when an ally is within 5 feet of that target and is not Incapacitated. A few instead gain Advantage while Bloodied, or when attacking a target that is missing any Hit Points.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these specific ally-or-injury triggers for attack bonuses; a world can widen or narrow the trigger, with stronger teamwork or injury making attacks more reliable.

rules.statement: Several charging attacks add damage or knock a target Prone if the attacker moved at least 20 feet straight toward it immediately before the hit; the target’s maximum size varies by creature. Some attacks also grapple or knock Prone without a charge.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a straight 20-foot approach and the listed size limit; a world can relax either condition, trading stricter positioning for more frequent knockdowns.

rules.statement: Certain attacks impose Grappled or Restrained, with escape DCs stated for particular creatures. Some creatures can swallow a creature they have grappled, imposing Blinded and Restrained and, in some cases, dealing acid damage at the end of their turns; death of the swallower or other stated conditions allow escape.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed size limits, escape DCs, and release conditions; a world can make capture harder to escape, at the cost of greater danger to swallowed targets.

rules.statement: An underwater octopus can release an ink cloud that heavily obscures an area for 1 minute, or until a strong current or similar effect disperses it, and then move up to its Swim Speed. The reaction is limited to once per day and has a creature-specific trigger and area.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a temporary, localized obscuring cloud with a dispersal condition and once-per-day use; a world can enlarge or prolong it, making escape easier but concealment more potent.

rules.statement: Some creatures can breathe both air and water, while others can breathe only underwater or hold their breath for a stated duration, such as 1 hour, 30 minutes, or 10 minutes. These limits govern how long they can function in the other environment.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to each creature’s stated breathing mode and duration; a world can change these limits, trading environmental flexibility against aquatic specialization.

rules.statement: Some creatures can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check; a spider also ignores movement restrictions caused by webs and senses the location of creatures touching the same web. Other listed movement exceptions include narrow-space passage, long jumps, and avoiding opportunity attacks while moving or flying away.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the specific movement exceptions stated for each creature; a world can broaden them, granting greater mobility while reducing the value of terrain as an obstacle.

rules.statement: A few creatures can restrain a target with a web or grapple it with attacks; one web can be destroyed and has AC 10, 5 Hit Points, Fire Vulnerability, and immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. A giant scorpion can grapple with one claw while making its other listed attacks.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the printed escape or destruction requirements and the web’s stated defenses; a world can make restraints more durable, at the cost of making trapped targets harder to free.

rules.statement: A giant ape’s boulder attack recharges on a 6 and affects creatures in a 5-foot-radius area at a point it can see within 90 feet; a failed Dexterity save takes full damage and can cause Prone, while a success halves damage. The listed elephant and mammoth tramples target a nearby Prone creature, with a Dexterity save for half damage.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated recharge, range, area, target state, and save outcomes; a world can increase reach or area, making these attacks more powerful but less constrained.

rules.statement: A swarm can share a creature’s space and pass through openings large enough for one of its Tiny members. It cannot regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Swarm of Bats, p. 361 (Swarm trait) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing shared-space movement through member-sized gaps but no healing; a world could relax either limit to make swarms more resilient or able to infiltrate tighter spaces.

rules.statement: A swarm’s listed damage is reduced when it is Bloodied: the reduction varies by swarm, and some swarms have no listed reduction. The piranha swarm instead has Advantage against a target missing any Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Swarm of Bats, p. 361; Swarm of Piranhas, p. 362 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the damage and bloodied values in each creature’s entry; a world could make injury affect swarm output more sharply, reflecting loss of members.

rules.statement: A creature has Advantage on an attack against a target when one of its allies is within 5 feet of that target and the ally is not Incapacitated.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Reef Shark, p. 360 (Pack Tactics trait) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a nearby, active ally; a world could broaden or narrow the required teamwork, changing how readily packs gain an edge.

rules.statement: A rhinoceros, triceratops, or warhorse that moves at least 20 feet straight toward a qualifying target immediately before hitting it deals extra damage and knocks the target Prone. The rhinoceros and warhorse limit the target to Large or smaller; the triceratops allows Huge or smaller.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rhinoceros, p. 360; Triceratops, p. 363; Warhorse, p. 364 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring the stated straight-line run-up and size limit; a world could alter the distance or size threshold, with greater reach making charges easier to land.

rules.statement: A tiger’s Rend knocks a Large or smaller target Prone. A tyrannosaurus’s Bite Grapples a Large or smaller target (escape DC 17), Restrains it while held, and prevents the tyrannosaurus from targeting it with its Tail; its Tail knocks a Huge or smaller target Prone.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Tiger, p. 363; Tyrannosaurus Rex, p. 363 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed size limits and grapple escape difficulty; a world could change which targets these attacks can disable, balancing control against creature size.

rules.statement: A rule that explicitly conflicts with a general rule takes precedence over that general rule; when division or multiplication produces a fraction, round down unless a rule specifically directs rounding up.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Playing the Game, page 5 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: apply the general rule; dial: none; the specific effect controls when it states an exception.

rules.statement: A D20 Test succeeds when a d20 roll plus its applicable ability modifier, relevant proficiency bonus, and situational modifiers equals or exceeds its target number; advantage or disadvantage instead uses the higher or lower of two d20s. Multiple instances of either do not add more dice, and having both cancels them.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: D20 Tests; Advantage/Disadvantage, pages 6–8 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: one d20 and applicable modifiers; dial: advantage or disadvantage changes the selected roll, reflecting favorable or adverse circumstances.

rules.statement: A creature can use a saving throw to resist a threat, with the effect setting the result and usually the DC; it may choose to fail without rolling. Proficiency in the relevant save adds the creature’s proficiency bonus.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Saving Throws, page 7 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: roll to resist; dial: voluntary failure permits accepting the effect, at the creature’s choice.

rules.statement: A creature’s base Armor Class is 10 plus its Dexterity modifier, and armor, magic, spells, or other rules can modify it. If multiple features offer different base calculations, only one can be used at a time.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Armor Class, page 7 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: use the standard base calculation; dial: a creature with alternatives chooses one, limiting simultaneous defenses.

rules.statement: A creature with Heroic Inspiration can spend it immediately after rolling any die to roll that die again, and must use the new result; it can hold only one such inspiration at a time. If it would gain another while already holding one, it can give the new one to a player character who lacks it; human characters begin each day with one.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Heroic Inspiration, page 8 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: no reroll unless inspiration is held; dial: one stored use limits repeated correction, and using it commits the new result.

rules.statement: A creature adds its proficiency bonus to a test only when proficient in the relevant skill, save, weapon, or tool; the bonus cannot be added more than once to a roll. A tool check also gains advantage if the creature has proficiency in the skill used for that same check.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Proficiency, pages 8–9 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: untrained attempts receive no proficiency bonus; dial: relevant training improves the result, but duplicate training does not stack.

rules.statement: A creature can take only one action at a time; it takes a bonus action only when a specific feature, spell, or rule permits one, and can take at most one bonus action on its turn. A reaction happens immediately after its trigger unless its rule says otherwise, and cannot be taken again until the start of the creature’s next turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Actions; Bonus Actions; Reactions, pages 9–10 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: one action, one available bonus action, and one reaction per interval; dial: special abilities grant extra options within these limits.

rules.statement: Dim light, patchy fog, or moderate foliage lightly obscures an area and gives disadvantage on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks; darkness, heavy fog, or dense foliage heavily obscures it, making it opaque and imposing the Blinded condition for attempts to see within it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Vision and Light, page 11 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: visibility follows the area’s illumination and obstruction; dial: obscuration reduces sight or prevents it, with the environment imposing the cost.

rules.statement: Outside combat, a traveling group chooses a fast, normal, or slow pace, covering respectively 400 feet, 4 miles, or 30 miles per minute, hour, or day; 300 feet, 3 miles, or 24 miles; or 200 feet, 2 miles, or 18 miles. Fast pace gives disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception or Survival) and Dexterity (Stealth) checks, normal pace gives disadvantage on Stealth, and slow pace gives advantage on Perception or Survival; mounts can double distance for 1 hour before needing a Short or Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Travel, page 12 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: normal pace; dial: faster travel sacrifices awareness and concealment, while slower travel improves noticing and tracking.

rules.statement: Combat proceeds in rounds of about 6 seconds, with each participant rolling Initiative using a Dexterity check to determine turn order; a surprised participant has disadvantage on that roll. On a turn, a participant can move up to its Speed and take one action, with one free interaction with an object or environmental feature during its movement or action.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Combat; The Order of Combat; Your Turn, pages 13–14 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default: one move and one action per turn; dial: surprise worsens initiative, and additional object interaction requires an action.

rules.statement: Each foot moved through difficult ground costs one additional foot of movement, regardless of how many difficult-terrain causes occupy that space.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Difficult Terrain (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charge the extra movement; dial: terrain severity; the in-world cause is obstructed footing.

rules.statement: On your turn, you may become Prone without spending an action or movement, unless your Speed is 0.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dropping Prone (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow voluntary prone posture; dial: disable it at zero Speed; the in-world reason is that the creature cannot move.

rules.statement: A creature may pass through an ally’s space, an incapacitated creature’s space, a Tiny creature’s space, or a creature at least two size categories larger or smaller; another creature’s space costs extra movement unless the creature is Tiny or an ally. You cannot willingly finish movement in another creature’s space; ending a turn there makes you Prone unless you are Tiny or larger than that creature.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Moving around Other Creatures (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the passage and occupancy limits; dial: size and ally exceptions; the in-world reason is creatures contesting physical space.

rules.statement: An attack selects a creature, object, or location in range; the GM determines cover and advantage or disadvantage, then the attacker rolls, dealing damage on a hit unless the attack specifies otherwise. An attack can also produce other effects instead of, or in addition to, damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Making an Attack (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve targeting, modifiers, and hit effects in sequence; dial: applicable bonuses and penalties; the in-world reason is the attack’s circumstances and outcome.

rules.statement: Half cover grants +2 to AC and Dexterity saves, and three-quarters cover grants +5 to both; total cover prevents direct targeting. Only the highest cover degree applies, and cover benefits a target only when the attack or effect comes from the opposite side.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cover (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the strongest applicable cover only; dial: cover degree; the in-world reason is obstacles physically shielding the target.

rules.statement: A ranged attack with one listed range cannot target beyond it; with normal and long ranges, attacks beyond normal range have disadvantage and attacks beyond long range are prohibited. A ranged attack roll has disadvantage if an able-to-see enemy within 5 feet threatens the attacker.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ranged Attacks (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enforce range and nearby-threat penalties; dial: the weapon or effect’s listed ranges; the in-world reason is distance and pressure disrupting aim.

rules.statement: A creature can make a melee attack against a target within its reach, ordinarily 5 feet unless its description gives a greater reach. When a visible creature leaves your reach, you may spend a Reaction to make one melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike immediately before it leaves; Disengage, teleportation, and movement imposed without your movement, action, Bonus Action, or Reaction do not provoke this attack.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Melee Attacks; Opportunity Attacks (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit one reaction attack on departure; dial: reach and listed exceptions; the in-world reason is an opening created by careless movement.

rules.statement: Mounting or dismounting a willing, suitably built creature at least one size larger costs movement equal to half your Speed, rounded down. A trained controlled mount takes your Initiative, follows your direction, and can Dash, Disengage, or Dodge; an independent mount keeps its own Initiative and acts as it chooses.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mounted Combat (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the movement cost and controlled-mount action limits; dial: training and willingness; the in-world reason is the mount’s cooperation and physical fit.

rules.statement: If an effect is about to move your mount against its will, or you or the mount becomes Prone while mounted, you must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity save or fall Prone into an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the mount.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Falling Off (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require the save in the stated circumstances; dial: DC 10; the in-world reason is losing balance on a disrupted mount.

rules.statement: Underwater, a creature without a Swim Speed has disadvantage on melee weapon attacks unless the weapon deals piercing damage. A ranged weapon attack automatically misses beyond normal range and has disadvantage within normal range; anything underwater has Resistance to Fire damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Underwater Combat (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply underwater attack penalties and fire resistance; dial: Swim Speed and damage type; the in-world reason is water impeding weapons and fire.

rules.statement: When damage would reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points with a melee attack, the attacker may instead leave it at 1 Hit Point and give it Unconscious; it begins a Short Rest. The condition ends when it regains Hit Points, someone administers first aid with an action and a successful DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check, or the Short Rest ends.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Knocking Out a Creature (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow nonlethal incapacitation by melee attack; dial: first-aid check DC 10; the in-world reason is deliberately stopping short of a killing blow.

rules.statement: Damage reduces current Hit Points, but does not impair capabilities until they reach 0; at half or fewer Hit Points, a creature is Bloodied, with no effect by itself. Healing adds Hit Points up to the maximum, losing any excess, while Temporary Hit Points are lost before actual Hit Points, do not stack, and last until depleted or a Long Rest; they cannot restore consciousness at 0 Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Damage and Healing; Hit Points; Temporary Hit Points (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: track current, maximum, and temporary Hit Points separately; dial: healing or temporary-point amount; the in-world reason is finite bodily endurance and a temporary damage buffer.

rules.statement: A character who reaches 0 Hit Points and does not die instantly becomes Unconscious and makes a Death Saving Throw at the start of each turn: 10 or higher is a success, lower is a failure, and three successes stabilize while three failures kill. A natural 1 counts as two failures, a natural 20 restores 1 Hit Point, and damage at 0 causes a failure (two for a Critical Hit); damage at least equal to the Hit Point maximum kills.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dropping to 0 Hit Points; Death Saving Throws (dnd-srd-5.2.1#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: track successes and failures until three of either; dial: stabilization or healing resets the count; the in-world reason is the uncertain struggle between life and death.

rules.statement: When determining multiclass spell slots, add all levels in Spellcasting classes and half the Ranger levels; higher-level slots can cast only prepared lower-level spells, though they can improve a spell that scales when cast at a higher level. Pact Magic slots can cast spells prepared through Spellcasting, and Spellcasting slots can cast prepared Warlock spells.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Multiclass Spellcaster / Pact Magic, p. 26 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: slot access follows combined class progression; dial: spell preparation restricts what those slots can cast.

rules.statement: A character can roll once on the Trinkets table during character creation to gain a Tiny, mysterious simple item; the GM can also roll on it to stock a dungeon room or a creature’s pockets. The table uses 1d100 to select an entry.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Trinkets, pp. 26–27 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one randomly selected trinket; dial: none, and the item’s mystery is left to the GM.

rules.statement: A Barbarian can enter Rage as a Bonus Action if not wearing Heavy armor, a number of times shown for their level; they recover one use on a Short Rest and all uses on a Long Rest. While raging, they resist Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, gain listed bonus damage on Strength-based weapon or Unarmed Strike hits, and have Advantage on Strength checks and saves, but cannot concentrate or cast spells.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Barbarian: Rage, pp. 28–29 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: Rage grants offensive and defensive power; dial: use limits and spell/concentration lockout constrain it.

rules.statement: Rage lasts until the end of the Barbarian’s next turn and can be extended each round by attacking an enemy, forcing an enemy to save, or spending a Bonus Action; each extension lasts to the next turn, and the total duration is at most 10 minutes. Rage ends early if the Barbarian dons Heavy armor or becomes Incapacitated.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Barbarian: Rage, p. 29 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ongoing combat activity or an action sustains the state; dial: the 10-minute cap and ending conditions limit duration.

rules.statement: While unarmored, a Barbarian’s base Armor Class is 10 plus Dexterity and Constitution modifiers; a Shield is allowed. Weapon mastery applies to two chosen kinds of Simple or Martial Melee weapons, and after each Long Rest one choice can be changed; the number of usable weapon kinds increases with Barbarian level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Barbarian: Unarmored Defense and Weapon Mastery, p. 29 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: training sets defense and weapon options; dial: armor restriction and limited, rest-based choice changes.

rules.statement: When using Reckless Attack, a Barbarian can forgo Advantage on one eligible Strength-based attack roll that has no Disadvantage; on a hit, it deals an extra 1d10 damage and can push the target 15 feet, then move the Barbarian up to half Speed toward it without provoking Opportunity Attacks, or reduce its Speed by 15 feet until the Barbarian’s next turn. At level 13, additional options impose Disadvantage on the target’s next save and prevent its Opportunity Attacks, or grant the next attack by another creature against it +5; at level 17, the extra damage becomes 2d10 and two distinct effects can be applied.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Barbarian: Brutal Strike, pp. 29–30 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: trading the attack’s Advantage for a hit-triggered rider; dial: requires Reckless Attack, a qualifying hit, and level-based options.

rules.statement: When a raging Barbarian who has not died outright drops to 0 Hit Points, they can make a DC 10 Constitution save; success changes their Hit Points to twice their Barbarian level. Each later use raises the DC by 5, resetting to 10 after a Short or Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Barbarian: Relentless Rage, p. 30 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a successful save prevents the fall to 0 Hit Points; dial: escalating difficulty and the Rage and rest requirements limit repeated use.

rules.statement: A Berserker’s Reckless Attack while raging deals extra damage to the first target hit that turn, rolling d6s equal to the Rage Damage bonus. While raging, the Berserker is immune to Charmed and Frightened; either condition already affecting them ends when Rage begins.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Path of the Berserker: Frenzy and Mindless Rage, p. 30 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: Rage increases the first-hit damage and blocks two mental conditions; dial: both benefits depend on Rage being active.

rules.statement: A Bard can grant a visible or audible creature within 60 feet a Bardic Inspiration die as a Bonus Action; the target can add it to a failed D20 Test within the next hour, then the die is expended. The Bard has uses equal to their Charisma modifier (minimum one), regains all on a Long Rest, and the die improves from d6 to d8, d10, and d12 at levels 5, 10, and 15.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Bard: Bardic Inspiration, pp. 31–32 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a limited die is lent to another creature to improve a test; dial: range, visibility or hearing, one-hour duration, and finite uses bound it.

rules.statement: A Bard’s level 1+ spell slots return on a Long Rest, and their prepared Bard spells must be of levels for which they have slots; the prepared-spell count follows the class table. On gaining a Bard level, the Bard can replace one prepared spell, and can replace one cantrip; Charisma governs Bard spellcasting and a Musical Instrument can serve as its focus.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Bard: Spellcasting, p. 32 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell access is learned and prepared from the Bard list; dial: slots, known options, and level eligibility limit casting.

rules.statement: A Bard can use a Reaction when they or a creature within 30 feet fails a save against an effect that applies Charmed or Frightened, causing that save to be rerolled with Advantage. At level 10, when the Bard gains new prepared spells, those spells can come from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, or Wizard lists, and replacements can use those lists too.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Bard: Countercharm and Magical Secrets, p. 33 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a reaction improves a qualifying save and later training broadens spell access; dial: range, trigger, and level-based access restrict the options.

rules.statement: A Cleric can use Channel Divinity twice, regaining one use after a Short Rest and all uses after a Long Rest; its save DC is the Cleric spell save DC. Divine Spark uses a Magic action and a visible creature within 30 feet: roll 1d8 plus Wisdom modifier to restore that many Hit Points or make the creature save against that much Necrotic or Radiant damage, taking half on success; the roll gains dice at Cleric levels 7, 13, and 18.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cleric: Channel Divinity—Divine Spark, p. 37 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a limited divine reserve can heal or damage; dial: action, range, uses, and the target’s save constrain its effect.

rules.statement: As a Magic action, a Cleric can present a Holy Symbol to make chosen Undead within 30 feet save against the Cleric’s spell save DC; on failure, they become Frightened and Incapacitated for 1 minute and try to move as far away as possible on their turns. The effect ends early on a target if it takes damage, the Cleric becomes Incapacitated, or the Cleric dies.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cleric: Channel Divinity—Turn Undead, p. 37 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed saves impose a temporary forced retreat; dial: target type, range, save, duration, and interruption conditions limit it.

rules.statement: A Druid starts knowing two Druid cantrips and preparing four level 1 Druid spells; the prepared-spell limit rises with Druid level, and the Druid can replace the list after each Long Rest. Spell slots return after a Long Rest, and the Druid uses Wisdom for spellcasting.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Druid, Level 1: Spellcasting (p. 42) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated preparation and recovery schedule; dial: the GM may set access to eligible spells; the cost is spell slots and preparation limits.

rules.statement: A Druid can spend a Bonus Action to take a learned Beast form for up to half their Druid level in hours, or until they use the feature again, become Incapacitated, or die; they can also end the form with a Bonus Action. The form grants temporary Hit Points equal to Druid level, replaces most statistics with the Beast’s, and prevents spellcasting until the Druid reaches level 18, when some spells become usable in Beast form.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Druid, Level 2: Wild Shape and Rules While Shape-Shifted (pp. 42–43); Level 18: Beast Spells (p. 43) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use learned eligible Beast forms and the listed duration; dial: the GM can limit forms from other sources; the cost is a use of Wild Shape.

rules.statement: A Druid can use a Magic action and expend a spell slot or Wild Shape use to cast Find Familiar without Material components; the familiar is Fey and disappears when the Druid finishes a Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Druid, Level 2: Wild Companion (p. 43) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the summoned helper lasts only until the next Long Rest; dial: choose between spending a slot or a Wild Shape use; the cost is one of those resources.
