rules.statement: Once on each of the Druid’s turns, if they have no Wild Shape uses remaining, they can expend a spell slot without an action to regain one use. They can also expend one Wild Shape use without an action to gain a level 1 spell slot, but cannot do that again until a Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Druid, Level 5: Wild Resurgence (p. 43) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit the stated exchange in either direction; dial: limit the slot-to-use conversion to once each turn and the reverse to once per Long Rest; the cost is the resource spent.

rules.statement: A Circle of the Land Druid chooses arid, polar, temperate, or tropical land after each Long Rest and has that land’s listed spells, up to their Druid level, prepared. At level 10, the Druid is immune to Poisoned and gains Resistance to the damage type associated with the chosen land.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Circle of the Land, Level 3: Circle of the Land Spells; Level 10: Nature’s Ward (pp. 46–47) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: land choice and its spell and resistance effects persist until the next Long Rest; dial: the player chooses among four land types; the tradeoff is being tied to one type at a time.

rules.statement: A Monk has Focus Points equal to Monk level, regains all expended points after a Short or Long Rest, and uses a saving throw DC of 8 plus Wisdom modifier and Proficiency Bonus for features that require a save. Spending 1 point can enable two unarmed strikes as a Bonus Action, combine Disengage with Dodge as a Bonus Action, or combine Disengage with Dash and double jump distance for the turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Monk, Level 2: Monk’s Focus (pp. 50–51) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated point pool and rest recovery; dial: choose which focused maneuver to fuel; the cost is a Focus Point for the enhanced options.

rules.statement: At the end of each of their turns, a level 10 Monk can remove Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned from themself. They also avoid gaining Exhaustion from going without food or drink.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Monk, Level 10: Self-Restoration (p. 52) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow removal of one listed condition at each turn’s end; dial: none stated; the in-world limit is restricted to those three conditions.

rules.statement: A Monk can spend 3 Focus Points at the start of their turn to gain Resistance to all damage except Force for 1 minute, ending early if they become Incapacitated.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Monk, Level 18: Superior Defense (p. 52) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the one-minute duration and stated early ending; dial: none stated; the cost is three Focus Points.

rules.statement: A Monk who hits a creature with an Unarmed Strike can spend 4 Focus Points to establish hidden vibrations that last a number of days equal to Monk level, with only one creature affected at a time. Ending them requires the Monk and target to be on the same plane; the target then makes a Constitution save, taking 10d12 Force damage on a failure or half on a success, and the Monk can end them harmlessly without an action.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Warrior of the Open Hand, Level 17: Quivering Palm (p. 52) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated duration, save, and damage; dial: the Monk may end the effect harmlessly; the cost is four Focus Points and a one-target limit.

rules.statement: A level 3 Life Domain Cleric’s spell-slot spell that restores Hit Points gives its targets additional healing on the casting turn equal to 2 plus the slot’s level. At level 6, when such a spell heals others, the Cleric also regains 2 plus the slot’s level in Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Life Domain, Level 3: Disciple of Life; Level 6: Blessed Healer (p. 40) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the extra healing when the specified spell-slot healing occurs; dial: none stated; the amount is bounded by the spell slot’s level.

rules.statement: A level 3 Life Domain Cleric can use a Magic action and expend Channel Divinity to distribute healing equal to five times Cleric level among chosen Bloodied creatures within 30 feet, including themself. No recipient can be raised above half its Hit Point maximum by this feature.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Life Domain, Level 3: Preserve Life (p. 40) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated radius and total healing pool; dial: choose recipients and allocation; the cost is a Channel Divinity use and each recipient has a half-maximum ceiling.

rules.statement: A Paladin can use a Bonus Action to spend from a healing pool and restore up to that many Hit Points to a touched creature. Spending 5 pool points instead removes the Poisoned condition without also restoring Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Paladin Features, p. 54; Lay On Hands (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited healing reserve; dial: pool size and recovery; the Paladin spends the same resource on healing or condition removal.

rules.statement: For 10 minutes, a level 6 Paladin projects an inactive-when-incapacitated aura 10 feet around them; the Paladin and allies in it add the Paladin’s Charisma modifier (minimum +1) to saving throws. A creature near multiple Paladins benefits from only one such aura, chosen by that creature; at level 18 the radius becomes 30 feet.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 6: Aura of Protection; Level 18: Aura Expansion, p. 55 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a local protective field; dial: radius and bonus; incapacitation suppresses it and overlapping sources do not stack.

rules.statement: At level 9, a Paladin can spend a Channel Divinity use as a Magic action to target a number of visible creatures up to their Charisma modifier (minimum one) within 60 feet. Each target that fails a Wisdom save is Frightened for 1 minute or until it takes damage, and while affected can only move, take an action, or take a Bonus Action on its turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 9: Abjure Foes, p. 55 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a resource-limited fear effect; dial: target count, range, save and duration; damage can end the state early.

rules.statement: At level 14, when a Paladin uses the healing pool on a creature, they may also remove Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned from it. Each condition removed costs 5 pool points, which do not also restore Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 14: Restoring Touch, p. 55 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing energy can clear listed conditions; dial: 5 pool points per condition; those points cannot do double duty as healing.

rules.statement: A level 3 Oath of Devotion Paladin can spend a Channel Divinity use when taking the Attack action to empower a held melee weapon for up to 10 minutes. The Paladin adds their Charisma modifier (minimum +1) to its attack rolls, may deal its normal damage type or Radiant damage on hits, and the weapon sheds Bright Light for 20 feet and Dim Light for a further 20 feet; the effect ends early if dismissed, replaced, or the Paladin stops carrying the weapon.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Oath of Devotion, Level 3: Sacred Weapon, p. 56 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a temporary weapon-bound blessing; dial: use cost and duration; carrying the weapon sustains the effect.

rules.statement: A Ranger always has Hunter’s Mark prepared and can cast it twice without spending a spell slot, refreshing all such uses on a Long Rest; the free-use count rises at specified Ranger levels. At level 13, taking damage cannot break the Ranger’s Concentration on Hunter’s Mark.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 1: Favored Enemy; Level 13: Relentless Hunter, pp. 58–59 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: free casts and concentration protection
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a prepared tracking spell with limited free casts; dial: free-use count by level; damage no longer disrupts concentration at level 13.

rules.statement: At level 14, a Ranger can use a Bonus Action to become Invisible until the end of their next turn. They can do this a number of times equal to their Wisdom modifier (minimum once), regaining all uses on a Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 14: Nature’s Veil, p. 59 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: brief magical concealment; dial: uses per Long Rest; the state lasts only through the next turn.

rules.statement: When a Rogue deals Sneak Attack damage, they may forgo Sneak Attack dice to apply a Cunning Strike effect immediately after the attack’s damage: Poison costs 1d6 and on a failed Constitution save inflicts Poisoned for 1 minute, with a repeat save at each turn’s end; Trip costs 1d6 and can knock a Large-or-smaller target Prone on a failed Dexterity save; Withdraw costs 1d6 and moves the Rogue up to half Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Poison also requires carrying a Poisoner’s Kit; at level 11 the Rogue can apply up to two effects, paying each cost.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 5: Cunning Strike; Level 11: Improved Cunning Strike, p. 63 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: trade damage dice for tactical effects; dial: effect costs and save outcomes; poison also requires a kit.

rules.statement: A level 13 Thief can attune to up to four magic items at once. When using a magic-item property that spends charges, a roll of 6 on 1d6 avoids spending them; the Thief can also use any Spell Scroll, using Intelligence, with an Arcana check at DC 10 plus spell level for spells above level 1, and a failed check destroys the scroll.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Thief, Level 13: Use Magic Device, p. 64 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a specialist handles magic items unusually well; dial: four bonds and a one-in-six charge save; failed higher-level scroll use consumes the scroll.

rules.statement: A Sorcerer can convert a spell slot into Sorcery Points equal to the slot’s level without an action, or use a Bonus Action to turn points into one spell slot of level 1–5, subject to the minimum Sorcerer level and point costs in the slot-creation table. A created slot disappears at the next Long Rest, and the Sorcerer cannot hold more points than their level’s listed maximum.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 2: Font of Magic, p. 66 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: exchange between spell slots and a capped personal reserve; dial: conversion costs and slot limits; created slots expire at a Long Rest.

rules.statement: A Sorcerer’s Innate Sorcery lasts 1 minute, raises the save DC of their Sorcerer spells by 1, and grants Advantage on their Sorcerer spell attack rolls; it has two uses per Long Rest. At level 7, if no uses remain, they can activate it by spending 2 Sorcery Points, and while it is active they can apply up to two Metamagic options to each spell.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Level 1: Innate Sorcery; Level 7: Sorcery Incarnate, pp. 65–66 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a temporary boost to the Sorcerer’s own magic; dial: uses, duration, and point cost; higher-level activation permits more spell alteration.

rules.statement: When casting a spell that makes other creatures save, spend 1 Sorcery Point to choose up to your Charisma modifier creatures (minimum 1); each chosen creature automatically succeeds, and takes no damage if a successful save would otherwise deal half damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 67, Careful Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the feature optional; dial: limit protection to a Charisma-based number of targets and charge 1 Sorcery Point.

rules.statement: Spend 1 Sorcery Point while casting a spell with a range of at least 5 feet to double its range, or change its Touch range to 30 feet.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 67, Distant Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow limited range modification; dial: require 1 Sorcery Point and restrict which ranges qualify.

rules.statement: When rolling a spell’s damage, spend 1 Sorcery Point to reroll up to your Charisma modifier damage dice (minimum 1), and use the new results; this can accompany another Metamagic option used on that casting.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 67, Empowered Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit controlled damage adjustment; dial: charge 1 Sorcery Point and cap rerolls by Charisma.

rules.statement: When casting a spell with a duration of at least 1 minute, spend 1 Sorcery Point to double its duration, up to 24 hours; if it requires Concentration, you have Advantage on saves to maintain it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 67, Extended Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit duration extension; dial: charge 1 Sorcery Point, require a minimum duration, and cap the result at 24 hours.

rules.statement: When casting a spell that forces a creature to save, spend 2 Sorcery Points to give one target Disadvantage on saves against that spell.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 67, Heightened Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow a targeted increase in spell pressure; dial: limit it to one target and charge 2 Sorcery Points.

rules.statement: Spend 2 Sorcery Points to change an action-casting-time spell to a Bonus Action for that casting. This is unavailable if you have already cast a level 1+ spell this turn, and after modifying it you cannot cast a level 1+ spell during the same turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 67, Quickened Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit faster casting; dial: charge 2 Sorcery Points and enforce the turn’s level-1-or-higher spell restriction.

rules.statement: After missing with a spell attack roll, spend 1 Sorcery Point to reroll the d20 and use the new roll; this can accompany another Metamagic option used on that casting.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 67, Seeking Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow one correction to a failed spell attack; dial: require a miss and charge 1 Sorcery Point.

rules.statement: Spend 1 Sorcery Point when casting a spell to omit its Verbal, Somatic, and most Material components; components consumed by the spell or with a specified cost remain required.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 67, Subtle Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit less observable casting; dial: charge 1 Sorcery Point while retaining costly or consumed components.

rules.statement: When casting a spell that deals Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder damage, spend 1 Sorcery Point to change that damage to another type on that list.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 67, Transmuted Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit damage-type adaptation; dial: limit eligible damage types and charge 1 Sorcery Point.

rules.statement: For a spell that can gain an additional target when cast with a higher-level slot, spend 1 Sorcery Point to increase its effective level by 1.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 67, Twinned Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow an eligible spell to reach its higher-level targeting mode; dial: require that the spell has that option and charge 1 Sorcery Point.

rules.statement: A Warlock’s pact with a mysterious entity grants the ability to cast spells. The Warlock knows 2 cantrips initially, may replace one cantrip whenever gaining a Warlock level, and learns additional cantrips at levels 4 and 10.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 71, Level 1: Pact Magic (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: represent a pact as a source of magical ability; dial: the passage specifies the grant but no demanded payment or patron enforcement.

rules.statement: A Warlock’s Pact Magic slots are all the same level, with their quantity and level set by the class table, and return after a Short or Long Rest. The Warlock prepares a limited list of eligible spells, uses Charisma for spellcasting, and can replace one prepared spell whenever gaining a Warlock level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pages 71–72, Level 1: Pact Magic (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: model casting from a replenishing reserve; dial: cap slots and prepared spells by level and require a rest to restore slots.

rules.statement: A 1-minute esoteric rite restores expended Pact Magic slots up to half the Warlock’s maximum, rounded up; it can be used once per Long Rest. At Warlock level 20, using this feature restores all expended Pact Magic slots instead.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 72, Magical Cunning; Eldritch Master (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: let the Warlock recover some stored power through a rite; dial: limit recovery by the slot maximum and rest-based uses, with full recovery only at level 20.

rules.statement: At level 9, a Warlock always has Contact Other Plane prepared and can cast it to contact their patron without spending a spell slot, automatically succeeding on its saving throw; this use returns after a Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 72, Contact Patron (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enable direct contact with the patron; dial: make the contact use once per Long Rest and specify no additional price or response guarantee.

rules.statement: At levels 11, 13, 15, and 17, the patron grants a chosen Warlock spell of levels 6, 7, 8, and 9 respectively; each can be cast once without a spell slot and all uses return after a Long Rest. On gaining a Warlock level, one such spell can be replaced by another Warlock spell of the same level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Page 72, Mystic Arcanum (dnd-srd-5.2.1#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: model a patron’s high-level magical grant; dial: restrict each spell to one free use per Long Rest and permit replacement only at level-up.

rules.statement: An Evoker adds two Evocation spells of level 2 or lower to their spellbook without cost at level 3. Each time they gain access to a new spell-slot level in the class, they can also add one Evocation spell of a level they can cast, without cost.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wizard Subclass: Evoker — Level 3: Evocation Savant, p. 82 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: free learning is limited to Evocation spells and the listed spell-level access; the in-world cost is none.

rules.statement: At level 3, when an Evoker’s damaging cantrip misses its attack or a target succeeds on its save, that target still takes half the cantrip’s damage, if any, but suffers no additional effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wizard Subclass: Evoker — Level 3: Potent Cantrip, p. 82 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: this softens a cantrip’s damage outcome only; it does not preserve other effects.

rules.statement: At level 6, when an Evoker casts an Evocation spell affecting other creatures they can see, they can choose up to one plus the spell’s level of those creatures. Chosen creatures automatically succeed on the spell’s saves and take no damage from it when a successful save would normally deal half damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wizard Subclass: Evoker — Level 6: Sculpt Spells, p. 82 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: protect up to one plus spell level creatures the caster can see; the in-world limit is the spell’s area and the chosen creatures.

rules.statement: At level 10, whenever an Evoker casts a Wizard Evocation spell, they can add their Intelligence modifier to one damage roll for that spell.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wizard Subclass: Evoker — Level 10: Empowered Evocation, p. 82 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bonus applies to only one damage roll per spell; the in-world source is the caster’s Intelligence.

rules.statement: At level 14, when an Evoker casts a damaging Wizard spell using a level 1–5 spell slot, they can deal maximum damage with it on the casting turn. The first use after a Long Rest has no adverse effect; each later use before that rest deals unavoidable Necrotic damage immediately, starting at 2d12 per slot level and increasing by 1d12 per slot level for every further use.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wizard Subclass: Evoker — Level 14: Overchannel, p. 82 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: repeat use trades maximized damage for escalating Necrotic harm that ignores Resistance and Immunity; a Long Rest resets the cost.

rules.statement: A Dragonborn can replace one attack in its Attack action with magical breath in a 15-foot cone or a 30-foot line that is 5 feet wide. Creatures in the area make a Dexterity save against DC 8 plus the Dragonborn’s Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus, taking 1d10 damage of the ancestry type on a failure or half on a success; damage rises to 2d10 at character level 5, 3d10 at 11, and 4d10 at 17.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Species Descriptions — Dragonborn: Breath Weapon, p. 84 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: breath replaces one attack and uses a fixed area and save; damage type follows chosen draconic ancestry.

rules.statement: A Dragonborn can use its Breath Weapon a number of times equal to its Proficiency Bonus, regaining all uses after a Long Rest. Its ancestry also grants Resistance to the corresponding damage type and Darkvision to 60 feet.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Species Descriptions — Dragonborn: Breath Weapon, Damage Resistance, and Darkvision, p. 84 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: breath uses are proficiency-limited and rest-recharged; resistance and sight are persistent traits.

rules.statement: From character level 5, a Dragonborn can use a Bonus Action to sprout spectral wings and gain a Fly Speed equal to its Speed for up to 10 minutes. The wings can be ended without an action, end if the Dragonborn becomes Incapacitated, and can be used once per Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Species Descriptions — Dragonborn: Draconic Flight, p. 84 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: temporary flight lasts at most 10 minutes and is limited to once per Long Rest; Incapacitation ends it.

rules.statement: A Dwarf has Poison damage Resistance, Advantage on saves to avoid or end the Poisoned condition, and a Hit Point maximum that rises by 1 initially and by 1 at every level gained. A Dwarf can also use a Bonus Action while on or touching stone to gain 60-foot Tremorsense for 10 minutes, with uses equal to Proficiency Bonus per Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Species Descriptions — Dwarf, p. 84 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: Tremorsense requires contact with stone and is bounded by duration and rest-based uses; the other benefits are ongoing.

rules.statement: An Elf chooses an Elven lineage and gains its level 1 benefit; at character levels 3 and 5 it learns the listed spell, always has it prepared, and can cast it once without a slot per Long Rest or with an appropriate spell slot. The Elf chooses Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as the spellcasting ability for these lineage spells.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Species Descriptions — Elf: Elven Lineage, pp. 84–85; Elven Lineages table, p. 86 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lineage fixes the spell choices and progression; each learned spell has one free casting per Long Rest, with slots as an alternative.

rules.statement: A Rock Gnome can spend 10 minutes casting Prestidigitation to make a Tiny clockwork device with AC 5 and 1 Hit Point, choosing one effect of that cantrip for it. A creature can activate it by touching it as a Bonus Action; only three devices can exist at once, and each falls apart after 8 hours or when dismantled by touch as a Utilize action.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Species Descriptions — Gnome: Rock Gnome, p. 85 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: one chosen cantrip effect per device, maximum three, and an 8-hour lifespan; making one costs 10 minutes.

rules.statement: A Goliath chooses one Giant Ancestry benefit and can use it a number of times equal to Proficiency Bonus per Long Rest. The options include teleporting up to 30 feet as a Bonus Action to a visible empty space, adding specified elemental damage on a hit, slowing or knocking down a hit target, reducing damage with a Reaction, or dealing Thunder damage as a Reaction to a nearby creature that damaged it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Species Descriptions — Goliath: Giant Ancestry, pp. 85–86 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the player selects one ancestry benefit; its use count is proficiency-limited and recharges on a Long Rest.

rules.statement: From character level 5, a Goliath can become Large as a Bonus Action if space permits, for up to 10 minutes. While transformed, it has Advantage on Strength checks and its Speed increases by 10 feet; the change can be ended without an action and is available once per Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Species Descriptions — Goliath: Large Form, p. 86 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformation requires sufficient space and lasts at most 10 minutes; it is once per Long Rest.

rules.statement: When you take the Attack action, you can replace one attack by throwing Alchemist’s Fire at a visible creature or object within 20 feet. On a failed Dexterity save (DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + Proficiency Bonus), it takes 1d4 Fire damage and begins burning.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Adventuring Gear — Alchemist’s Fire, p. 95 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one attack and a saving throw gate the effect; the target pays in damage and continued burning.

rules.statement: As a Bonus Action, drink Antitoxin to gain Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Antitoxin, p. 96 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the benefit lasts one hour and requires consuming the vial.

rules.statement: As a Utilize action, spill Ball Bearings to cover a level 10-foot-square within 10 feet. A creature entering that area for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity save or become Prone; recovering the bearings takes 10 minutes.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ball Bearings, p. 96 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the field is localized and recoverable, with a failed save causing the condition.

rules.statement: As a Utilize action, spread Caltrops over a 5-foot-square within 5 feet. A creature entering for the first time on a turn must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity save or take 1 Piercing damage and have Speed 0 until the start of its next turn; recovery takes 10 minutes.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Caltrops, p. 96 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited area and brief movement denial are traded for setup and recovery time.

rules.statement: As a Utilize action, you can chain-bind an unwilling creature within 5 feet that is Grappled, Incapacitated, or Restrained by succeeding on a DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check. Bound legs impose Restrained until escape; escaping takes an action and a successful DC 18 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check, while bursting the chain takes an action and a successful DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Chain, p. 96 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: binding requires the target to be vulnerable first, and escape or breaking it takes effort.

rules.statement: As a Utilize action, set a Hunting Trap fixed by a heavy chain to an immobile object. A creature stepping on it must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity save or take 1d4 Piercing damage and have Speed 0 until the start of its next turn; afterward its movement is limited by the chain, typically 3 feet, until freed with an action and a successful DC 13 Strength (Athletics) check. Each failed escape check deals 1 Piercing damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Hunting Trap, pp. 97–98 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the trap is anchored and escape attempts are costly, including damage on failure.

rules.statement: A flask of Holy Water can replace one attack in the Attack action and targets a visible creature within 20 feet. On a failed Dexterity save (DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + Proficiency Bonus), a Fiend or Undead takes 2d8 Radiant damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Holy Water, p. 97 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: it costs an attack and only harms specified creature types after a failed save.

rules.statement: When you take the Attack action, you can replace one attack by throwing a Net at a creature you can see within 15 feet. On a failed Dexterity save (DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + Proficiency Bonus), it becomes Restrained until escape; a Huge or larger target succeeds automatically. The target or a creature within 5 feet can use an action and succeed on a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check to free it, or destroying the Net (AC 10, 5 HP; immune to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage) ends the effect.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: range, size immunity, and an escape or destruction route limit the restraint.

rules.statement: If an oiled creature or object takes Fire damage before the oil dries after 1 minute, it takes 5 extra Fire damage. As a Utilize action, oil poured over a level 5-foot-square burns for 2 rounds after ignition, dealing 5 Fire damage to a creature that enters or ends its turn there, at most once per turn; oil also fuels a Lamp or Lantern for 6 hours total and can be extinguished or rekindled with a Utilize action.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: fire damage requires an ignition opportunity, and area damage is bounded by duration and once-per-turn exposure.

rules.statement: A creature drinking a Potion of Healing as a Bonus Action regains 2d4 + 2 Hit Points; you can instead administer it to another creature within 5 feet.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Healing, p. 99 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one potion is consumed for a limited, immediate restoration.

rules.statement: To attune, spend a Short Rest focused solely on the item while touching it; the rest cannot also be used to identify it, and interruption makes the attempt fail. Attunement allows access to its magical properties, but you can have no more than three items attuned and cannot attune to more than one copy of an item.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Attunement, p. 102 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: bonding costs focused rest time and is limited to three distinct item slots.

rules.statement: Attunement ends if you cease meeting its prerequisites, the item stays more than 100 feet away for at least 24 hours, you die, or another creature attunes to it. You may also end it by spending another Short Rest focused on the item, unless it is cursed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ending Attunement, p. 102–103 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: separation, death, replacement, or a focused rest ends the bond; a curse can block voluntary release.

rules.statement: A level 0 cantrip requires no spell slot; a Ritual-tagged spell can be cast as a Ritual by a spellcaster who has it prepared, taking 10 minutes longer and using no slot. A Long Rest restores expended spell slots, and casting a spell with a higher-level slot makes it that higher level for that casting.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Casting Spells — Spell Slots and Casting without Slots, p. 104 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: limited slots recover on a Long Rest; rituals exchange extra time for preserving slots.

rules.statement: A spell can affect only targets named or permitted by its description, and the caster needs an unobstructed path to the target; Total Cover blocks targeting. A creature may target itself unless the spell requires a hostile creature or someone other than the caster.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Targets (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a clear path is required; dial: none; cover prevents direct magical targeting.

rules.statement: A spell’s area shape determines its targets, and a creature generally does not know it was targeted unless the spell’s effect is perceptible or its description says otherwise. If a target cannot be affected, nothing happens to it, but any spell slot used is still spent; a failed-looking save may conceal the target’s invalidity when saves would normally negate the effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Targets (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: subtle targeting can go unnoticed and invalid attempts still cost a slot; dial: none; the magic cannot affect an ineligible target.

rules.statement: Spell save DC equals 8 + the caster’s spellcasting ability modifier + Proficiency Bonus. Spell attack modifier equals the spellcasting ability modifier + Proficiency Bonus.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Saving Throws; Attack Rolls (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: spell attack and save calculations
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the stated formulas; dial: none; training and casting aptitude set accuracy and resistance difficulty.

rules.statement: Different spells’ effects add together while their durations overlap. Multiple castings of the same spell do not stack; the strongest applies, or the newest if equally strong, and it lasts until that casting ends.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Combining Spell Effects (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: distinct effects combine but duplicate castings do not; dial: none; repeated magic cannot multiply an identical benefit.

rules.statement: Acid Arrow makes a ranged spell attack at a target within 90 feet: a hit deals 4d4 Acid damage and another 2d4 at the end of the target’s next turn; a miss deals half the initial damage only. Each slot level above 2 adds 1d4 to each damage instance.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Descriptions, Acid Arrow (p. 107) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: delayed damage follows a hit; dial: higher slots add damage; the target’s exposure continues briefly after impact.

rules.statement: Aid affects up to three creatures within 30 feet for 8 hours, increasing each target’s current and maximum Hit Points by 5. Each slot level above 2 increases that amount by 5 per target.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Descriptions, Aid (p. 107) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: up to three allies gain a temporary increase for eight hours; dial: higher slots increase the amount; the benefit is limited by duration and range.

rules.statement: Alarm wards a door, window, or area no larger than a 20-foot Cube within 30 feet for 8 hours, alerting the caster when a creature touches or enters it; chosen creatures can be excluded. The caster chooses an audible bell heard within 60 feet or a mental alert received within 1 mile that can awaken them.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Descriptions, Alarm (p. 107) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an intrusion triggers a bounded warning; dial: audible or mental, with stated ranges; the ward monitors only its chosen space and duration.

rules.statement: Alter Self lasts up to 1 hour with Concentration and lets the caster switch options using a Magic action: gain underwater breathing and a Swim Speed equal to Speed; alter appearance without changing statistics, size, or basic shape; or grow a natural weapon that deals 1d6 of its specified damage type on an Unarmed Strike, using the spellcasting modifier for attack and damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Descriptions, Alter Self (p. 107) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one bodily alteration at a time; dial: switchable with a Magic action; Concentration and the spell’s limits constrain the transformation.

rules.statement: Animate Dead turns a Medium or Small Humanoid corpse into a Zombie, or bones into a Skeleton. As a Bonus Action, the caster can mentally command creations within 60 feet; otherwise they Dodge and avoid harm, and control lasts 24 hours unless the spell is recast before then to renew it, maintaining control over up to four such creatures.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Descriptions, Animate Dead (p. 108) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: command is limited by distance and a 24-hour control period; dial: higher slots animate or renew two more per slot level above 3; remains and repeated magic carry the cost.

rules.statement: Antimagic Field creates a 10-foot Emanation around the caster for up to 1 hour with Concentration. Inside it, spells, Magic actions, other magical effects, magic-item properties, incoming area effects, teleportation, and planar travel are blocked; portals temporarily close and ongoing spells are suppressed, with their duration still passing, except effects from Artifacts or deities.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Descriptions, Antimagic Field (p. 109) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: magic is suppressed in a small moving zone; dial: none; the field also prevents entry or exit by teleportation and planar travel.

rules.statement: Astral Projection sends the caster and up to eight willing creatures to the Astral Plane, leaving their bodies unconscious, ageless, and without need for food or air; each target requires consumed components worth at least 1,100 GP. A severed silver cord kills both forms, damage to either form does not affect the other, and leaving the Astral Plane carries the body and possessions along the cord so the target re-enters its body on the destination plane.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Descriptions, Astral Projection (p. 111) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel requires willing targets and costly consumed components; dial: up to eight companions; a severed cord kills, while planar departure returns each traveler to its body.

rules.statement: Banishment sends one creature that fails a Charisma save to a harmless demiplane for up to 1 minute, where it is Incapacitated; when the spell ends it returns to its former space or the nearest open space. If the target is an Aberration, Celestial, Elemental, Fey, or Fiend and the spell lasts a full minute, it instead goes to a random location on a plane selected by the GM that is associated with its creature type.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Descriptions, Banishment (p. 112) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save removes one target temporarily; dial: higher slots can add targets; certain extraplanar types risk permanent displacement after a full minute.

rules.statement: Commune lets the caster ask a deity or divine proxy up to three yes-or-no questions and receive correct answers if the being knows them; the spell takes 1 minute. Each casting after the first before a Long Rest adds a cumulative 25% chance of receiving no answer.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Descriptions, Commune (p. 116) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: up to three questions receive answers within the contacted being’s knowledge; dial: repeated use raises the no-answer chance; divine knowledge is not unlimited.

rules.statement: A creature you touch regains 2d8 Hit Points plus your spellcasting ability modifier; each spell slot level above 1 adds another 2d8 healing.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cure Wounds, p. 121 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing restores a measurable amount; dial: spell-slot level; in-world cost: a spell slot.

rules.statement: You can mentally command up to three eligible Humanoid corpses to become Ghouls, but only at night; the creatures obey you for 24 hours and then require another casting to renew control. Higher-level slots increase the number or allow stronger undead, up to two Mummies with a level 9 slot.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Create Undead, p. 121 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: created undead obey for a fixed term; dial: slot level and number or strength of undead; in-world cost: corpses, black onyx, and repeated castings to maintain control.

rules.statement: You create an object no larger than a 5-foot cube from shadow-stuff, using a form and material you have seen. Its duration depends on its material, from 24 hours for plant matter down to 1 minute for adamantine or mithral; the object cannot serve as another spell’s material component.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Creation, p. 121 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: created matter is temporary; dial: material and spell-slot level; in-world cost: short duration and restriction on spell components.

rules.statement: A magical 30-foot-square-or-smaller door opens into an empty 30-foot room of wood or stone for 1 hour. When it vanishes, contents remain inside; creatures may leave as it closes, and each casting can open a new room or connect to a known room created by this spell, including one made by another caster.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Demiplane, p. 123 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the door connects to a bounded pocket space; dial: access duration and destination; in-world cost: creatures or objects left inside can be stranded.

rules.statement: You teleport yourself up to 500 feet to a spot you can see, visualize, or specify by distance and direction, and may take one willing creature within 5 feet to a destination within 5 feet of yours. If either arrival space is occupied or completely obstructed, the teleport fails and each traveler takes 4d6 Force damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dimension Door, p. 123–124 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: teleportation moves travelers to a chosen location; dial: range and optional passenger; in-world cost: failed arrival causes damage.

rules.statement: One visible creature you choose within 60 feet must resist or become Charmed for up to 1 minute; while you and it remain on the same plane, you can telepathically issue commands without an action. Damage lets it repeat the save, and it may resist better if you or allies are fighting it; ordering it to use a Reaction costs your Reaction.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dominate Person, p. 126 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save permits compelled behavior; dial: target type, duration, and resistance; in-world cost: concentration and the target’s repeated saves when harmed.

rules.statement: A visible target that fails its save against the level 6 spell takes 10d6 + 40 Force damage; if this reduces a creature to 0 Hit Points, it and its nonmagical gear are destroyed as dust and can be restored only by True Resurrection or Wish. The spell automatically destroys a Large-or-smaller nonmagical object or force creation, or a 10-foot-cube portion of a larger one.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Disintegrate, p. 124 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save can destroy a target; dial: spell-slot level increases damage; in-world cost: the effect is lethal and ordinary revival is insufficient.

rules.statement: You can end ongoing spells of level 3 or lower on one creature, object, or magical effect within 120 feet; for each higher-level spell, you must succeed on a spellcasting ability check against DC 10 plus that spell’s level. A slot at a higher level automatically ends spells no higher than that slot’s level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dispel Magic, p. 124 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ongoing spells can be ended; dial: the target spell’s level and slot level; in-world cost: higher-level effects require a check unless matched by a stronger slot.

rules.statement: You ask one question about a specific goal, event, or activity expected within 7 days and receive a truthful answer that may be cryptic; the spell does not account for circumstances that could change the answer. After the first casting before a Long Rest, each additional casting has a cumulative 25% chance of yielding no answer.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Divination, p. 125 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a divine source answers one near-term question; dial: repeated castings increase failure chance; in-world cost: consumed incense and unreliable applicability when circumstances change.

rules.statement: You contact an otherworldly intelligence and, after succeeding on a DC 15 Intelligence save, may ask up to five questions answered in one word or a short phrase. On a failed save, you take 6d6 Psychic damage and remain Incapacitated until a Long Rest, unless Greater Restoration ends the effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Contact Other Plane, p. 119 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: questions obtain limited otherworldly knowledge; dial: up to five answers; in-world cost: risk of severe mental injury and incapacitation.

rules.statement: You can teleport a summoned Fey spirit up to 30 feet as a Bonus Action and make a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet of its new space, dealing 3d12 Psychic damage plus your spellcasting modifier and frightening it until your next turn on a hit. The spirit lasts up to 10 minutes while you maintain concentration; higher-level slots add 1d12 damage per level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Conjure Fey, p. 118 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a conjured spirit enables a repeatable attack and repositioning; dial: spell-slot level and concentration duration; in-world cost: maintaining concentration.

rules.statement: A creature that fails its save against the elemental spirit’s effect takes 8d8 damage of the chosen element and becomes Restrained; while restrained, it repeats the save at the start of each turn, taking 4d8 damage on a failure and ending the restraint on a success. The spirit lasts up to 10 minutes with concentration, and higher-level slots increase damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Conjure Elemental, p. 118 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the conjured spirit can restrain and damage a creature; dial: elemental choice, spell-slot level, and concentration; in-world cost: the effect ends when concentration ends or the target succeeds.

rules.statement: For up to 8 hours, you can enter the Border Ethereal where it overlaps your current plane. You can move in any direction, but each foot of upward or downward movement costs 2 feet; you can perceive the plane you left only within 60 feet, and can interact only with things on the Ethereal Plane. When the spell ends, you return to the corresponding spot; if it is occupied, you move to the nearest unoccupied space and take Force damage equal to twice the distance moved in feet. Casting it while already on the Ethereal Plane or on a plane that does not border it ends the spell instantly.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Etherealness, p. 128 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the spell enables temporary planar passage, limited by its duration, movement cost, and restricted interaction.

rules.statement: For 1 day, ward up to 40,000 square feet of floor area to a height of 30 feet against teleportation, portals, and access by planar travel, including travel through the Astral or Ethereal Plane, the Feywild, the Shadowfell, or Plane Shift. Choose one or more creature types to take 5d10 Radiant or Necrotic damage when they enter for the first time on a turn or end a turn inside; a spoken password prevents that damage. Casting the spell at the same location every day for 30 days makes it last until dispelled and consumes the final casting’s material components.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Forbiddance, p. 133 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the ward blocks magical entry and penalizes selected intruders, at the cost of a costly component and repeated daily castings for permanence.

rules.statement: For up to 1 minute, create a 5-to-20-foot-wide portal from a visible unoccupied space within 60 feet to a precise location on another plane; the destination is visible through it, and passage works only through its front. A planar ruler can prevent the portal from opening in its presence or domain. Alternatively, naming a specific creature on another plane opens the portal beside it and transports it to your side, but gives you no control over it.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the portal allows cross-plane movement but requires a precise destination, costly diamond, and brief concentration.

rules.statement: A 1-hour casting using incense worth at least 10 GP summons one familiar spirit in a chosen eligible animal form. It obeys your commands but acts independently, cannot attack, and can communicate telepathically with you within 100 feet; as a Bonus Action you can borrow its senses until your next turn. It can deliver a touch-range spell using its Reaction if within 100 feet. You can have only one familiar: recasting replaces its form; at 0 Hit Points it disappears and returns only after you cast the spell again, while a Magic action can dismiss it temporarily to a pocket dimension or permanently.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Find Familiar, p. 130 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the spirit provides scouting and spell delivery, limited by distance, action economy, one-companion capacity, and consumed incense.

rules.statement: A 1-minute casting gives a visible creature a verbal command for 30 days; if it fails a Wisdom save, it is Charmed for the duration, but automatically succeeds if it cannot understand the command. Acting directly against the command deals 5d10 Psychic damage, at most once per day; a command that would certainly kill the target ends the spell. Remove Curse, Greater Restoration, or Wish ends it; a level 7–8 slot extends it to 365 days, and a level 9 slot lasts until ended by one of those spells.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the command binds behavior through recurring pain, but requires comprehension and can be broken by specified magic.

rules.statement: A visible creature that fails a Constitution save becomes Restrained for up to 1 minute; constructs automatically succeed. A Restrained target makes another Constitution save at the end of each turn: three successes end the spell, while three failures turn it to stone and give it the Petrified condition. If you maintain Concentration for the spell’s entire possible duration, the target remains Petrified until Greater Restoration or similar magic ends the condition.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Flesh to Stone, p. 133 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the effect escalates through repeated saves, giving the target chances to resist before lasting petrification.

rules.statement: Immediately after hitting a creature with a weapon, you can cast this spell as a Bonus Action: grasping vines force a Strength save, with Large or larger creatures having Advantage. Failure gives the target Restrained for up to 1 minute and deals 1d6 Piercing damage at the start of each of its turns; the target or a creature within reach can use an action to succeed on a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC to end the spell. A slot above level 1 adds 1d6 damage per level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ensnaring Strike, p. 128 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the hit sets up a temporary restraint with recurring damage, while a successful escape check ends it.

rules.statement: Plants fill a 20-foot square within 90 feet for up to 1 minute, making the ground Difficult Terrain. Each creature other than the caster in the area when the spell is cast must succeed on a Strength save or become Restrained; a restrained creature can use an action to succeed on a Strength (Athletics) check against the caster’s spell save DC and free itself.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Entangle, p. 128 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the plants impede movement across a bounded area and allow restrained creatures to escape through effort.

rules.statement: A 1-hour casting inscribes a nearly imperceptible glyph on a surface or inside a closable object, using diamond powder worth at least 200 GP. The inscription ends if its surface or object moves more than 10 feet; you set its trigger and can specify creature types or passwords that exempt creatures. When triggered, it either deals 5d8 chosen elemental damage in a 20-foot-radius Sphere, or releases a prepared spell of level 3 or lower; the spell targets the trigger creature or centers its area on that creature, and a stored spell requiring Concentration lasts its full duration. A higher-level slot adds 1d8 explosive damage per level or permits storing a spell up to that slot’s level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Glyph of Warding, pp. 136–137 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; delayed magic can be hidden and selectively triggered, but requires costly materials, lengthy casting, and a fixed location.

rules.statement: A touch spell can grant a willing creature the Invisible condition for up to 1 minute, as long as the caster maintains Concentration.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Greater Invisibility, p. 137 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; invisibility lasts only while Concentration is maintained.

rules.statement: You can magically remove one effect from a touched creature: one Exhaustion level, Charmed or Petrified, a curse including attunement to a cursed magic item, an ability-score reduction, or a Hit Point maximum reduction. The spell consumes diamond dust worth at least 100 GP.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Greater Restoration, p. 137 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; powerful afflictions can be removed, but only one listed effect per casting and at a material cost.

rules.statement: A 10-minute casting converts visible raw materials into an object of the same material, given sufficient material: at most Large within a 10-foot Cube or eight connected 5-foot Cubes, but at most Medium for metal, stone, or other minerals. Quality depends on the materials; the spell cannot create creatures or magic items, and cannot make objects requiring high skill, such as weapons or armor, unless the caster is proficient with the relevant Artisan’s Tools.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fabricate, p. 129 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; raw materials become useful products, constrained by material quantity, size, quality, and the caster’s crafting proficiency.

rules.statement: A summoned familiar or steed is not reproduced here as a general patron bargain or pact: this passage assigns the familiar spell to Wizards and the steed spell to Paladins, and specifies their summoning rules rather than a patron’s grants or demands.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Find Familiar and Find Steed, pp. 130–131 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the passage gives spell access by class and does not state a patron contract or pact rule.

rules.statement: If Guards and Wards is cast on the same area every day for 365 days, it lasts until all its effects are dispelled. Its warding can obscure corridors, misdirect creatures at junctions with a 50% chance, magically lock doors, disguise up to ten doors as walls, and refill destroyed stair webs after 10 minutes; the caster also selects one listed additional effect, some of which can likewise return after 10 minutes.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Guards and Wards, Wards ends / Corridors / Doors / Stairs / Other Spell Effect (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the protected area and its chosen effects; the caster must maintain the daily casting for a year, and dispelling all effects ends the long-lasting ward.

rules.statement: Hallow infuses an area of up to 60-foot radius, takes 24 hours to cast, consumes incense worth at least 1,000 GP, and fails if its area overlaps another Hallow. Choose a creature type barred from willing entry and unable to impose possession, Charmed, or Frightened there; also bind one listed area effect, such as blocking specified creatures’ teleportation and planar travel or granting chosen creatures a damage resistance or vulnerability.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Hallow (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the warded types and one extra effect; costly incense, a full day of casting, and the no-overlap restriction limit deployment.

rules.statement: Haste doubles a willing visible creature’s Speed, grants +2 AC and Advantage on Dexterity saves, and grants one extra action each turn, restricted to one attack, Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Utilize. When the spell ends, the target is Incapacitated and has Speed 0 until the end of its next turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Haste (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the duration up to 1 minute; concentration and the lethargy aftereffect make the temporary acceleration costly.

rules.statement: Heal restores 70 Hit Points to a visible creature within 60 feet and ends its Blinded, Deafened, and Poisoned conditions; each spell slot level above 6 adds 10 Hit Points restored. Lesser Restoration instead ends one of Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, or Poisoned, while Mass Heal can distribute up to 700 Hit Points among visible creatures within 60 feet and also ends the first three of those conditions on each healed creature.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Heal; Lesser Restoration; Mass Heal (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the amount of healing by spell slot for Heal and Lesser Restoration; Mass Heal has a fixed 700-point pool to divide.

rules.statement: Imprisonment targets a visible creature within 30 feet: on a successful Wisdom save it is unaffected and immune to this spell for 24 hours, while failure traps it until dispelled. The target does not need food, drink, air, or age, cannot be located or perceived by divination spells, and cannot teleport; the caster chooses a prison form and a specific observable release trigger likely to occur within a decade, and only Dispel Magic cast with a level 9 slot can end it by targeting the prison or its component.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Imprisonment / Ending the Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the prison form and release trigger subject to GM approval; a failed save can impose an indefinite confinement that is difficult to dispel.

rules.statement: Magic Jar puts the caster’s soul in a costly container while their body becomes catatonic; from it, the caster can project within 100 feet or attempt to possess a visible Humanoid in that distance. A failed Charisma save swaps the host’s soul into the jar and gives the caster control of the host body, but the caster takes the host’s Hit Points, Hit Point Dice, physical abilities, Speed, and senses; destroying the jar or ending the spell returns the caster to their body only if it is alive and within 100 feet, otherwise the caster dies.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magic Jar (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial possession to visible Humanoids within 100 feet; the caster risks their own body and life, and the displaced soul is confined.

rules.statement: Magnificent Mansion creates a door to an extradimensional dwelling for 24 hours; its layout may contain at most 50 connected 10-foot cubes, and up to 100 designated creatures may enter while the door remains open. Furnishings removed from the dwelling dissipate, its servants cannot leave or directly harm creatures, and when the spell ends anything inside is expelled into unoccupied spaces nearest the entrance.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magnificent Mansion (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the layout and designated entrants within the stated limits; the space and its contents are temporary, and occupants are expelled when it ends.

rules.statement: Magic Circle creates a 10-foot-radius, 20-foot-high cylinder for 1 hour, choosing one or more creature types from Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, or Undead. Chosen creatures cannot willingly enter by nonmagical means and must save against Charisma to enter by teleportation or interplanar travel; they have Disadvantage on attacks against targets inside, which cannot be possessed or Charmed or Frightened by them, and the caster may reverse the boundary’s direction.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magic Circle (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the affected creature types and whether the boundary blocks entry or exit; consumed materials and limited duration constrain the ward.

rules.statement: Meld into Stone lets the caster and equipment merge into a stone surface large enough to contain them for up to 8 hours; nonmagical senses cannot detect the caster, who cannot see outside or move except to exit at the entry point. Partial destruction or reshaping that makes the stone too small expels the caster and deals 6d6 Force damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Meld into Stone (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the stone’s size and duration; the caster is immobile and risks damage if the stone is altered.

rules.statement: Mass Suggestion can affect up to twelve creatures within 60 feet that hear and understand a plausible instruction of no more than 25 words; each target that fails a Wisdom save is Charmed and follows it as well as it can. The effect ends for a target if the caster’s side damages it or it completes the activity, and a higher-level slot can extend its duration from 24 hours to 10, 30, or 366 days at levels 7, 8, or 9.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mass Suggestion (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial target count and duration by spell slot; the instruction must seem achievable and cannot plainly threaten damage to targets or allies.

rules.statement: Identify takes 1 minute or can be cast as a ritual while touching an object; for a magic item it reveals properties, use, whether Attunement is required, charge count, ongoing spells, and the name of a creating spell if applicable. If cast while touching a creature, it instead reveals ongoing spells affecting that creature.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Identify (dnd-srd-5.2.1#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the target as an object or creature; the caster must sustain touch through casting and provide a pearl worth at least 100 GP.

rules.statement: You can call on a known cosmic being to send a loyal Celestial, Elemental, or Fiend to an unoccupied space within 60 feet. You must negotiate for its service; typical payment is 100 GP per minute, 1,000 GP per hour, or 10,000 GP per day for up to 10 days, with adjustments for danger, safety, or alignment. If no price is agreed, it immediately returns home.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Planar Ally (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: make aid a negotiated exchange; dial: adjust or waive payment for circumstances and shared ethos; in-world cost: the summoned being is not compelled to help.

rules.statement: You can spend an hour and a consumed jewel worth at least 1,000 GP attempting to bind a Celestial, Elemental, Fey, or Fiend within 60 feet; it must remain in range throughout the casting and can resist with a Charisma save. On failure, it must follow commands for 24 hours, though a Hostile creature may twist them; higher-level slots extend the binding to 10, 30, 180, or 366 days at levels 6 through 9.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Planar Binding (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: binding lasts for a defined term; dial: higher slots extend that term; in-world cost: a costly jewel is consumed and the target can resist.

rules.statement: You and up to eight willing creatures holding hands can travel to another plane by touch, using a forked metal rod worth at least 250 GP attuned to a plane. You arrive at a broadly specified destination as the GM determines, or at a teleportation circle whose sigil sequence you know; travelers who do not fit beside it arrive in nearby unoccupied spaces.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Plane Shift (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow group travel between planes; dial: require a plane-attuned rod and limit precise arrival to known circle sigils; in-world cost: the party risks arriving near rather than exactly at its destination.

rules.statement: A 100-foot-sided Cube or smaller can be warded for 24 hours to block selected forms of access or detection: sound, vision through its boundary, divination sensors, divination targeting, teleportation, or planar travel. Recasting daily on the same location for 365 days makes the ward last until dispelled; each slot level above 4 increases the Cube’s side length by 100 feet.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Private Sanctum (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: let the caster select ward functions; dial: require a year of daily casting for permanence; in-world cost: the protected space is bounded and must be maintained.

rules.statement: A touched willing creature is immune to Psychic damage and the Charmed condition for 24 hours. During that time, effects cannot sense its emotions or alignment, read its thoughts, detect its location, gather information about it, observe it remotely, or control its mind—even through Wish.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mind Blank (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: provide a fixed-day defense against mental intrusion and detection; dial: make the protection comprehensive; in-world cost: it requires a level 8 spell.

rules.statement: You can reshape a visible creature’s memories of an event from the past 24 hours, lasting no more than 10 minutes, if it fails a Wisdom save; a creature you are fighting has Advantage on that save. The target is Charmed and Incapacitated while you describe the change, but damage or another spell ends the effect before alteration; a completed change takes hold when the spell ends and can be reversed by Remove Curse or Greater Restoration. Higher-level slots extend the event’s age limit to 7, 30, or 365 days, or any time in the past, at levels 6 through 9.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Modify Memory (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit alteration only of a bounded event; dial: higher slots reach further into the past; in-world cost: the target can resist, interruption prevents the change, and restorative magic can undo it.

rules.statement: A creature that fails its save against Moonbeam takes 2d10 Radiant damage and, if shape-shifted, returns to its true form and cannot shape-shift while it remains in the beam. The 5-foot-radius, 40-foot-high beam can be moved up to 60 feet with a later Magic action, and creatures save when it appears, moves onto them, or they enter it or end a turn there, at most once per turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Moonbeam (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an area effect can force a shape-shifted creature back to its true form; dial: repeat exposure can trigger another save once each turn; in-world cost: maintaining and moving the beam requires concentration and actions.

rules.statement: You can teleport yourself up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see as a Bonus Action; the effect is instantaneous.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Misty Step (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow a short, immediate relocation; dial: restrict arrival to a visible unoccupied space within 30 feet; in-world cost: it does not provide longer-range travel.

rules.statement: A creature inside a Passwall opening when the spell ends, or inside a passage made in a different substance, is expelled to the nearest unoccupied space by the surface where it entered and takes 50 Force damage. It also falls Prone.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Passwall (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: expel anything left in an incompatible or expired passage; dial: apply fixed damage and Prone; in-world cost: remaining in the passage is dangerous.

rules.statement: A willing creature enclosed by Resilient Sphere can breathe, but nothing—including objects, energy, or spell effects—can cross its barrier, and neither side can harm the other across it. The sphere lasts up to 1 minute with concentration, rolls at up to half the enclosed creature’s Speed if pushed, and a Disintegrate spell can destroy it without harming its contents.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Resilient Sphere (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: create a temporary, two-way barrier; dial: allow escape by destroying the sphere with a specific spell; in-world cost: the occupant cannot affect anything outside while enclosed.

rules.statement: You can revive a creature that died within the last minute by touch; it returns with 1 Hit Point. The spell cannot revive someone who died of old age and does not restore missing body parts.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Revivify (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow a rapid return from recent death; dial: enforce a one-minute window and 1 Hit Point return; in-world cost: it cannot overcome old age or replace lost parts.

rules.statement: A creature that fails its save against Power Word Stun becomes Stunned if it has 150 Hit Points or fewer. Otherwise, its Speed becomes 0 until the start of your next turn; a Stunned target can repeat a Constitution save at the end of each of its turns to end the condition.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Power Word Stun (dnd-srd-5.2.1#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: make the effect depend on the target’s Hit Points; dial: targets above the threshold suffer only a brief movement restriction; in-world cost: a Stunned target can recover through repeated saves.

rules.statement: A caster can hide a nonliving chest and up to 12 cubic feet of contents on the Ethereal Plane, then recall it to the ground within 5 feet by spending a Magic action and touching its miniature replica; another Magic action and touching both chest and replica sends it back. After 60 days, the spell has a cumulative 5% chance to end at each day’s end; recasting it or destroying the replica also ends it, leaving a chest still on the Ethereal Plane there.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Secret Chest, p. 160 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the long-term risk; valuable storage can be stranded if the spell ends while the chest is elsewhere.

rules.statement: Scrying takes 10 minutes and requires a focus worth at least 1,000 GP; the chosen creature gets a Wisdom save modified by familiarity (+5 for secondhand, 0 for firsthand, −5 for extensive) and physical evidence (−2 for a likeness, −4 for a possession, −10 for a body part). On a success, the spell cannot target that creature again for 24 hours; on a failure, an invisible sensor appears within 10 feet and follows it for up to 10 minutes, while a known location can instead be sensed by a stationary sensor.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Scrying, p. 160 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial access through saves and costly evidence; the target may resist and successful resistance temporarily blocks another attempt.

rules.statement: Sequester makes an object or willing creature invisible and prevents magical divination, detection, and remote viewing; a creature also becomes unconscious, does not age, and needs no food, water, or air. The caster may set an early-ending condition that occurs or is visible within 1 mile; any damage also ends the spell, and casting it consumes gem dust worth at least 5,000 GP.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sequester, p. 161 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the costly, damage-sensitive protection; hiding a person also suspends their awareness and ordinary needs.

rules.statement: Teleport moves the caster and up to eight willing creatures they can see within 10 feet, or one eligible object, to a known destination on the same plane. Arrival depends on familiarity: a mishap deals 3d10 Force damage and requires a reroll, a similar-area result sends the group to a nearby lookalike place, an off-target result places them 2d12 miles away in a random direction, and an on-target result reaches the intended spot.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Teleport, p. 168 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial destination reliability; uncertain knowledge can cause injury or a dangerous arrival away from the intended place.

rules.statement: Teleportation Circle opens a portal for a short time by drawing a 5-foot-radius circle and spending rare inks worth at least 50 GP; it links only to a permanent circle on the same plane whose sigil sequence the caster knows. A creature entering arrives within 5 feet of the destination circle, or in its nearest unoccupied space; making a circle permanent requires casting the spell at the same site every day for 365 days.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Teleportation Circle, pp. 168–169 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial destination access; travel requires learned sigils, a prepared endpoint, and costly inks.

rules.statement: Sending can deliver a message of at most 25 words to a known or sufficiently described creature at any distance, including across planes, but cross-planar delivery has a 5% failure chance that the caster learns about. A recipient can block further messages for 8 hours; an attempted message during that period fails and reveals the block.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sending, p. 161 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial cross-planar reliability; distance does not prevent contact, but planar boundaries can disrupt delivery and recipients can refuse repeat contact.

rules.statement: Sanctuary wards one creature within 30 feet for up to 1 minute; anyone targeting it with an attack roll or damaging spell must pass a Wisdom save or choose another target or lose the attack or spell. The ward does not protect against areas of effect and ends if the warded creature attacks, casts a spell, or deals damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sanctuary, p. 160 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the ward’s limits; protection fails against area effects and is lost when the protected creature acts aggressively.

rules.statement: Shapechange lasts up to 1 hour with concentration and changes the caster into a previously seen non-Construct, non-Undead creature whose Challenge Rating does not exceed the caster’s level or rating. The caster gains temporary Hit Points equal to the first form’s Hit Points, uses that form’s statistics while retaining specified personal traits and spellcasting, and may use a Magic action to change to another eligible form.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Shapechange, p. 161 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial form eligibility and concentration; transformation is limited by known forms, rank, and the risk of losing the spell.

rules.statement: Sleep affects chosen creatures in a 5-foot-radius Sphere: each must pass a Wisdom save or become incapacitated until the end of its next turn, then save again; failing that second save makes it unconscious for up to 1 minute. Damage ends the effect on that target, as does an action by someone within 5 feet to shake it; creatures that do not sleep or are immune to exhaustion automatically succeed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sleep, p. 163 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the staged saves and counters; the effect can be resisted, interrupted by damage, or ended by an ally.

rules.statement: Storm of Vengeance lasts up to 1 minute with concentration and develops on a fixed sequence of later turns: acid rain on turn 2, six lightning strikes on turn 3, hail on turn 4, then cold damage and severe weather on turns 5–10. The initial storm can damage and deafen creatures beneath it; later stages add area damage, difficult terrain, heavy obscurity, and restrictions on ranged weapon attacks.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Storm of Vengeance, pp. 165–166 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the escalating sequence; the storm’s strongest effects take time to arrive and require maintaining concentration.

rules.statement: A Telepathic Bond links up to eight willing creatures within 30 feet for 1 hour so each can communicate mentally with all the others over any distance; the link cannot cross planes, and creatures unable to communicate in any language are unaffected.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Telepathic Bond, p. 168 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
