rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial membership and planar reach; participants must consent and the connection cannot bridge planes.

rules.statement: After entering a tree at a cost of 5 feet of movement, you learn the locations of same-kind trees within 500 feet and may travel to one or leave the tree as part of that move, appearing within 5 feet of the destination for another 5 feet of movement. This can happen once per turn, and you must finish each turn outside a tree.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Tree transportation ability (preceding True Polymorph) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by tree kind and 500-foot range; the route requires suitable trees and movement.

rules.statement: True Polymorph can affect one visible creature or nonmagical object within 30 feet, with an unwilling creature allowed a Wisdom save to avoid it. It lasts up to 1 hour with Concentration, but becomes lasting until dispelled if Concentration is maintained for the full hour; it also ends if the target dies or is destroyed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: True Polymorph (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by target type, range, and Concentration; persistence requires sustaining the full duration.

rules.statement: When changing one creature into another, the new creature’s Challenge Rating can’t exceed the target’s CR or level; it uses the new form’s statistics but retains its Hit Points, Hit Point Dice, alignment, and personality, and gains temporary Hit Points equal to the new form’s Hit Points. It is restricted by its anatomy, cannot speak or cast spells, and cannot use or benefit from gear that melds into the form.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: True Polymorph—Creature into Creature (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by the target’s CR or level; form power is capped and gear and speech or spellcasting are unavailable.

rules.statement: An object can become a creature no larger than itself and with CR 9 or lower; the creature is friendly to you and your allies, acts immediately after you in combat, and obeys your commands. After the spell has lasted more than an hour, you lose control, though it might remain friendly depending on its treatment.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: True Polymorph—Object into Creature (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by object size and CR 9 limit; command ends after an hour, with subsequent attitude depending on treatment.

rules.statement: Turning a creature into an object also transforms its worn and carried belongings if the object is no larger than the creature; the creature takes the object’s statistics and remembers none of the time spent transformed once restored.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: True Polymorph—Creature into Object (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by the size limit; transformation suppresses creature statistics and erases memory of the interval.

rules.statement: True Resurrection revives a creature dead for no more than 200 years, unless it died of old age, restoring all Hit Points. It closes wounds, neutralizes poison, cures magical contagions, lifts curses present at death, restores missing or damaged limbs and organs, and returns an Undead creature to its non-Undead form; if the original body is gone, it can create a new one when the caster speaks the creature’s name, at a chosen unoccupied spot within 10 feet.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: True Resurrection (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by the 200-year and old-age limits; a 25,000+ GP diamond is consumed and casting takes an hour.

rules.statement: True Seeing gives a willing touched creature Truesight out to 120 feet for 1 hour; the spell consumes mushroom powder worth at least 25 GP.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: True Seeing (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by 120-foot range and 1-hour duration; the target must consent and the material is consumed.

rules.statement: Wish can duplicate any spell of level 8 or lower without requiring its normal casting requirements or costly components. Alternatively, it can create a nonmagical object worth up to 25,000 GP and no more than 300 feet in any dimension; restore all Hit Points and end Greater Restoration-type effects on you and up to 20 visible creatures; grant up to 10 visible creatures permanent Resistance to one chosen damage type or immunity to one spell or magical effect for 8 hours; replace one eligible feat; or force a reroll of any die roll from the last round, choosing whether to use the reroll or original and whether the reroll has Advantage or Disadvantage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wish (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by the listed targets, limits, and durations; broad options have powerful and potentially lasting effects.

rules.statement: A Wish that seeks another outcome is adjudicated by the GM and may fail, work only partly, or cause unintended consequences; large-scale wishes can attract powerful foes, divine agents may intervene over effects on a god, and a wish to undo the multiverse fails. Using any Wish effect other than spell duplication causes unavoidable Necrotic damage of 1d10 per level whenever you cast a spell before your next Long Rest, reduces Strength to 3 for 2d4 days (with each full day resting and doing only light activity reducing recovery time by 2 days), and carries a 33% chance of permanently losing the ability to cast Wish.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wish—Reshape Reality and stress (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial; default the scope and consequences to the GM; reality alteration exacts severe bodily costs and may permanently remove access to the spell.

rules.statement: Word of Recall teleports you and up to five willing creatures within 5 feet to the nearest unoccupied space at a previously designated sanctuary; without first designating a sanctuary by casting the spell there, it has no effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Word of Recall (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by the prepared destination and six-creature limit; travel requires a sanctuary established in advance.

rules.statement: A creature can be attuned to at most three magic items at once; the glossary identifies attunement as a bond required by some items before their magical properties can be used.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Attunement (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial at three simultaneous bonds; some item powers remain unavailable without forming the bond.

rules.statement: Concentration ends if its creator starts another Concentration effect, becomes Incapacitated, or dies. After taking damage, the creator must make a Constitution save with DC 10 or half the damage (rounded down), whichever is higher, capped at 30; the creator may end Concentration at any time without an action.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Concentration (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by the damage-based save DC; maintaining an effect competes with other Concentration effects and is disrupted by incapacitation or death.

rules.statement: A creature under Restrained can try to escape sticky webs with an action, succeeding on a Strength (Athletics) check against the caster’s spell save DC. The web spell can impose Restrained when a creature first enters the webs on a turn or starts its turn there after a failed Dexterity save; the condition lasts while it remains in the webs or until it breaks free.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Web (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by the spell save DC and web placement; escape costs an action and requires a successful check.

rules.statement: A creature in Zone of Truth that enters its area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a Charisma save; on failure it cannot deliberately lie within the area, and the caster knows whether it passed. The affected creature knows of the effect and may stay silent or answer evasively, but not falsely.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Zone of Truth (dnd-srd-5.2.1#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial by the 15-foot radius and 10-minute duration; a failed save blocks deliberate lies but does not compel answers.

rules.statement: A dead creature has 0 Hit Points and cannot regain them until magic revives it; its departed spirit knows who is attempting the revival and may refuse. On return, it has the Hit Points specified by the revival effect, retains still-active conditions, magical contagions, and curses, loses one Exhaustion level if it had any, and loses all item attunements.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial revival availability; the spirit has agency and may refuse to return.

rules.statement: Exhaustion accumulates one level at a time; at level 6 the creature dies. Each level subtracts 2 from D20 Test rolls and 5 feet from Speed; finishing a Long Rest removes one level, and the condition ends at level 0.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Exhaustion, p. 181 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the rate of accumulating Exhaustion; repeated hardship progressively reduces capability.

rules.statement: A creature with 0 Hit Points that starts its turn must make a Death Saving Throw. The passage points to the damage-and-healing rules for the procedure, without specifying its resolution here.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Death Saving Throw, p. 181 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial specified; the detailed check procedure is outside this passage.

rules.statement: To escape a grapple, the grappled creature can use its action to succeed on a Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against the grapple’s escape DC. The grapple also ends if the grappler is Incapacitated, the target moves beyond the grapple’s range, or the grappler releases it, which takes no action.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Grappling, p. 182 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the escape DC and grapple range; restraint persists until escape, separation, incapacitation, or release.

rules.statement: To hide, a creature must be Heavily Obscured or behind Three-Quarters or Total Cover, out of every enemy’s line of sight, and succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) check. Success grants the Invisible condition while hidden; the check total sets the DC to find it, and loud noise, discovery, an attack roll, or casting a spell with a Verbal component ends hiding.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the Stealth DC; concealment depends on cover, line of sight, and avoiding revealing actions.

rules.statement: An Incapacitated creature cannot take actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions; it loses Concentration, cannot speak, and has Disadvantage on an Initiative roll made while in this state.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Incapacitated, p. 184 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial specified; the condition disables actions, speech, and Concentration.

rules.statement: A spell with a casting time of 1 minute or longer requires the caster to take the Magic action on every turn of its casting and maintain Concentration. If Concentration breaks, the spell fails without expending a spell slot.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magic, p. 185 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial specified; lengthy casting requires sustained action and focus, but failure preserves the slot.

rules.statement: A prepared spell with the Ritual tag can be cast as a Ritual, taking 10 minutes longer than normal and expending no spell slot; this version cannot be cast at a higher level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ritual, p. 187 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial specified; the caster trades extra time for avoiding slot expenditure and cannot increase the spell’s level.

rules.statement: A creature can teleport instantly without crossing intervening space; this uses no movement unless the effect says otherwise and never provokes Opportunity Attacks. Carried and worn equipment goes with it, but a touched creature does not unless specified; an occupied or blocked destination instead places the teleporter in the nearest unoccupied space of its choice.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Teleportation, p. 190 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial destination visibility or other limits in the specific effect; teleportation bypasses intervening space but does not automatically transport companions.

rules.statement: A creature can spend its action to grapple using an Unarmed Strike if it has a free hand and the target is no more than one size larger. The target chooses a Strength or Dexterity saving throw against DC 8 plus the grappler’s Strength modifier and Proficiency Bonus; failure gives it the Grappled condition.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Unarmed Strike, p. 190 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the save DC through the grappler’s attributes and proficiency; grappling requires a free hand and a size limit.

rules.statement: An effect that allows shape-shifting specifies what happens during the change; unless it says otherwise, ongoing conditions, spells, curses, and similar effects carry over between forms. The creature returns to its true form if it dies.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Shape-Shifting, p. 187 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial exceptions in the individual effect; changing form does not ordinarily clear ongoing effects.

rules.statement: A creature with Truesight, within its specified range, can see in normal and magical Darkness, perceive Invisible creatures and objects, see visual illusions as transparent and automatically succeed on saves against them, recognize magically transformed true forms, and see into the Ethereal Plane.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Truesight, p. 190 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the sense’s range; its benefits are limited to that range.

rules.statement: After 8 hours of travel in a day, each additional hour requires a Constitution saving throw; the DC is 10 plus the number of hours already traveled beyond 8, and failure adds 1 Exhaustion level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Extended Travel, p. 193 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: extra travel risks exhaustion; dial: none; the rising DC makes continued exertion increasingly costly.

rules.statement: For sustained special movement, hourly travel distance in miles is Speed divided by 10; multiply the resulting daily distance by 1⅓ for Fast pace or ⅔ for Slow pace, rounding down. Flying or movement that ignores Difficult Terrain permits Fast pace regardless of terrain.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Special Movement, p. 193 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: convert unusual movement to travel distance; dial: none; pace still trades speed against terrain limits.

rules.statement: A creature that becomes the target of demonic possession must succeed on a DC 15 Charisma save or be possessed; rolling a 1 on a D20 Test lets the entity control its behavior. At the end of each later turn, a successful DC 15 Charisma save restores control; a successful DC 15 save after a Long Rest, Dispel Evil and Good, or curse-removing magic ends the possession.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Environmental Curses: Demonic Possession, p. 193 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: possession persists until a specified save or magic ends it; dial: the GM decides whether curse-removal magic applies to other cursed origins.

rules.statement: A creature recuperating from a magical contagion for 3 days, while doing nothing that interrupts a Long Rest, makes a DC 15 Constitution save; success grants Advantage on saves against that contagion for 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magical Contagions: Rest and Recuperation, p. 194 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: recuperation improves resistance rather than curing the infection; dial: none; three days of uninterrupted rest are required.

rules.statement: Cackle Fever affects Humanoids other than gnomes after 1d4 days: it causes 1 Exhaustion level, and while that level remains, taking non-Psychic damage can trigger a DC 13 Constitution save or 1d10 Psychic damage and Incapacitation. At each Long Rest’s end, a DC 13 Constitution save counts toward ending the contagion; three successes end it and grant immunity for 1 year, while nearby Humanoids can catch it from a 10-foot Emanation on a failed DC 10 Constitution save.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magical Contagions: Cackle Fever, p. 194 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: infection has delayed symptoms, a repeated cure check, and a contagious radius; dial: none; proximity exposes others to infection.

rules.statement: In extreme cold at or below 0°F, an exposed creature makes a DC 10 Constitution save at each hour’s end or gains 1 Exhaustion level; Cold Resistance or Immunity guarantees success. In extreme heat at or above 100°F, a creature without drinkable water saves hourly against a DC starting at 5 and rising by 1 each hour; Medium or Heavy armor imposes Disadvantage, while Fire Resistance or Immunity guarantees success.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Environmental Effects: Extreme Cold and Extreme Heat, p. 195 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: exposure accumulates exhaustion; dial: none; cold protection, water, and armor modify the risk.

rules.statement: A supernatural fear effect typically calls for a Wisdom save against a DC set by its severity; a Frightened creature usually repeats the save at the end of each turn and ends the effect on a success. The GM may add further behavior or combat restrictions while the condition lasts.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fear and Mental Stress: Fear Effects, p. 196 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: fear can be resisted repeatedly; dial: the GM chooses the DC and any additional effects to match the threat.

rules.statement: A contact poison affects a creature when it touches the substance with exposed skin; an ingested poison requires swallowing a full dose, though a partial dose may have a reduced effect. Inhaled poison affects creatures in a 5-foot Cube and dissipates immediately, while injury poison can be applied as a Bonus Action and exposes a creature that takes Piercing or Slashing damage from the coated object.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Poison, p. 197 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: delivery method determines exposure; dial: the GM may reduce a partial ingested dose, with weaker damage or Advantage on its save.

rules.statement: A character can spend 1d6 minutes trying to harvest poison from a dead or Incapacitated venomous creature, then make a DC 20 Intelligence (Nature) check using a Poisoner’s Kit. Success yields one dose; failure yields none, and failing by 5 or more also exposes the character to the creature’s poison.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Poison: Harvesting Poison, p. 197 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: harvesting takes time and risks exposure; dial: none; one creature yields at most one dose.

rules.statement: A trap’s trigger activates its effect, whose duration determines whether it ends immediately, persists, or resets; unless it specifies a reset, the trap is inert after activation. Detection and disarming depend on the individual trap’s stated actions, checks, and methods.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Traps: Parts of a Trap, p. 199 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each trap resolves through its specified trigger and duration; dial: construction and disarming methods vary by trap.

rules.statement: A creature caught by a falling net fails a DC 10 Dexterity save and becomes Restrained, unless it is Huge or larger, which succeeds automatically. A creature can use an action and succeed on a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check to free itself or a nearby creature; reducing the net to 0 Hit Points also frees those trapped.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Example Traps: Falling Net, p. 199 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the net restrains until a check or damage frees the target; dial: none; escape costs an action or requires destroying the net.

rules.statement: Drinking a potion or administering it to another creature takes a Bonus Action; the potion takes effect immediately and is consumed. Applying an oil can take longer if its description says so.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magic Items: Potions, p. 204 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: potion use is quick and consumes the item; dial: an oil’s application time is set by its description.

rules.statement: When two potions are mixed, roll d100: 1 makes both ineffective and causes a 5-foot-radius blast dealing 4d10 Force damage; 2–8 makes both ineffective and turns the mixture into a chosen ingested poison; 9–15 makes both ineffective; 16–25 removes one potion’s effect; 26–35 halves both potions’ numerical effects and durations, or removes an effect with neither; 36–90 leaves both working normally; 91–99 doubles one potion’s numerical effects and duration, or leaves both unchanged if neither can be doubled; and 00 leaves one potion working permanently. For more than two potions, roll again for each added potion, combining results; effects not immediately apparent are revealed when they become evident.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion Miscibility (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a d100 roll for each mixture; dial the outcomes or permanence down if unpredictable mixtures would overwhelm the campaign, since the cost is losing, distorting, or dangerously changing potion effects.

rules.statement: A creature can attune to an item with a class prerequisite only if it belongs to that class; a spellcaster prerequisite is met by being able to cast at least one spell through the creature’s own traits or features, not through a magic item. A curse on an item usually prevents voluntary ending of attunement until the curse is broken.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magic Item Rules; Cursed Items (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these eligibility and curse restrictions; dial them if access to magical gear should be easier, because class access and curse-breaking otherwise limit who can use or leave an item.

rules.statement: A creature that understands a written language can try to activate a scroll by reading it, unless the scroll says otherwise; after its magic is invoked, it is spent and its writing fades or the scroll crumbles. Activating an item usually takes a Magic action, but its description can require an additional specific act.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Scrolls; Activating a Magic Item (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a readable, single-use scroll and the usual Magic action; dial access or action cost to fit the item, since use consumes the stored magic.

rules.statement: A spell cast from a magic item uses the lowest possible spell and caster level, expends no user spell slot, and requires no components unless the item says otherwise; it keeps the spell’s normal casting time, range, and duration, and requires the user’s Concentration when applicable. If the item requires the user’s spellcasting ability and the user has none, use a +0 ability modifier and the user’s Proficiency Bonus.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spells Cast from Items (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the spell’s normal operation with item-supplied casting and no slot cost; dial exceptions in the item description, since the item supplies power but may still demand concentration or a user ability.

rules.statement: An item with charges spends them when its properties require it; Identify reveals its remaining charges, and an attuned creature knows both the remaining charges and how many the item regains. If an item recharges at an event that does not occur on its current world or plane, the GM decides when it recharges.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Charges; “The Next Dawn” (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the item’s stated recharge event; dial recharge timing when the setting lacks that event, since the power supply otherwise has no reliable reset.

rules.statement: A magic item’s curse is generally hidden from identification methods, including Identify; attuning to a cursed item cannot be voluntarily ended until the curse is broken, for example by Remove Curse. An item description can specify a different way to reveal or remove its curse.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cursed Items (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concealed curses and binding attunement until the curse is broken; dial either restriction if involuntary item attachment is undesirable, because removal otherwise does not free the wearer.

rules.statement: Creating a magic item requires the crafter and assistants to have Arcana proficiency, the appropriate proficient tool, and all spells the item can cast prepared on every crafting day. Crafting takes 5, 10, 50, 125, or 250 days and costs 50, 200, 2,000, 20,000, or 100,000 GP for common through legendary rarity respectively; for consumables other than Spell Scrolls, halve the time and cost, and add the cost of any underlying nonmagical item.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Crafting Magic Items; Time and Cost (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed proficiency, preparation, time, and material costs; dial the requirements to the campaign’s crafting economy, because item creation consumes skilled labor and scarce materials.

rules.statement: If a bearer acts against a sentient item’s alignment or purpose, the bearer makes a Charisma save against DC 12 plus the item’s Charisma modifier; on failure, the item can demand that the bearer pursue its goals, discard something it dislikes, give it away, or keep it close. If the bearer refuses, the item can prevent attunement, suppress activated properties, or attempt control; a failed further save against the same DC gives the bearer Charmed for 1d12 hours, requiring attempts to obey the item, with a new save when the bearer takes damage, and the control attempt cannot recur until the next dawn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Conflict (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the Charisma checks and the item’s limited control attempt; dial the demands or control severity if sentient items should be less coercive, since disobedience risks lost powers and compelled behavior.

rules.statement: A creature wearing an Amulet of the Planes can use a Magic action to name a familiar location on another plane and make a DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check; success casts Plane Shift. On failure, the user and each creature and object within 15 feet travel to a random destination, with d100 results selecting the named plane on 1–60, an Inner Plane on 61–70, a listed Outer Plane on 71–90, or the Astral Plane on 91–00.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Amulet of the Planes (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a check that risks misrouting the whole nearby group; dial the failure table or check difficulty, because planar travel can strand travelers far from their intended destination.

rules.statement: Putting a Bag of Holding inside an extradimensional space made by a Handy Haversack, Portable Hole, or similar item destroys both and opens a one-way gate to a random Astral Plane location; creatures within 10 feet are pulled through, and the gate then closes. If a Bag of Holding is overloaded, pierced, or torn, it is destroyed and its contents are scattered in the Astral Plane.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Bag of Holding (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the destructive interaction and one-way displacement; dial the danger if extradimensional storage should be safer, since combining or damaging these containers can lose cargo and transport nearby creatures.

rules.statement: A Bag of Holding has an interior about 2 feet square and 4 feet deep, holds up to 500 pounds within 64 cubic feet, and weighs 5 pounds regardless of contents; retrieving an object takes a Utilize action. It contains enough air for 10 minutes divided by the number of breathing creatures inside, and turning it inside out spills its contents unharmed but prevents use until it is restored.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Bag of Holding (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the fixed weight, capacity, retrieval action, and finite air; dial capacity or air if the campaign needs different storage logistics, because the container is not unlimited or safe for prolonged habitation.

rules.statement: When lit, a Candle of Invocation lasts up to 4 hours, can be snuffed and relit with unused time tracked in 1-minute increments, and grants Advantage on D20 Tests to creatures in its 30-foot Dim Light; Clerics and Druids there can cast prepared level 1 spells without spending spell slots. On its first lighting, the user can instead cast Gate, destroying the candle and linking the portal to an Outer Plane chosen by the GM or determined from its table.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Candle of Invocation (dnd-srd-5.2.1#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the four-hour burn and the choice between ongoing benefits and a one-use Gate; dial the benefits or destination, since opening the portal consumes the candle.

rules.statement: While worn, this silk garment grants resistance to poison damage, a climbing speed equal to the wearer’s speed with hands free, and the ability to move through webs as difficult terrain without being caught in them. It also allows casting Web with save DC 13 at twice its normal area, usable again at the next dawn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cloak of Arachnida (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: these benefits are available only while worn, and the spell-like property recharges at dawn.

rules.statement: While worn, the cloak projects an illusion that gives attackers disadvantage on attack rolls against the wearer. The illusion stops working until the start of the wearer’s next turn after the wearer takes damage, and it is suppressed while the wearer’s Speed is 0.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cloak of Displacement (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: damage briefly breaks the protection, and immobility suppresses it.

rules.statement: While worn, the cloak gives disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks to notice the wearer and advantage on the wearer’s Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cloak of Elvenkind (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the benefits require wearing the cloak.

rules.statement: The cloak has 3 charges and regains 1d3 charges daily at dawn. While wearing it, the user can take a Magic action and spend 1 charge to become Invisible for 1 hour; the effect ends early if the hood is lowered or the cloak is removed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cloak of Invisibility (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: invisibility costs a charge and ends when the garment is no longer used to cover the wearer.

rules.statement: While worn, the cloak gives a +1 bonus to Armor Class and saving throws.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cloak of Protection (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the bonuses apply only while wearing the cloak.

rules.statement: In Dim Light or Darkness, the worn cloak grants a 40-foot Fly Speed while the wearer grips its edges; losing grip or leaving those lighting conditions removes that speed. Once per day, the wearer can cast Polymorph on themself to become a bat, retaining Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cloak of the Bat (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: flight depends on darkness and grip, and transformation is limited to once before dawn.

rules.statement: The cube has 3 charges and regains 1d3 daily at dawn. As a Magic action, spending 1 charge casts Gate by pressing a face to open a portal to its keyed plane, or casts Plane Shift by pressing a face twice to transport the targets to that plane; one face is keyed to the Material Plane and the others are set by the GM.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cubic Gate (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: planar passage consumes a charge, and destinations are limited to the cube’s keyed planes.

rules.statement: A poisoned blade can be prepared with a Bonus Action; the poison lasts 1 minute or until an attack hits. A hit creature must make a DC 15 Constitution save or take 2d10 Poison damage and have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute; this property recharges at dawn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dagger of Venom (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the poison is a limited-use coating, with a saving throw and dawn recharge.

rules.statement: The shackles can be placed with a Utilize action on an Incapacitated creature of Small to Large size, preventing extradimensional movement such as teleportation and planar travel, but not passage through an interdimensional portal. The user and designated creatures can remove them with a Utilize action; once every 30 days, the captive can attempt a DC 30 Strength (Athletics) check to break them.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dimensional Shackles (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: travel is blocked while bound, but portals remain an escape route and a rare, difficult check can destroy the restraint.

rules.statement: When the attuned user peers into the orb with a Magic action, a DC 15 Charisma save determines whether they control it while attuned or become Charmed by it while attuned. A Charmed user cannot voluntarily end attunement, and the orb can cast Suggestion at will to urge its own aims.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dragon Orb (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; control is tested on use, while failure creates a persistent charm that prevents voluntary separation and subjects the user to the orb’s influence.

rules.statement: When the orb’s user controls it, spending a Magic action sends a telepathic call across 40 miles that compels chromatic dragons to approach by the most direct route; dragon deities are unaffected, and the call cannot be used again for 1 hour. The called dragons may be Hostile because they were compelled.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dragon Orb, Call Dragons (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the call has a 40-mile limit, a one-hour reuse delay, and may provoke hostility.

rules.statement: Using the bottle for the first time triggers a d10 outcome: on 1, the efreeti attacks for 5 rounds, then vanishes and the bottle loses its magic; on 2–9, it obeys for 1 hour, with the same result on the next two openings, then escapes and the bottle is emptied on the fourth opening. On 10, it grants one Wish and vanishes, or disappears after 1 hour, consuming the bottle’s magic.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Efreeti Bottle (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; the bottle’s uncertain outcome may provide a brief servant or a Wish, but can instead produce an attack or consume the item.

rules.statement: Breaking an elemental gem consumes it and summons the elemental type determined by the gem; it appears nearby, understands the user’s languages, obeys commands, and acts immediately after the user in initiative. It vanishes after 1 hour, at 0 Hit Points, or when dismissed as a Bonus Action.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Elemental Gem (dnd-srd-5.2.1#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial: the gem is consumed to summon a temporary obedient creature, which can be dismissed or defeated.

rules.statement: Each use of the horn’s blast has a 20% chance to destroy the horn in an explosion that deals 10d6 Force damage to its user. The blast itself affects a 30-foot Cone: creatures make a DC 15 Constitution save, taking 5d8 Thunder damage and becoming Deafened for 1 minute on a failure, or taking half damage on a success; unattended glass and crystal objects take 10d8 Thunder damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Horn of Blasting (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the blast’s chance of destruction; the unstable horn may injure its user and be lost.

rules.statement: A creature from another plane that you can see within 60 feet must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom save or be trapped in an empty flask; a creature previously trapped by it has Advantage on the save. The flask holds only one creature, which does not age or need air, food, or drink while inside; releasing it gives you command of it for 1 hour, subject to the stated limits on commands, after which its normal disposition and alignment resume.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Iron Flask (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the capture and command durations; the flask’s otherworldly prisoner is contained, then only temporarily compelled.

rules.statement: An activated mirror can trap a creature other than its owner that sees its reflection within 30 feet if it fails a DC 15 Charisma save; Constructs succeed automatically, and a creature aware of the mirror’s nature has Advantage. Its twelve cells are extradimensional, and a trapped creature can escape by planar-travel magic or be freed by a command; if all cells are occupied, a new capture releases one prisoner at random.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mirror of Life Trapping (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the number of cells and escape routes; capture risks confinement until magic or another release frees the creature.

rules.statement: Opening a Portable Hole against a solid surface creates a 10-foot-deep extradimensional space, not an open passage to another place. Folding it closes the space with its contents inside; a creature trapped there can force its way out with a DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check, and the stored air supports breathing for 1 hour divided by the number of breathing creatures.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Portable Hole (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the air supply and escape check; storage is useful but can strand living occupants.

rules.statement: Putting a Portable Hole inside a Bag of Holding, Handy Haversack, or similar extradimensional space destroys both items and opens a one-way gate to a random Astral Plane location. Creatures within 10 feet that lack Total Cover are pulled through before the gate closes.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Portable Hole (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the destructive interaction; combining spatial containers risks losing the items and involuntary planar displacement.

rules.statement: The Mysterious Deck user declares a draw count before drawing randomly, and each drawn card takes effect immediately; draws must be no more than 1 hour apart. If the declared count is not completed, the remaining cards fly out and resolve at once; drawn cards disappear, except that most return to the deck and may be drawn again.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mysterious Deck (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the declared draw count and deadline; accepting a draw can produce unpredictable benefits or lasting costs.

rules.statement: A deck’s Fates result lets the drawer avoid or erase one event as though it never occurred, usable immediately or any time before the drawer dies. Its Donjon result instead removes the drawer and carried belongings to an extradimensional prison, unlocatable by divination, until someone finds and retrieves them; Wish can reveal the prison’s location.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mysterious Deck: Fates; Donjon (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial whether the result rewrites an event or removes the drawer; fate may erase consequences or impose indefinite imprisonment.

rules.statement: When tossed into the air with a Magic action, an Ioun Stone orbits its user and grants its type’s benefit; no more than three can orbit at once. The Reserve type stores spells totaling up to 4 levels, can accept a level 1–4 spell from any creature touching it as the spell is cast, and lets its wearer cast a stored spell using the original caster’s spell statistics; casting removes that spell from storage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ioun Stone (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the three-stone and four-spell-level limits; stored casting is finite and consumes the stored spell.

rules.statement: An Absorption or Greater Absorption stone can use its wearer’s Reaction to cancel a spell the wearer can see being cast, up to level 4 or level 8 respectively; the spell has no effect and its casting resources are wasted. Either stone loses its magic after cancelling a total of 20 spell levels.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ioun Stone: Absorption; Greater Absorption (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the spell-level ceiling and 20-level capacity; spell cancellation is powerful but exhausts the stone.

rules.statement: A creature within 5 feet can use an action to try to break bands restraining a creature with a DC 20 Strength (Athletics) check; success destroys the bands and frees the prisoner. After one use, the bands cannot be used again until the next dawn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Iron Bands (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the escape check and daily reuse limit; restraint can be resisted, but the device’s power is temporarily spent.

rules.statement: The immovable rod fixes itself in place when its button is pressed with a Utilize action and stays fixed until a creature presses the button again that way; it can hold up to 8,000 pounds. Excess weight deactivates it, while moving it while fixed requires a DC 30 Strength (Athletics) check and can shift it up to 10 feet on success.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Immovable Rod (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the weight limit and difficult check; anchoring is reliable only within the rod’s load capacity.

rules.statement: Four attached horseshoes let a horse or similar creature float 4 inches above surfaces, cross nonsolid or unstable surfaces, leave no tracks, ignore Difficult Terrain, and travel up to 12 hours daily without gaining Exhaustion from extended travel. Each shoe takes a Magic action to attach or remove.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Horseshoes of a Zephyr (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the four-shoe requirement and 12-hour travel limit; the benefit depends on equipping the complete set.

rules.statement: A creature whose soul is taken by the Void card leaves an inert body that does not age or need food, air, or water; its soul is held in an object at a GM-chosen location guarded by powerful beings. Wish cannot restore the soul, though it reveals the object’s location, and the drawer cannot draw further cards.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mysterious Deck: Void (dnd-srd-5.2.1#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the inaccessible soul and its location; the result leaves the body preserved but helpless until the soul is recovered.

rules.statement: Drinking the potion lets you cast the 3rd-level version of Animal Friendship with save DC 13. The drinker can do so once by consuming the potion.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Animal Friendship, p. 235 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a single use consumes the potion; dial: potion availability controls access to the spell.

rules.statement: Drinking the potion grants the effect of Clairvoyance without requiring Concentration. The potion is consumed to gain that effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Clairvoyance, p. 235 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the potion is consumed; dial: remove or restore the no-Concentration benefit to tune its reliability.

rules.statement: For 1 hour after drinking, the drinker has a Climb Speed equal to their Speed and Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to climb.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Climbing, p. 235 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the consumed potion grants a temporary movement mode; dial: the one-hour duration sets its cost window.

rules.statement: Drinking grants the reduce effect of Enlarge/Reduce for 1d4 hours without Concentration. The potion is consumed when used.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Diminution, p. 235 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: consumption grants a variable-duration transformation; dial: the 1d4-hour duration makes its endpoint uncertain.

rules.statement: For 1 hour after drinking, the drinker has a Fly Speed equal to their Speed and can hover. If the potion expires while the drinker is airborne, they fall unless another effect keeps them aloft.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Flying, p. 235 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the potion is consumed; dial: flight ends after an hour and can impose a fall.

rules.statement: Drinking grants Gaseous Form’s effect for 1 hour without Concentration, and the drinker can end it early with a Bonus Action. The potion is consumed when drunk.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Gaseous Form, p. 235 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: consumption produces a temporary form change; dial: the drinker controls early termination.

rules.statement: For 1 hour after drinking, the drinker’s Strength becomes the value set by the potion’s giant type: hill 21, frost or stone 23, fire 25, cloud 27, or storm 29. The potion has no effect if the drinker’s Strength already meets or exceeds that value.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Giant Strength, p. 235 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a consumed potion sets a time-limited score; dial: its threshold prevents benefit to already-strong drinkers.

rules.statement: Drinking grants the enlarge effect of Enlarge/Reduce for 10 minutes without Concentration. The potion is consumed when used.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Growth, p. 235 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: consumption grants a fixed-duration transformation; dial: the short duration limits the benefit.

rules.statement: A healing potion restores Hit Points when drunk: common restores 2d4 + 2, uncommon 4d4 + 4, rare 8d4 + 8, and very rare 10d4 + 20. Drinking consumes the potion.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potions of Healing, p. 236 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a consumed item restores a rarity-scaled amount; dial: rarity controls the recovery range.

rules.statement: Drinking grants 10 Temporary Hit Points for 1 hour and the effect of Bless for that duration without Concentration. The potion is consumed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Heroism, p. 236 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one consumed potion grants temporary durability and a timed spell effect; dial: both expire after an hour.

rules.statement: Drinking grants the Invisible condition for 1 hour; it ends early if the drinker makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell. The potion is consumed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Invisibility, p. 236 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the potion is consumed; dial: specified actions end invisibility before the hour elapses.

rules.statement: For 1 minute after drinking, the drinker has Resistance to all damage. The potion is consumed to gain the protection.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Invulnerability, p. 236 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use grants brief broad damage mitigation; dial: the one-minute duration caps the protection.

rules.statement: Drinking reduces the drinker’s physical age by 1d6 + 6 years, but not below 13. On each later use, a cumulative 10% chance per use causes the same number of years to be added instead; each use consumes the potion.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Longevity, p. 236 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the potion changes age; dial: repeated use raises a cumulative risk of aging rather than rejuvenation.

rules.statement: For 10 minutes after drinking, the drinker gains Detect Thoughts’ effect with save DC 13 and no Concentration. The potion is consumed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Mind Reading, p. 236 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: consuming the item grants temporary thought-sensing; dial: the 10-minute duration bounds exposure.

rules.statement: The potion appears to be a beneficial potion but is actually poison disguised by illusion; Identify reveals what it is. A drinker takes 4d6 Poison damage and must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution save or have the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Poison, p. 236 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: drinking triggers damage and a save-gated condition; dial: concealment creates risk, while identification can expose it.

rules.statement: Drinking grants Resistance to one damage type for 1 hour; the GM chooses the type or rolls 1d10: acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic, radiant, or thunder.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Resistance, p. 236 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: consumption grants one hour of resistance; dial: the randomly or GM-selected damage type determines its usefulness.

rules.statement: Drinking grants Haste’s effect for 1 minute without Concentration and without the lethargy normally suffered when that effect ends. The potion is consumed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Speed, p. 236 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the potion grants a brief spell effect; dial: omitting the usual aftermath makes it more favorable.

rules.statement: Drinking removes all the drinker’s Exhaustion levels and ends the Poisoned condition. For the next 24 hours, any Hit Point Die the drinker spends restores the maximum possible Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Vitality, pp. 236–237 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one consumed item clears specified harmful states and improves recovery for a day.

rules.statement: After drinking, the drinker can breathe underwater for 24 hours. The potion is consumed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Potion of Water Breathing, p. 236 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the potion grants a time-limited bodily capability; dial: it expires after 24 hours.

rules.statement: While holding the attuned quarterstaff, you gain +2 to its attack and damage rolls, can toggle 10-foot Dim Light, and can use a Bonus Action to change it into a 6-inch rod, a 10-foot pole, or a quarterstaff, limited by available space. In quarterstaff or pole form it grants Advantage on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks; in quarterstaff form, once per Short or Long Rest, a Reaction can add +5 AC against a triggering hit, and a thrown attack at 30/120 feet returns immediately to your hand.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Quarterstaff of the Acrobat, p. 237 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement and holding gate its benefits; dial: form and space limit which properties can be used.

rules.statement: The Ring of Animal Influence has 3 charges and regains 1d3 at dawn. While wearing it, expend 1 charge to cast Animal Friendship, Fear affecting only Beasts, or Speak with Animals, each with save DC 13.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Animal Influence, p. 237 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charges limit daily spell use; dial: the partial recharge sets its sustainable use rate.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned ring, you can use a Magic action to summon its particular Djinni into a chosen unoccupied space within 120 feet. It is Friendly to you and your allies and obeys commands; it remains while you Concentrate, up to 1 hour, or until it reaches 0 Hit Points, then cannot be summoned for 24 hours, and the ring becomes nonmagical if it dies.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Djinni Summoning, p. 237 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement enables a controlled summon; dial: Concentration, duration, recovery delay, and the ring’s destruction on the djinni’s death constrain it.

rules.statement: The attuned elemental ring gives Advantage on attacks against Elementals and imposes Disadvantage on their attacks against you. It can also use a Magic action to make a visible Elemental within 60 feet save against DC 18 Wisdom; on failure it is Charmed until your next turn begins, and you choose its move and action on its next turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Elemental Command, p. 237 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: wearing and attunement gate protection and a control attempt; dial: the command lasts only briefly and allows a save.

rules.statement: The ring’s linked plane grants additional benefits: air gives Auran, Lightning Resistance, and hovering flight; earth gives Terran, Acid Resistance, ignores rubble, rock, and dirt as Difficult Terrain, and permits passage through solid earth or rock as Difficult Terrain, but ending a turn there shunts you to the nearest unoccupied space last occupied. Fire gives Ignan and Fire immunity; water gives Aquan, a 60-foot Swim Speed, and underwater breathing.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Elemental Command, pp. 237–238 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement to the plane-linked ring grants specific elemental traits; dial: the earth passage is limited by movement and forces relocation at turn end.

rules.statement: The attuned elemental ring has 5 charges, recovering 1d4 + 1 at dawn, and casts spells from its linked-plane list at save DC 18 for the listed charge costs. The choices are air: Chain Lightning (3), Feather Fall (0), Gust of Wind (2), Wind Wall (1); earth: Earthquake (5), Stone Shape (2), Stoneskin (3), Wall of Stone (3); fire: Burning Hands (1), Fireball (2), Fire Storm (4), Wall of Fire (3); water: Create or Destroy Water (1), Ice Storm (2), Tsunami (5), Wall of Ice (3), Water Walk (2).
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Elemental Command, pp. 237–238 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charges and linked plane restrict spell access; dial: dawn recharge and spell costs govern frequency.

rules.statement: The attuned Ring of Evasion has 3 charges and regains 1d3 at dawn; when you fail a Dexterity saving throw while wearing it, you can use a Reaction and expend 1 charge to succeed instead.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Evasion, p. 238 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a charge converts a failed save to success; dial: the charge pool limits uses.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Ring of Feather Falling, you descend 60 feet per round while falling and take no damage from the fall.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Feather Falling, p. 238 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: wearing the ring changes falling speed and removes fall damage.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Ring of Free Action, Difficult Terrain costs no extra movement, and magic cannot reduce your Speeds or give you the Paralyzed or Restrained condition.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Free Action, p. 238 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: wearing the ring blocks specified magical movement and condition effects.

rules.statement: The attuned Ring of Invisibility lets you use a Magic action to become Invisible; the effect lasts until the ring is removed or you use a Bonus Action to become visible.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Invisibility, p. 238 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement grants repeatable invisibility; removing the ring or choosing to end it terminates the effect.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Ring of Mind Shielding, you are immune to magic that reads thoughts, detects lies, or reveals alignment or creature type, and telepathy reaches you only with your permission. You can make the ring imperceptible with a Magic action; it remains so until another Magic action restores it, removal, or your death.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Mind Shielding, p. 238 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement blocks specified mental detection; dial: telepathic access is under the wearer’s control.

rules.statement: If a wearer of the Ring of Mind Shielding dies while wearing it and it has no soul already, the wearer’s soul enters the ring; the soul may remain or depart for the afterlife. While inside, it can telepathically communicate with any wearer, who cannot block that communication.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Mind Shielding, p. 238 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death can transfer the wearer’s soul into the ring; dial: the soul may depart, but communication with a wearer cannot be refused.

rules.statement: The attuned Ring of Protection grants +1 AC and +1 to saving throws while worn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Protection, p. 238 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement grants a constant small defensive bonus while worn.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Ring of Regeneration and at least 1 Hit Point, you regain 1d6 Hit Points every 10 minutes. A lost body part regrows to full function after 1d6 + 1 days if you stay at 1 Hit Point or more throughout.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Regeneration, p. 238 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: regeneration requires wearing the ring and staying alive; dial: lost parts take days to regrow.

rules.statement: While wearing the unattuned Ring of Resistance, you have Resistance to the damage type indicated by its gemstone, chosen by the GM or determined by 1d10. The table pairs the results with acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, necrotic, poison, psychic, radiant, or thunder.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Resistance, p. 238 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the gemstone sets a single resistance; dial: its type is chosen or random.

rules.statement: The attuned Ring of Shooting Stars lets you cast Dancing Lights or Light. It has 6 charges, regaining 1d6 at dawn; 1 charge casts Faerie Fire, 2 create up to four lightning spheres, and 1–3 launch radiant motes that each affect a 15-foot Cube with a DC 15 Dexterity save, dealing 5d4 Radiant damage or half on success.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Shooting Stars, pp. 238–239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charge costs and dawn recovery limit access to the ring’s spells and attacks.

rules.statement: The lightning spheres last while you Concentrate, up to 1 minute, shed Dim Light within 30 feet, and can each be moved up to 30 feet as a Bonus Action, no farther than 120 feet from you. The first time a sphere comes within 5 feet of a creature other than you without Total Cover, it discharges and vanishes; the creature makes a DC 15 Dexterity save, taking lightning damage based on the number created, or half on success: 1 sphere 4d12, 2 spheres 5d4, 3 spheres 2d6, or 4 spheres 2d4.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Shooting Stars, p. 239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spheres require Concentration and disappear at a trigger; dial: sphere count changes the damage.

rules.statement: The attuned Ring of Spell Storing holds up to 5 spell levels and is found with 1d6 − 1 levels of spells chosen by the GM. Any creature can touch it while casting a level 1–5 spell to store that spell; if there is insufficient capacity, the spell is expended without effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Spell Storing, p. 239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: storage capacity limits spells; an overflow attempt consumes the spell without benefit.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Ring of Spell Storing, you can cast a stored spell using the original caster’s slot level, save DC, attack bonus, and spellcasting ability, but it otherwise counts as if you cast it. Casting removes it from storage and frees its capacity.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Spell Storing, p. 239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: releasing a spell empties its stored capacity; dial: its casting statistics remain those of the original caster.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Ring of Spell Turning, you have Advantage on saves against spells; succeeding against a spell of level 7 or lower makes it have no effect on you. If such a spell targeted only you and creates no area, you can use a Reaction to send it back, making its caster save against its own spell using that caster’s save DC.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Spell Turning, p. 239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement protects against spells and can redirect a limited category; dial: the spell-level and target restrictions bound reflection.

rules.statement: While wearing the unattuned Ring of Swimming, you have a Swim Speed of 40 feet.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Swimming, p. 239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: wearing the ring grants a fixed Swim Speed.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Ring of Telekinesis, you can cast Telekinesis from it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Telekinesis, p. 239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement gates access to the spell.

rules.statement: The attuned Ring of the Ram has 3 charges and regains 1d3 at dawn. As a Magic action, spend 1–3 charges to make a +7 ranged spell attack against a visible creature within 60 feet; on a hit each charge deals 2d10 Force damage and pushes it 5 feet, or instead spend the charges to make a +5-per-charge Strength check to break a visible nonmagical object within range that is not worn or carried.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of the Ram, p. 239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charges limit attacks or object-breaking attempts; dial: spending more charges increases damage, push, or check bonus.

rules.statement: The unattuned Ring of Three Wishes has 3 charges, each allowing Wish to be cast; after its last charge is used, the ring becomes nonmagical.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Three Wishes, p. 239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ring grants three uses and is exhausted permanently on the last.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Ring of Warmth, you reduce Cold damage by 2d8 and you and your carried or worn belongings are unharmed by temperatures at or below 0°F.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Warmth, p. 239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: wearing the ring mitigates cold damage and prevents harm from extreme cold.

rules.statement: The unattuned Ring of Water Walking casts Water Walk targeting only its wearer.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of Water Walking, p. 239 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ring’s casting is limited to its wearer.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Ring of X-ray Vision, you can use a Magic action to see through solid objects within 30 feet for 1 minute. The sight penetrates 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or 3 feet of wood or dirt; thicker material or a thin lead sheet blocks it, and each use before a Long Rest requires a DC 15 Constitution save or gives 1 Exhaustion level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ring of X-ray Vision, pp. 239–240 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement enables limited penetration vision; dial: materials block it and repeat use risks Exhaustion.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Robe of Eyes, you have Advantage on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks and Darkvision and Truesight out to 120 feet. Light cast on the robe or Daylight cast within 5 feet blinds you for 1 minute; at the end of each turn you can make a Constitution save (DC 11 for Light, DC 15 for Daylight) to end it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Robe of Eyes, p. 240 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement grants enhanced vision but creates a specific exposure that can blind; repeated saves can end the condition.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Robe of Scintillating Colors, you can spend 1 of its 3 charges, recovering 1d3 at dawn, to display dazzling hues until the end of your next turn. It sheds Bright Light 30 feet and Dim Light another 30; creatures that see you have Disadvantage on attacks, and creatures in the Bright Light that see you must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom save or be Stunned until the effect ends.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Robe of Scintillating Colors, p. 240 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charges limit brief area effects; dial: visibility and a saving throw determine who is impaired or stunned.

rules.statement: The attuned Robe of Stars grants +1 to saving throws. A Magic action removes one of its six stars to cast level-5 Magic Missile; at dusk, 1d6 removed stars reappear.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Robe of Stars, p. 240 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a finite set of stars fuels spellcasting; dial: variable dusk recovery controls replenishment.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Robe of Stars, a Magic action transports you and what you wear and carry to the Astral Plane; another Magic action returns you to your prior plane and space, or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Robe of Stars, p. 240 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement enables travel to and return from the Astral Plane; dial: return placement is limited by occupancy.

rules.statement: A Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard attuned to the Robe of the Archmagi gains base AC 15 plus Dexterity while wearing no armor, Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects, and +2 to spell save DC and spell attack bonus.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Robe of the Archmagi, p. 240 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: class eligibility, attunement, and not wearing armor gate its benefits.

rules.statement: While wearing the Robe of Useful Items, you can use a Magic action to detach a patch and make it become its represented object or creature; after the last patch is removed, the robe is ordinary. It always has two each of a lantern, dagger, mirror, pole, rope, and sack, plus 4d4 GM-selected or randomly determined patches.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Robe of Useful Items, pp. 240–241 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each patch is a one-use conversion and the robe loses its magic when depleted.

rules.statement: The attuned Rod of Absorption can use a Reaction while held to cancel a spell targeting only you that creates no area and store its energy, up to 50 levels over the rod’s existence; an ineligible or over-capacity spell is unaffected. Casting costs for the canceled spell are still spent.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rod of Absorption, p. 241 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the rod cancels only qualifying spells and has a lifetime 50-level absorption cap; the caster still loses spent resources.

rules.statement: An attuned spellcaster holding the Rod of Absorption can convert stored energy into spell slots for spells they know or have prepared. Slots cannot exceed their own highest slot or level 5, and the converted energy is spent in place of slots; a depleted rod that can no longer absorb energy becomes nonmagical.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rod of Absorption, p. 241 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: stored energy substitutes for slots; dial: caster level, level-5 maximum, and finite stored energy limit conversion.

rules.statement: While holding the attuned Rod of Alertness, you have Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and Initiative rolls and can cast Detect Evil and Good, Detect Magic, Detect Poison and Disease, and See Invisibility. Planting it with a Magic action creates a 60-foot Bright Light and 60-foot Dim Light radius; you and allies in the Bright Light gain +1 AC and saves and can locate Invisible creatures there; it ends after 10 minutes or when pulled up, and can be used again only at dawn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rod of Alertness, p. 241 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: holding and planting the rod enable its benefits; dial: the protective field is limited to 10 minutes and recharges at dawn.

rules.statement: The attuned Rod of Lordly Might is a +3 magic Mace. As a Bonus Action, one of six buttons can transform it into a fiery sword dealing an extra 2d6 Fire damage, a +3 battleaxe, a +3 spear, an anchored ladder-pole up to 50 feet that holds 4,000 pounds, a battering ram granting +10 to relevant Athletics checks, or a direction-and-altitude indicator; buttons remain reachable when it becomes a pole, and excess load or failed anchoring reverts it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rod of Lordly Might, pp. 241–242 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement and button choice gate its forms; dial: load and anchoring limits the pole form.

rules.statement: Once per dawn, a hit with the attuned Rod of Lordly Might can force a DC 17 Constitution save; failure deals an extra 4d6 Necrotic damage and restores Hit Points equal to half that damage. Once per dawn, a hit can instead force the same save or Paralyze the target for up to 1 minute, with a save at each turn’s end to end it; a Magic action can also force visible creatures within 30 feet to save against DC 17 Wisdom or become Frightened for up to 1 minute, repeating the save at each turn’s end.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rod of Lordly Might, p. 242 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each special property is once per dawn; saving throws can resist or end the conditions.

rules.statement: The attuned Rod of Resurrection has 5 charges and casts Heal for 1 charge or Resurrection for 5; it regains 1 charge at dawn. After its last charge is spent, a roll of 1 on a d20 makes the rod disappear harmlessly.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rod of Resurrection, p. 242 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell use costs charges and dawn restores one; spending the final charge risks losing the rod.

rules.statement: The attuned Rod of Rulership can use a Magic action to make chosen visible creatures within 120 feet save against DC 15 Wisdom; failure gives Charmed for 8 hours and makes the target regard you as a trusted leader. Harm by you or allies, or a command against its nature, ends the charm; use recharges at dawn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rod of Rulership, p. 242 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the command is save-gated and use is limited to once per dawn; harm or an unnatural command breaks the bond.

rules.statement: The unattuned Rod of Security can use a Magic action to transport you and up to 199 willing visible creatures instantly to a chosen demiplane. It supplies enough food and water, prevents environmental harm, and lets each visitor regain Hit Points as if spending one Hit Point Die per hour without aging; objects from within vanish if taken out.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rod of Security, p. 242 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the rod transports only willing creatures and sustains them in a bounded refuge; dial: its contents cannot be carried out.

rules.statement: Visitors can stay in the demiplane for at most 200 days divided by the number of visitors, rounded down. When time expires or the user ends the effect with a Magic action, everyone returns to their original location or the nearest unoccupied space; the rod cannot be used again for 10 days.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rod of Security, p. 242 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: visitor count shortens the refuge period; a 10-day cooldown limits repeated travel.

rules.statement: The unattuned Rope of Climbing can bear 3,000 pounds and is 60 feet long. While holding one end, a Magic action commands the other to move 10 feet on the turn and 10 feet at the start of each later turn toward a destination within its length, or to stop, fasten or unfasten, knot or unknot, or coil itself; knots shorten it to 50 feet and grant Advantage on checks to climb it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rope of Climbing, p. 242 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the commanded rope has a fixed length, load, and movement rate; dial: knots improve climbing but shorten it.

rules.statement: The Rope of Climbing has AC 20, 20 Hit Points, and immunity to Poison and Psychic damage; it regains 1 Hit Point every 5 minutes while above 0 Hit Points, but is destroyed at 0.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rope of Climbing, p. 242 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the rope can be damaged and is destroyed at 0 Hit Points; periodic recovery requires it to survive.

rules.statement: The unattuned Rope of Entanglement is 30 feet long; while holding one end, a Magic action can send the other at a visible creature within 20 feet. A DC 15 Dexterity save failure gives Restrained; the holder can release the target by letting go or using a Bonus Action to recall the rope.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rope of Entanglement, pp. 242–243 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a save resists the binding; the holder can release or recall the rope.

rules.statement: A restrained target can use an action to make a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check to escape. If the holder is still gripping the rope when the target escapes, the holder can use a Reaction to recall it; otherwise it coils in the target’s space.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rope of Entanglement, p. 243 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the target can spend an action to try to escape, with the rope’s position depending on the holder’s reaction.

rules.statement: The Rope of Entanglement has AC 20, 20 Hit Points, and immunity to Poison and Psychic damage; it regains 1 Hit Point every 5 minutes while above 0 Hit Points and is destroyed at 0.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rope of Entanglement, p. 243 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: damage can destroy the rope; slow recovery applies only while it remains intact.

rules.statement: While the attuned Scarab of Protection is on your person, you gain +1 AC and Advantage on saves against spells. It has 12 charges; when you fail a save against a Necromancy spell or harmful effect from an Undead, a Reaction and 1 charge turn that failure into success, and the scarab is destroyed when its last charge is spent.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Scarab of Protection, p. 243 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement grants passive protection and charges can avert specified failed saves; the last charge destroys the item.

rules.statement: The attuned Scimitar of Speed grants +2 to its attack and damage rolls and lets its wielder make one attack with it as a Bonus Action on each turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Scimitar of Speed, p. 243 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement grants a recurring extra attack, limited to one per turn.

rules.statement: Sending Stones come as a matched pair; while touching one, you can cast Sending to the bearer of the other. If no creature bears the partner, you learn that and do not cast; after either stone casts, neither can be used until dawn, and destruction of one makes the other nonmagical.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sending Stones, p. 243 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the paired stones enable one daily message; bearer absence prevents casting, and destruction disables the pair.

rules.statement: While holding the Sentinel Shield, you have Advantage on Initiative rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sentinel Shield, p. 243 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: holding the shield grants two ongoing advantages.

rules.statement: A +1, +2, or +3 Shield grants that additional AC bonus while held, on top of its normal shield bonus; the listed bonuses correspond to Uncommon, Rare, and Very Rare rarity.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the shield’s rarity sets its extra AC bonus.
