rules.statement: While holding the attuned Shield of Missile Attraction, you have Resistance to damage from ranged-weapon attacks. The shield curses its attuned wearer until Remove Curse or similar magic; removing it does not end the curse, and ranged-weapon attacks aimed at creatures within 10 feet instead target the wearer.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Shield of Missile Attraction, p. 243 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement grants resistance but the curse redirects nearby ranged attacks; removing the shield alone cannot end the curse.

rules.statement: The attuned Shield of the Cavalier grants +2 AC beyond a shield’s normal bonus. When taking the Attack action, its wielder can substitute an attack to hit a target within 5 feet using Proficiency Bonus and Strength modifier; on a hit it deals 2d6 + 2 + Strength Force damage, pushes a creature up to 10 feet, and can knock down a creature no larger than the wielder.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Shield of the Cavalier, p. 243 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the shield grants defense and an attack option; dial: the attack uses one attack and only smaller or equal-sized targets can be knocked down.

rules.statement: Once per dawn, the attuned Shield of the Cavalier can use a Reaction when you or an ally within 5 feet is targeted by an attack or saves against an area effect to create an immobile 5-foot Emanation centered on you. On creation, anything not wholly inside is pushed to the nearest unoccupied space outside; for up to 1 minute while you Concentrate, nothing passes across the boundary, effects from outside cannot affect those inside, and those inside cannot harm anything outside.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Shield of the Cavalier, p. 243 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a reaction creates a bounded safe space; Concentration and once-per-dawn use limit its duration and frequency.

rules.statement: While wearing the attuned Slippers of Spider Climbing, you can move on vertical surfaces and ceilings with hands free and have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed. They do not work on slippery surfaces such as ice or oil.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Slippers of Spider Climbing, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement grants unusual climbing movement; slippery surfaces block it.

rules.statement: Sovereign Glue permanently bonds any two objects; one ounce covers a 1-foot square, application takes a Utilize action, and it sets in 1 minute. The bond can be broken only by Universal Solvent, Oil of Etherealness, or Wish; it must be stored in a container coated with Oil of Slipperiness, and a found container holds 1d6 + 1 ounces.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sovereign Glue, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a small quantity creates a permanent bond; dial: only rare specified means undo it and special storage is required.

rules.statement: While holding the attuned Spellguard Shield, you have Advantage on saves against spells and other magical effects, and spell attack rolls against you have Disadvantage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spellguard Shield, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attunement grants passive protection against magic.

rules.statement: A Spell Scroll lets a reader cast its single spell without Material components if the spell is on their spell list; otherwise it is unreadable. Casting takes the spell’s normal time and destroys the scroll on completion, but interruption does not consume it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Scroll, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a successful casting consumes the scroll; interruption preserves it.

rules.statement: If the scroll’s spell is on your spell list but above the highest level you can normally cast, make a check using your spellcasting ability against DC 10 plus spell level. Failure loses the spell from the scroll without effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Scroll, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: casting above your level requires a check and failure consumes the stored spell.

rules.statement: A scroll’s spell level sets its rarity, save DC, and attack bonus: cantrip and 1st are Common, DC 13, +5; 2nd Uncommon, DC 13, +5; 3rd Uncommon, DC 15, +7; 4th Rare, DC 15, +7; 5th Rare, DC 17, +9; 6th Very Rare, DC 17, +9; 7th Very Rare, DC 18, +10; 8th Very Rare, DC 18, +10; 9th Legendary, DC 19, +11.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Scroll, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell level determines the scroll’s fixed casting statistics and rarity.

rules.statement: A Wizard can copy a Wizard spell from a scroll into a spellbook by succeeding on an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 plus spell level. The scroll is destroyed whether the check succeeds or fails.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spell Scroll, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: copying requires a check and consumes the scroll regardless of outcome.

rules.statement: The Sphere of Annihilation obliterates matter it passes through or that passes through it, except Artifacts not susceptible to its damage; anything merely touching it without being wholly engulfed takes 8d10 Force damage. It is stationary until controlled.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphere of Annihilation, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: contact destroys or damages matter; artifacts have a specific exception.

rules.statement: Within 60 feet, a creature can use a Magic action to make a DC 25 Intelligence (Arcana) check to control the sphere until the start of its next turn, taking control from another creature if successful. Failure makes the sphere move 10 feet toward that creature; while in control, a Bonus Action moves it up to five times the controller’s Intelligence modifier in feet, at least 5 feet, in a chosen direction.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphere of Annihilation, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control lasts one turn and requires a hard check; failure moves the sphere toward the would-be controller.

rules.statement: A creature whose space the controlled sphere enters must succeed on a DC 19 Dexterity save or take 8d10 Force damage; if this reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it is obliterated, leaving possessions but no physical remains.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphere of Annihilation, p. 244 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: entry triggers a save and severe damage, with obliteration at 0 Hit Points.

rules.statement: If the sphere touches a planar portal or extradimensional space, roll 1d100: on 01–50 it is destroyed; 51–85 it enters or passes through; 86–00 a spatial rift sends it and every creature and object within 180 feet to a random plane.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphere of Annihilation, pp. 244–245 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: contact triggers one of three random outcomes; the rarest outcome transports a broad nearby area to a random plane.

rules.statement: The attuned Staff of Charming has 10 charges. It can spend 1 charge to cast Charm Person, Command, or Comprehend Languages using your spell save DC; on a successful save against an Enchantment spell targeting only you, a Reaction and 1 charge can reflect it at its caster; failing such a save can instead be changed to success, but that defense recharges only at dawn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of Charming, p. 245 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charges fuel casting and reflection; the automatic save correction is limited to once per dawn.

rules.statement: The Staff of Charming regains 1d8 + 2 charges at dawn; after its last charge is spent, a roll of 1 on a d20 destroys it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of Charming, p. 245 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: dawn restores a variable number of charges; exhausting it risks destruction.

rules.statement: A Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard attuned to and holding the Staff of Fire has Fire Resistance and can spend its 10 charges to cast Burning Hands (1), Fireball (3), or Wall of Fire (4), using their spell save DC. It regains 1d6 + 4 charges at dawn; spending the last charge risks destruction on a d20 roll of 1.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of Fire, p. 245 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: class, attunement, and holding restrict access; charges and last-charge risk limit repeated use.

rules.statement: A Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard attuned to and holding the Staff of Frost has Cold Resistance and can spend its 10 charges to cast Cone of Cold (5), Ice Storm (4), Fog Cloud (1), or Wall of Ice (4), using their spell save DC. It regains 1d6 + 4 charges at dawn; the passage continues beyond the available text.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of Frost, p. 245 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: class, attunement, and holding restrict access; charges and daily recovery limit use.

rules.statement: While holding the staff, you have Advantage on saves against spells. When a spell targets only you, you can use your Reaction to cancel it and add charges equal to its level; if this would exceed 50 charges, the staff explodes using its retributive-strike effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of the Magi, Spell Absorption (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the reaction, single-target restriction, and 50-charge ceiling; dial: the blast is catastrophic, so absorbing an overfilling spell risks everyone nearby.

rules.statement: While holding the wand, spend 1 charge and choose a point within 120 feet, then roll d100 on its effects table to determine the magic produced. Outcomes can affect that point, the wielder, or nearby creatures; some require further dice rolls or saving throws, and the wand regains 1d6 + 1 charges at dawn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wand of Wonder; Wand of Wonder Effects, pp. 251–252 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the stated random table and charge use; dial: the wielder cannot reliably select the result and may suffer the outcome.

rules.statement: As a Magic action, unfold the cloth on a solid surface to create a two-way, 6-foot-wide portal to a world or plane chosen by the GM. A creature within 5 feet can close it by taking a Magic action to fold it up; after opening it, the cloth cannot open another portal for 1d8 hours.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Well of Many Worlds (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the destination externally chosen and the portal closable; dial: access to another world is constrained by the 1d8-hour reuse delay.

rules.statement: As a Magic action, throw the staff into an unoccupied space within 10 feet to transform it into a Giant Constrictor Snake under your control, acting immediately after you in initiative. You can command it mentally without an action while it is within 60 feet and you are not Incapacitated; reverting it takes a Bonus Action and prevents reuse for 1 hour, while reducing it to 0 Hit Points destroys the staff.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of the Python (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the range, control, and one-hour reuse limit; dial: losing the transformed creature to damage destroys the item.

rules.statement: Plant the staff in earth in an unoccupied space and expend 1 charge as a Magic action to turn it into a healthy, ordinary-looking tree 60 feet tall with a trunk 5 feet across and branches spreading 20 feet. Touching it and taking a Magic action restores the staff; creatures in the tree fall when it reverts.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of the Woodlands, Tree Form (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the charge cost and physical placement; dial: reverting the tree can cause creatures in it to fall.

rules.statement: While holding the wand, spend 1 charge as a Magic action to learn the direction, but not distance, of the nearest hostile creature within 60 feet for 1 minute. It senses hostile creatures even if invisible, ethereal, disguised, or hidden, and the effect ends if you stop holding it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wand of Enemy Detection (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the nearest-target and 60-foot limits; dial: the wand reveals direction without giving distance or exact location.

rules.statement: While attuned and with the weapon within your reach, you and allies within 30 feet gain Advantage on Initiative rolls, and natural sleepers among them awaken when combat begins; magically induced sleep is unaffected.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Weapon of Warning (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the benefits only while attuned and nearby; dial: magical sleep is not overcome.

rules.statement: When you hit a creature with this weapon, it takes an extra 2d6 Necrotic damage and must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution save or be unable to regain Hit Points for 1 hour. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sword of Wounding (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the one-hour maximum and end-on-save rule; dial: the healing block can persist through multiple turns.

rules.statement: While holding the staff, you can cast Cure Wounds, Lesser Restoration, or Mass Cure Wounds using your spellcasting ability modifier, spending charges as listed: Cure Wounds costs 1 per spell level up to level 4, Lesser Restoration costs 2, and Mass Cure Wounds costs 5. It regains 1d6 + 4 charges daily at dawn; after spending the last charge, a roll of 1 on d20 makes it vanish permanently.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Staff of Healing (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve the per-spell charge costs and dawn recovery; dial: exhausting the reserve risks permanent loss.

rules.statement: The wand has 7 charges and regains 1d6 + 1 daily at dawn; while holding it, you can spend at most 3 charges to cast Fireball, with 1 charge producing the level 3 version and each additional charge raising its level by 1. If you spend the final charge, a d20 roll of 1 destroys the wand.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wand of Fireballs (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the seven-charge pool and three-charge casting cap; dial: spending the final charge risks destroying the wand.

rules.statement: When you hit an object with this weapon, maximize its weapon damage dice. On a natural 20 against a creature, deal an extra 14 Slashing damage and give it 1 Exhaustion level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sword of Sharpness (dnd-srd-5.2.1#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply maximum dice only to object attacks and the added damage only on a natural 20; dial: the exhaustion consequence makes critical hits more consequential.

rules.statement: When a monster’s attack hits, its stat block specifies the resulting damage or other effects; effects that happen on a miss or regardless of hit are separately identified. For a saving-throw effect, the stat block gives the save type and DC, who rolls, and outcomes; a successful save for “half damage only” halves damage (round down) and avoids every other effect.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Saving Throw Effect Notation; Damage Notation, p. 257 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: resolve attack and save outcomes
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: follow the specified hit, miss, or save outcome; dial: use the stated damage expression or fixed number, because the notation allows either.

rules.statement: For damage shown as both a fixed number and a dice expression, choose one method and do not combine them. A creature’s Multiattack entry determines the attacks and any additional abilities it can use as part of its Attack action.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Damage Notation; Multiattack, p. 257 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use one listed damage method and the listed attack sequence; dial: none, since these specify resolution rather than a resource cost.

rules.statement: A monster spell list specifies its spellcasting ability and any save DC or attack bonus; absent a special rule, spells of level 1 or higher are cast at their lowest level and cannot be heightened. A listed spell may have restrictions, such as affecting only the caster, and its trait states which components are unnecessary; any required material components are available to the monster.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spellcasting, p. 257 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: cast at minimum level with listed restrictions and components; dial: special stat-block rules can override the general limits.

rules.statement: A monster casting a listed spell with a casting time of at least 1 minute must take the Magic action on each of its turns and maintain Concentration for the casting, unless the action description explicitly says otherwise.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spellcasting, p. 257 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require repeated actions and Concentration; dial: an explicit action-specific exception removes that burden.

rules.statement: A Legendary Action is taken immediately after another creature’s turn ends, at most one at a time; the monster cannot use one while Incapacitated or otherwise unable to act. It spends a listed use and regains all spent uses at the start of its own turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Legendary Actions, p. 257 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spend a limited use for an off-turn action; dial: the stat block sets the number of uses and incapacitation blocks access.

rules.statement: A stat-block option marked X/Day can be used that many times and regains all spent uses when the monster finishes a Long Rest. An option marked Recharge X–Y can be used once, then regains its use at the start of a turn on a d6 result in the stated range, and also recharges on a Short or Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Limited Usage, p. 257 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: track uses and restore them by the stated rest or die roll; dial: recharge range and daily allotment determine availability.

rules.statement: A stat-block option marked “Recharge after a Short or Long Rest” is usable once, then becomes available again only after the monster finishes either kind of rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Limited Usage, p. 257 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use between rests; dial: either listed rest restores it.

rules.statement: An aboleth can return in 5d10 days after destruction with all Hit Points, appearing in the Far Realm or another GM-chosen location. It can also choose to turn a failed saving throw into a success three times daily, or four times while in its lair.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Aboleth: Eldritch Restoration; Legendary Resistance, p. 258 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destruction triggers delayed return and failed saves can be negated; dial: restoration timing and save-negation uses are limited.

rules.statement: While underwater, an aboleth exposes creatures ending its turn within 5 feet to a DC 14 Constitution save; failure curses the creature, allowing air-and-water breathing but preventing Hit Point recovery unless underwater. Away from water, the cursed creature takes 1d12 Acid damage every 10 minutes unless its skin is moistened in time.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Aboleth: Mucus Cloud, p. 258 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed save imposes the curse and its ongoing restrictions; dial: moisture prevents the periodic damage, while water is required for healing.

rules.statement: An aboleth that can see a creature communicating with it telepathically learns that creature’s greatest desires. Its Dominate Mind, usable twice daily, can charm one visible creature within 30 feet on a failed DC 16 Wisdom save; the target acts as its ally and is controlled within 60 feet, while telepathic communication works at any distance. The target retries the save when damaged and after each 24-hour period spent at least 1 mile away; success ends the effect, as does the aboleth’s death or the two moving to different planes.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Aboleth: Probing Telepathy; Dominate Mind, p. 258 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed save binds behavior and shares thoughts; dial: damage, sustained distance, death, or planar separation can end the binding.

rules.statement: A balor that dies explodes, forcing creatures within 30 feet to make a DC 20 Dexterity save against 9d6 Fire plus 9d6 Force damage (half on success). If it dies outside the Abyss, it immediately returns at full Hit Points somewhere in the Abyss.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Balor: Death Throes, p. 261 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death triggers an area blast and return; dial: returning applies only when death occurs outside the Abyss.

rules.statement: A balor can teleport itself or a willing demon within 10 feet up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Balor: Teleport, p. 261 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: move the balor or nearby willing demon within the stated range; dial: destination must be visible and unoccupied.

rules.statement: A devil that dies outside the Nine Hells disappears in sulfurous smoke and immediately returns at full Hit Points somewhere in the Nine Hells.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Barbed Devil: Diabolical Restoration, p. 262; Bone Devil: Diabolical Restoration, p. 267 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death outside the home plane triggers return there; dial: this restoration rule does not apply to death inside the Nine Hells.

rules.statement: A drider or ettercap can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check. A drider has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls in sunlight; a drider or ettercap ignores web-caused movement restrictions and senses the location of creatures touching the same web.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Drider and Ettercap, Traits (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; unusual climbing and web awareness are species traits, while sunlight impairs the drider.

rules.statement: A drider can cast Darkness, Faerie Fire, or Web as a bonus action, with no Material components; it uses Wisdom and has a save DC of 14. Each use requires the trait to recharge on a roll of 5–6.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Drider, Bonus Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; this is limited by the listed choices and recharge, and draws on the drider’s innate magic.

rules.statement: A dryad can communicate with Beasts and Plants as if they shared a language. It can teleport from within 5 feet of one Large or larger tree to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of another such tree within 60 feet.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dryad, Traits; Bonus Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; communication is limited to Beasts and Plants, and the teleport requires two nearby trees.

rules.statement: A dryad can cast Charm Monster at will without Material components, using Charisma with save DC 14; the charm lasts 24 hours, but ends early if the dryad casts the spell again. It can also cast Entangle and Pass without Trace once each per day.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dryad, Spellcasting (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; the long charm is constrained by its early-ending rule, while the other spells are each limited to once daily.

rules.statement: If an efreeti dies outside the Plane of Fire, its body dissolves and it revives with all Hit Points in a new body there in 1d4 days. An erinyes killed outside the Nine Hells instead revives there instantly at full Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Efreeti, Elemental Restoration; Erinyes, Diabolical Restoration (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; death relocates each creature’s return to its home plane, with the efreeti facing a 1d4-day delay.

rules.statement: An efreeti has a 30% chance to know Wish; if it does, it can cast it only for a non-genie who communicates an understandable wish. It avoids the spell’s stress when casting for that creature, but after three such castings it cannot do so again for 365 days.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Efreeti, Wishes (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; access is uncertain and the efreeti’s service is capped at three castings per 365 days.

rules.statement: An erinyes can use its magic rope to target one visible creature within 120 feet; a failed DC 16 Strength save deals 4d6 Force damage and Restrains it. The effect ends if the rope is destroyed, the erinyes releases the target as a bonus action, or it uses the rope action again; the rope has AC 20 and 90 Hit Points, and is restored after a Short or Long Rest if damaged or destroyed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Erinyes, Magic Rope; Entangling Rope (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; restraint depends on a destructible tool that can be repaired only at a rest.

rules.statement: An ettercap can target one visible Large or smaller creature within 30 feet with a web strand; on a failed DC 12 Dexterity save, the target is Restrained until the web is destroyed. The web has AC 10, 5 Hit Points, Vulnerability to Fire, and immunity to Bludgeoning, Poison, and Psychic damage; the ettercap can then use a bonus action to pull a creature it has restrained by this web up to 25 feet straight toward itself.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ettercap, Web Strand; Reel (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; escape hinges on destroying a fragile web, and pulling only works on a creature held by that web.

rules.statement: At the end of each of its turns, a fire elemental deals 1d10 Fire damage to each creature in its 10-foot Emanation, and creatures and flammable objects there start burning. It can pass through gaps as narrow as 1 inch without extra movement and enter a creature’s space; the first time it does so on a turn, that creature takes 1d10 Fire damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fire Elemental, Traits (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; the aura and contact harm are ongoing hazards tied to the elemental’s proximity and movement.

rules.statement: A flesh golem that starts its turn Bloodied rolls 1d6; on a 6, it goes berserk and attacks the nearest creature it can see on each turn, or an object if none is near enough to reach and attack. It stays berserk until destroyed or no longer Bloodied; its creator within 60 feet can use an action and succeed on a DC 15 Charisma (Persuasion) check to suppress the berserk state until the golem’s next turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Flesh Golem, Berserk (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; low health can trigger unpredictable aggression, and calming it takes proximity, an action, and a successful check.

rules.statement: A ghost can possess a visible Humanoid within 5 feet on a failed DC 13 Charisma save; the target is Incapacitated and loses control of its body but remains aware, while the ghost cannot be targeted except by effects that specifically target Undead. Possession ends if the body reaches 0 Hit Points or the ghost leaves as a bonus action, after which the ghost appears within 5 feet and that target is immune to this ghost’s possession for 24 hours; a successful initial save also grants that immunity.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ghost, Possession (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; control requires a nearby Humanoid and a failed save, and ends through bodily collapse or the ghost’s choice.

rules.statement: A ghost can see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane while on the Material Plane. It can also shift to the Border Ethereal with Etherealness, but while on one plane it cannot affect or be affected by anything on the other.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Ghost, Ethereal Sight; Etherealness (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; the ghost can cross the planar boundary, but separation prevents interactions across it.

rules.statement: A gibbering mouther makes nearby creatures that start their turn within 20 feet and can hear its babbling roll a DC 10 Wisdom save; on a failure, a d8 determines their turn, from doing nothing or moving randomly without acting to attacking a randomly chosen nearby creature. The effect applies only while the mouther is babbling and not Incapacitated.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Gibbering Mouther, Gibbering (dnd-srd-5.2.1#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial off; exposure can disrupt a turn unpredictably, but requires proximity and the mouther to be babbling.

rules.statement: When the steam mephit dies, each creature within 5 feet makes a DC 10 Dexterity save, taking 5 (2d4) fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Steam Mephit — Traits, p. 308 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the burst is limited to creatures close to the dying mephit.

rules.statement: Attack rolls against the steam mephit have disadvantage unless it is incapacitated.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Steam Mephit — Traits, p. 308 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the defense fails when the mephit is incapacitated.

rules.statement: On a recharge roll of 6, the steam mephit exhales steam in a 15-foot cone; each creature makes a DC 10 Constitution save, taking 5 (2d4) fire damage on a failure and losing 10 feet of Speed until the end of the mephit’s next turn. A success halves the damage and avoids the Speed reduction, and being underwater does not grant resistance to this fire damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Steam Mephit — Actions, p. 308 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the breath is limited by its recharge and short-lived movement penalty.

rules.statement: A merfolk can breathe both air and water. When its returning spear hits a creature, that creature’s Speed decreases by 10 feet until the end of its next turn; the spear returns to the merfolk’s hand immediately after a ranged attack whether it hits or misses.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Merfolk Skirmisher — Traits and Actions, p. 308 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the movement penalty lasts only until the target’s next turn ends.

rules.statement: A merrow’s bite poisons a creature until the end of the merrow’s next turn. Its harpoon pulls a Large or smaller target it hits up to 15 feet straight toward the merrow.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Merrow — Actions, p. 308 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the pull requires a hit and the poison is brief.

rules.statement: In object form, the mimic adheres to anything that touches it; a Huge or smaller creature stuck to it is grappled (escape DC 13), and attempts to escape have disadvantage. Its pseudopod can likewise grapple a Large or smaller creature on a hit, with the same escape DC and disadvantage on escape checks.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mimic — Traits and Actions, p. 309 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; grappling is limited by size and can be escaped with a check.

rules.statement: As a bonus action, the mimic can become a Small or Medium object or return to its blob form, retaining its game statistics; worn and carried equipment does not change form.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mimic — Bonus Actions, p. 309 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the disguise does not change statistics or equipment.

rules.statement: A mummy’s rotting fist curses a creature it hits: it cannot regain Hit Points, its maximum Hit Points decrease by 10 (3d6) every 24 hours, and the maximum does not return to normal after a Long Rest. If this attack reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, the target dies and turns to dust.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mummy — Actions, p. 309 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the curse imposes continuing deterioration and prevents ordinary recovery.

rules.statement: If its heart remains intact, a destroyed mummy lord forms a new body after 24 hours and revives with all its Hit Points in an unoccupied space in its lair. Its Tiny heart has AC 17 and 10 Hit Points, and is immune to all damage except fire.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mummy Lord — Traits, p. 310 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; revival depends on the heart surviving and is anchored to the lair.

rules.statement: A night hag can use Nightmare Haunting once per day only while on the Ethereal Plane and carrying its soul bag, targeting a creature it can see on the Material Plane with Dream. Protection from Evil and Good or Magic Circle prevents the effect; damage from the dream reduces the target’s Hit Point maximum by the same amount, and a target killed by it has its soul trapped in the bag and cannot be raised until released.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Night Hag — Traits and Actions, p. 311 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the effect costs a daily use, requires a bag and planar position, and has protective counters.

rules.statement: A night hag’s soul bag has AC 15, 20 Hit Points, and resistance to all damage; destroying it releases its stored souls, and the hag can make another after 7 days.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Night Hag — Traits, p. 311 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; souls remain contained only while the bag survives.

rules.statement: A nightmare can grant fire-damage resistance to a rider while that rider is on it. It can also take itself and up to three willing creatures within 5 feet between the Material and Ethereal Planes by teleportation.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Nightmare — Traits and Actions, p. 311 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; protection lasts only while mounted, and planar passage carries at most three willing companions.

rules.statement: A phase spider can see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane and vice versa. As a bonus action it can teleport between the Material and Ethereal Planes.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Phase Spider — Traits and Bonus Actions, p. 314 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; sight is limited to 60 feet and travel is between these two planes.

rules.statement: A creature caught by one of the roper’s tentacles is grappled with escape DC 14 and poisoned until that grapple ends. A tentacle has AC 20 and 10 Hit Points; destroying it releases its captive without harming the roper, and it regrows at the start of the roper’s next turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Roper — Tentacle (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these restrictions apply to creatures seized by a tentacle; dial: escape and tentacle destruction; the grapple and poison end when the hold is broken.

rules.statement: A rust monster can locate ferrous metal within 30 feet. Against a worn or carried nonmagical metal weapon or armor within 5 feet, its antennae force a DC 11 Dexterity save; on a failure, the item takes a cumulative −1 penalty to attack rolls or AC, respectively, and is destroyed at −5 or when armor AC reaches 10. Mending removes the penalty; touching an unattended nonmagical metal object destroys a 1-foot cube.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rust Monster — Iron Scent; Antennae; Destroy Metal (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only nearby ferrous metal and nonmagical metal objects are affected; dial: saves, penalties, and destruction thresholds; the gear can be repaired with Mending.

rules.statement: A sahuagin can magically direct sharks within 120 feet by special telepathy. It must submerge at least once every 4 hours or it risks suffocation while out of water, though it can breathe both air and water.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sahuagin Warrior — Traits (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shark control is limited to 120 feet; dial: air-breathing survival requires submersion every four hours.

rules.statement: At the end of each of its turns, a salamander deals 7 fire damage to creatures of its choice within its 5-foot emanation. Its flame spear returns to its hand immediately after a ranged attack, whether the attack hits or misses.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Salamander — Fire Aura; Flame Spear (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the aura reaches only 5 feet and triggers at turn end; dial: chosen targets and automatic weapon return; the spear is not lost after a throw.

rules.statement: When a sea hag is within 30 feet of at least two hag allies, it can cast one listed spell without material components using Intelligence and save DC 11; each spell cast this way cannot be used again until the hag finishes a Long Rest. A visible Beast or Humanoid that starts its turn within 30 feet must make a DC 11 Wisdom save or become frightened until the start of its next turn; a success grants immunity to that hag’s appearance for 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sea Hag — Coven Magic; Vile Appearance (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell access requires two nearby hag allies and fear requires seeing the true form; dial: each spell is once per Long Rest and a successful save gives temporary immunity.

rules.statement: The shadow’s draining swipe reduces a creature’s Strength by 1d4; if Strength reaches 0, the target dies. A Humanoid killed by this attack produces a shadow from its corpse after 1d4 hours.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Shadow — Draining Swipe (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only this attack causes the score loss and resulting death; dial: the transformation occurs after a random 1d4-hour delay and only for slain Humanoids.

rules.statement: A shambling mound regains Hit Points equal to lightning damage dealt to it. Its engulfed creature is grappled and, until freed, blinded and restrained, takes 10 lightning damage at the start of each of its turns, and moves with the mound; the mound can hold only one creature this way.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Shambling Mound — Lightning Absorption; Engulf (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lightning damage fuels recovery and engulfing holds one creature; dial: healing matches damage dealt and the damage continues only while the grapple lasts.

rules.statement: A shield guardian is bound to its amulet: on the same plane, its wearer can call it telepathically and it knows the amulet’s direction and distance. Within 60 feet, half the damage the wearer takes, rounded up, transfers to the guardian; the wearer can also store one spell of level 4 or lower in it by casting on it within 5 feet, replacing any previously stored spell, which the guardian can later cast without components before the stored spell is lost.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Shield Guardian — Bound; Spell Storing (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bond works only on the same plane and damage sharing only within 60 feet; dial: one stored spell at a time, with replacement erasing the previous spell.

rules.statement: A solar that dies outside Mount Celestia immediately reappears there in a new body at full Hit Points. Its wearer’s protection is not relevant; this restoration is limited by where the solar dies, and no further cost is specified.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Solar — Exalted Restoration (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: applies only if death occurs outside Mount Celestia; dial: restoration is immediate and complete, with the destination fixed to that plane.

rules.statement: A silver dragon’s paralyzing breath first incapacitates a failed-save target until the end of its next turn; the target then repeats the save, becoming paralyzed on a second failure. It repeats the save at each turn end to end the paralysis on success, and succeeds automatically after 1 minute.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Silver Dragons — Paralyzing Breath (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect requires successive failed Constitution saves; dial: repeated saves can end paralysis, which also ends automatically after one minute.

rules.statement: The sphinx of lore cannot be remotely observed or have its thoughts detected by magic without permission, and Insight checks to judge its sincerity or intentions are made with Disadvantage. Its listed spells use Intelligence and save DC 16, and each spell marked once per day is available once before recovery is specified by the trait’s daily limit.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphinx of Lore — Inscrutable; Spellcasting (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: magical observation and thought detection require permission; dial: Insight is disadvantaged and daily spells are limited to one use each.

rules.statement: A tarrasque’s bite grapples its target (escape DC 20), restrains it, and prevents teleportation until the grapple ends. It can swallow a grappled creature on a failed DC 27 Strength save, holding up to six; a swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, cannot teleport, has Total Cover from outside effects, and takes 56 acid damage at the start of each tarrasque turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Tarrasque — Bite; Swallow (dnd-srd-5.2.1#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: swallowing requires an existing grapple and failed save, with a six-creature capacity; dial: escape and teleport are blocked, while sustained acid damage and confinement continue inside.

rules.statement: If an ally is within 5 feet of the target and isn’t Incapacitated, the attacker has Advantage on its attack roll against that target.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: only attacks against a creature beside a non-Incapacitated ally qualify.

rules.statement: A treant deals double damage to objects and structures. Once per day, it can animate up to two visible trees within 60 feet; each acts immediately after the treant on its initiative, obeys it, and uses its statistics except Intelligence and Charisma become 1, speech is lost, and it lacks the animation action; the tree reverts after 1 day, on either creature’s death, or when more than 120 feet away, taking root if possible.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Treant — Siege Monster; Animate Trees, p. 333 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: at most two trees, once per day, with a 120-foot tether and temporary service.

rules.statement: A troll can lose a limb up to four times per day if it ends a turn Bloodied after taking at least 15 Slashing damage that turn. Each missing limb gives it one Exhaustion level; it regrows replacement limbs when it next regains Hit Points, while a severed limb acts after the troll and, if not destroyed within 24 hours, has a 1-in-12 chance to become a troll or otherwise withers.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Troll and Troll Limb — Loathsome Limbs; Troll Spawn, pp. 333–334 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: limb loss requires a specific damage-and-health crisis, and each missing limb burdens the troll with Exhaustion.

rules.statement: A troll regains 15 Hit Points at the start of each turn, except that Acid or Fire damage prevents this recovery on its next turn; it dies only if it starts its turn at 0 Hit Points without regenerating. A troll limb similarly regains 5 Hit Points, with the same Acid or Fire interruption and death check.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Troll and Troll Limb — Regeneration, p. 333 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: ongoing recovery is substantial but vulnerable to Acid or Fire.

rules.statement: A vampire familiar can communicate telepathically with its vampire master and let the master perceive through its senses while they are on the same plane. If its dagger attack reduces a target to 0 Hit Points, the target becomes Stable but remains Poisoned for 1 hour and Paralyzed while Poisoned.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Vampire Familiar — Vampiric Connection; Umbral Dagger, p. 334 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: remote perception and communication require the familiar and master to share a plane; the attack’s disabling effect requires reducing a target to 0 Hit Points.

rules.statement: A vampire spawn cannot enter a residence without an occupant’s invitation, takes 20 Acid damage if it ends its turn in running water, and takes 20 Radiant damage when it starts its turn in sunlight; sunlight also gives it Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks. A piercing weapon driven into its heart destroys it while it is Incapacitated.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Vampire Spawn — Vampire Weakness, p. 335 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: these vulnerabilities depend on thresholds or circumstances—residence entry, turn-end in running water, sunlight, or an incapacitated state.

rules.statement: A vampire that reaches 0 Hit Points outside its resting place becomes mist without using an action, if it can shape-shift; otherwise it is destroyed. At 0 Hit Points in mist form it must reach its resting place within 2 hours or be destroyed; there it returns to vampire form, is Paralyzed until it regains Hit Points, and recovers 1 Hit Point after 1 hour.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Vampire — Misty Escape, p. 335 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: survival at 0 Hit Points depends on reaching a designated resting place within 2 hours.

rules.statement: A vampire can shape-shift into a Tiny bat or Medium mist, or back to its vampire form, only when not in sunlight or running water; worn items transform with it. Bat form cannot speak, while mist form cannot act, speak, or manipulate objects, is weightless, can enter and stop in enemy spaces, passes through spaces air can pass through but not through liquid, and resists all damage except sunlight damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Vampire — Shape-Shift, p. 336 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: transformation is blocked by sunlight or running water, and mist form trades interaction and action capabilities for unusual movement and broad damage resistance.

rules.statement: When a vampire’s bite reduces a Humanoid to 0 Hit Points and the victim is then buried, the victim rises at the following sunset as a Vampire Spawn under the vampire’s control. A vampire’s Charm recharges on a 5–6, lasts 24 hours, makes the Charmed target willing to be bitten without the bite ending the spell, and leaves the target unaware of the charm when it ends.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Vampire — Bite and Charm, p. 336 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: spawn creation requires a Humanoid to reach 0 Hit Points from the bite and be buried; charm is limited by recharge and duration.

rules.statement: A vrock’s Spore attack recharges on a 6 and forces each creature in its 20-foot emanation to make a DC 15 Constitution save; on failure, the creature is Poisoned, takes 1d10 Poison damage at the start of each turn, and repeats the save at each turn’s end until successful, while Holy Water poured on it ends the effect early. Its once-per-day Screech forces the same save in that area; failure deals 3d6 Thunder damage and Stuns until the end of the vrock’s next turn, with demons succeeding automatically.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Vrock — Spores; Stunning Screech, p. 336 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: the effects are area-limited and require failed saves; spores can be ended by a successful repeat save or Holy Water.

rules.statement: A unicorn’s spells use Charisma, require no components, and have save DC 14; it can cast Detect Evil and Good or Druidcraft at will and each of five listed spells once per day. Three times per day it can touch another creature with its horn to cast Cure Wounds or Lesser Restoration.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Unicorn — Spellcasting; Unicorn’s Blessing, p. 334 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: spell access is limited by the listed at-will or once-daily uses, and the healing touch is limited to three uses per day.

rules.statement: A werebear’s Bite can curse a Humanoid that fails a DC 14 Constitution save; if that cursed target reaches 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Werebear under the GM’s control with 10 Hit Points. A successful save grants immunity to that werebear’s curse for 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Werebear — Bite, p. 337 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enabled; dial: the curse requires a failed save and only transforms the victim if it later reaches 0 Hit Points.

rules.statement: A creature with Pack Tactics has Advantage on an attack roll against a target when an ally is within 5 feet of that target and the ally isn’t Incapacitated.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Traits — Blood Hawk; also several other beast entries, pp. 346–357 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the attack bonus only when the nearby ally qualifies; dial: none; the ally’s incapacitation removes the benefit.

rules.statement: A Bloodied boar has Advantage on attack rolls; the Giant Boar instead has Advantage specifically on melee attack rolls while Bloodied.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Traits — Boar; Giant Boar (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enable the listed attack advantage while Bloodied; dial: none; the benefit depends on the creature being injured enough to meet that state.

rules.statement: A boar, elk, or goat that moves at least 20 feet straight toward a target immediately before a hit deals extra damage and can knock the target Prone; the target-size limits and added damage vary by creature.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Actions — Gore (Boar); Ram (Elk, Giant Goat, Goat) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require the stated straight-line movement and size limit; dial: none; the charge needs distance and a suitable target.

rules.statement: A crocodile’s Bite can Grapple a Medium or smaller target, and that target is Restrained while Grappled; the Giant Crocodile applies the same effects to Large or smaller targets and cannot Tail-attack the creature it is holding.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Actions — Bite (Crocodile); Actions — Bite (Giant Crocodile) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the grapple and restraint on a qualifying hit; dial: none; holding a target limits the giant crocodile’s use of its Tail.

rules.statement: A constrictor’s Constrict forces a specified-size target it can see within range to make a Strength save (DC 12 or 14); on failure it takes bludgeoning damage and is Grappled, with an escape DC equal to the save DC.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Actions — Constrict (Constrictor Snake; Giant Constrictor Snake) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve the save, damage, and grapple exactly as listed; dial: none; the target can escape using the listed DC.

rules.statement: A Giant Frog or Giant Toad can swallow a qualifying creature it is grappling; the swallowed creature becomes Blinded and Restrained, has Total Cover from outside effects, and is no longer Grappled. The frog’s target can escape if it dies and is disgorged after taking 5 acid damage at the end of its next turn if that damage does not kill it; the toad deals 10 acid damage at the end of each of its turns, can hold only one creature, and releases it if it dies.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Actions — Swallow (Giant Frog; Giant Toad), pp. 351–354 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use each animal’s stated capacity, timing, and escape clauses; dial: none; swallowing removes the victim from ordinary external targeting but risks harm over time.

rules.statement: The Giant Spider’s Web forces one visible creature within 60 feet to make a DC 13 Dexterity save; failure Restrains it until the web is destroyed, and the web has AC 10, 5 Hit Points, vulnerability to fire, and immunity to poison and psychic damage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Actions — Web (Giant Spider), p. 354 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the restraint in place until the web is destroyed; dial: none; escape depends on breaking a small, fire-vulnerable object.

rules.statement: A Giant Octopus can use its once-per-day Ink Cloud when it takes damage underwater; an Octopus can use its once-per-day cloud when a creature ends its turn within 5 feet underwater. Each fills the stated cube with heavy obscurement for 1 minute or until a strong current or similar effect disperses it, and the creature can move up to its Swim Speed.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Reactions — Ink Cloud (Giant Octopus, Octopus), pp. 352, 358 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow one cloud per day with the listed trigger and duration; dial: none; the obscuring escape is limited by underwater conditions and can be dispersed.

rules.statement: A Giant Owl can cast Detect Evil and Good and Detect Magic at will, and Clairvoyance once per day, without spell components; it uses Wisdom as its spellcasting ability.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Actions — Spellcasting (Giant Owl), p. 352 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant only the listed spells at the stated frequency; dial: none; the owl’s spell use is limited to its specified repertoire.

rules.statement: The Lion can replace one attack in its Multiattack with a Roar; one creature within 15 feet must make a DC 11 Wisdom save or become Frightened until the start of the lion’s next turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Actions — Multiattack and Roar (Lion), p. 357 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve the save and end the fear at the stated time; dial: none; using the roar replaces an attack.

rules.statement: A creature hit by the Giant Centipede’s Bite is Poisoned until the start of the centipede’s next turn; a creature hit by the Giant Vulture’s Gouge is Poisoned until the end of the vulture’s next turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Actions — Bite (Giant Centipede), p. 350; Gouge (Giant Vulture), p. 354 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply Poisoned for the specific duration after a hit; dial: none; the condition ends automatically at the stated turn boundary.

rules.statement: The Giant Spider and Giant Lizard can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check; a Giant Spider also ignores movement restrictions from webs and knows the location of any creature touching the same web.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Traits — Spider Climb and Web Walker (Giant Spider); Spider Climb (Giant Lizard), pp. 352, 354 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant these movement and web-awareness exceptions only to the listed creatures; dial: none; the spider’s detection is limited to creatures contacting its web.

rules.statement: A shark makes its attack roll with Advantage when one of its allies is within 5 feet of the target and that ally is not Incapacitated.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Reef Shark — Traits (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the benefit depends on nearby allied support.

rules.statement: A shark can breathe only underwater.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Reef Shark — Traits (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; its breathing is limited to its aquatic habitat.

rules.statement: A rhinoceros that moves at least 20 feet straight toward a Large or smaller target immediately before hitting it with Gore deals an extra 2d8 damage and knocks the target Prone.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rhinoceros — Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the added impact requires a direct charge.

rules.statement: A seahorse can breathe only underwater; while underwater, it can move up to its Swim Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Seahorse — Traits; Seahorse — Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the swift dash is restricted to underwater movement.

rules.statement: A spider can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without an ability check. It ignores movement restrictions caused by webs and senses the location of creatures touching the same web.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Spider — Traits (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; climbing and web awareness are limited to the spider's special abilities.

rules.statement: Each swarm can share a creature’s space and pass through openings large enough for one of its Tiny members; it cannot regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Swarm of Bats, Swarm of Insects, Swarm of Piranhas, Swarm of Rats, Swarm of Ravens, and Swarm of Venomous Snakes — Traits (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the swarm's movement through small gaps is balanced by its inability to recover hit points.

rules.statement: A swarm’s attacks deal less damage when it is Bloodied: the listed reduced damage applies to the bat, insect, piranha, rat, and raven swarms.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Swarm of Bats, Swarm of Insects, Swarm of Piranhas, Swarm of Rats, and Swarm of Ravens — Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the attack weakens as the swarm loses vitality.

rules.statement: A piranha swarm makes its Bite attack with Advantage against a target that is missing any Hit Points.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Swarm of Piranhas — Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the swarm is more effective against wounded prey.

rules.statement: A raven swarm can force one creature in its space to make a DC 10 Wisdom save; on failure the creature is Deafened until the swarm’s next turn begins and has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while Deafened. The swarm can use this attack again when its Recharge 6 condition is met.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Swarm of Ravens — Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the brief disruption requires the target to fail a save and is limited by recharge.

rules.statement: A tiger’s Rend knocks a Large or smaller target Prone on a hit; as a Bonus Action, the tiger can take the Disengage or Hide action.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Tiger — Actions; Tiger — Bonus Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the knockdown follows a hit, while its extra mobility uses a Bonus Action.

rules.statement: A tyrannosaurus that hits a Large or smaller creature with Bite Grapples it (escape DC 17); the target is also Restrained while Grappled and cannot be targeted by the tyrannosaurus’s Tail. Its Tail knocks a Huge or smaller target Prone on a hit.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Tyrannosaurus Rex — Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; the bite restricts both the target and the tyrannosaurus's follow-up options.

rules.statement: A wolf has Advantage on attack rolls against a creature if one of its allies is within 5 feet of that creature and the ally is not Incapacitated. On a Bite hit against a Medium or smaller creature, the wolf knocks it Prone.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Wolf — Traits; Wolf — Actions (dnd-srd-5.2.1#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no dial; its benefits rely on nearby allies or a successful bite.

rules.statement: At Warlock level 1, an occult pact with an entity grants the character spellcasting, but this passage specifies no service, payment, or other price owed to the entity. Pact Magic provides a limited set of same-level spell slots for Warlock spells of levels 1–5; all spent slots return after a Short or Long Rest, and a spell cast with one of these slots uses that slot’s level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Warlock, Level 1: Pact Magic (p. 71) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; no price or patron enforcement is stated, so do not add a cost or obligation.

rules.statement: At Warlock level 2, a one-minute rite restores spent Pact Magic slots, up to half the character’s maximum number of slots rounded up. This can be done once per Long Rest; at level 20, using the rite restores all spent Pact Magic slots instead.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Warlock, Level 2: Magical Cunning; Level 20: Eldritch Master (pp. 72) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; recovery is capped by the stated amount and limited to once per Long Rest.

rules.statement: At Warlock level 9, the character can cast Contact Other Plane without a slot to contact their patron, automatically succeeding on that spell’s saving throw. This use is available once per Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Warlock, Level 9: Contact Patron (p. 72) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the feature enables contact but states no bargain, answer, or further cost.

rules.statement: Beginning at Warlock level 11, the patron grants a chosen level 6 Warlock spell that can be cast once without a slot per Long Rest; further such spells are gained at levels 13, 15, and 17, at levels 7, 8, and 9 respectively. When gaining a Warlock level, the character may replace one arcanum spell with another Warlock spell of the same level.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Warlock, Level 11: Mystic Arcanum (p. 72) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the granted magic has a once-per-Long-Rest use limit, with no additional patron price specified.

rules.statement: A Warlock gains one Eldritch Invocation at level 1 and more at specified levels; an invocation’s prerequisites must be met, and the same option cannot be selected twice unless it says otherwise. Whenever the Warlock gains a level, one invocation can be replaced, except one required by another invocation they have.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Warlock, Level 1: Eldritch Invocations (pp. 70–71) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; selection is limited by prerequisites and dependency rules, with replacement only on gaining a level.

rules.statement: Pact of the Blade lets a Warlock use a Bonus Action to conjure a chosen Simple or Martial Melee weapon, or bond with a touched magic weapon that is neither attuned by someone else nor bonded to another Warlock. The Warlock is proficient with it, may use it as a spellcasting focus, may use Charisma for its attack and damage rolls, and may choose its damage to be Necrotic, Psychic, Radiant, or its normal type; the bond ends if this feature is used again, the weapon is more than 5 feet away for at least 1 minute, or the Warlock dies, and a conjured weapon then disappears.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Eldritch Invocation Options, Pact of the Blade (p. 74) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the weapon bond has explicit distance, replacement, and death limits, and cannot override another creature’s attunement.

rules.statement: Pact of the Chain teaches Find Familiar and lets the Warlock cast it as a Magic action without a spell slot, choosing a normal familiar form or one of the listed special forms. When the Warlock takes the Attack action, they may forgo one of their attacks so the familiar can make one attack using its Reaction.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Eldritch Invocation Options, Pact of the Chain (p. 74) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the familiar’s attack spends one of the Warlock’s attacks, and the summon uses the spell’s rules.

rules.statement: Pact of the Tome creates a Book of Shadows in the Warlock’s hand at the end of a Short or Long Rest; it vanishes if the Warlock creates another or dies. When it appears, the Warlock chooses three cantrips and two level 1 Ritual-tagged spells from any class, not already prepared; while carrying the book, those spells are prepared and count as Warlock spells, and the book can serve as a spellcasting focus.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Eldritch Invocation Options, Pact of the Tome (p. 74) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; access to the chosen spells depends on carrying the book, which is lost on replacement or death.

rules.statement: With the Gaze of Two Minds invocation, a Warlock can use a Bonus Action to touch a willing creature and perceive through its senses until the end of the Warlock’s next turn. The Warlock can extend the connection each subsequent turn with another Bonus Action while both are on the same plane; while connected, the Warlock gains the creature’s special senses and can cast spells as if in either creature’s space if they are within 60 feet of each other.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Eldritch Invocation Options, Gaze of Two Minds (p. 73) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; maintaining perception costs a Bonus Action each turn, and spellcasting through the link has a 60-foot limit.

rules.statement: A Druid can spend a spell slot or a use of Wild Shape as a Magic action to cast Find Familiar without Material components; the familiar is Fey and disappears when the Druid finishes a Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Druid, Level 2: Wild Companion (p. 43) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the casting consumes a spell slot or Wild Shape use, and the familiar has a stated duration.

rules.statement: When the Paladin uses Divine Sense as a Bonus Action, for 10 minutes or until Incapacitated they know the location and creature type of Celestials, Fiends, and Undead within 60 feet, and detect consecrated or desecrated places or objects within that radius.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Paladin, Level 3: Divine Sense (p. 55) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; sensing lasts at most 10 minutes and ends early if the Paladin becomes Incapacitated.

rules.statement: When a Cleric uses Turn Undead, each Undead of their choice within 30 feet makes a Wisdom saving throw; on a failure it is Frightened and Incapacitated for up to 1 minute and tries to move as far from the Cleric as possible on its turns. The effect ends early for that creature if it takes damage, the Cleric becomes Incapacitated, or the Cleric dies.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cleric, Level 2: Channel Divinity—Turn Undead (p. 37) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f00)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; the effect requires a failed save and ends early under the listed conditions.

rules.statement: A warlock’s pact can draw on a mighty fiend from the Lower Planes, whose aims are evil and may ultimately include the warlock’s corruption or destruction. The passage specifies no mechanical price or way for the patron to enforce those aims.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Warlock Subclass: Fiend Patron — Make a Deal with the Lower Planes, p. 76 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: patron influence is a narrative commitment; dial: make enforcement mechanical only if another rule defines it, since this passage gives no enforcement procedure.

rules.statement: When you or someone else reduces an enemy to 0 Hit Points within 10 feet of you, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Warlock level plus your Charisma modifier, with a minimum of 1.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fiend Patron — Dark One’s Blessing, p. 76 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant the stated temporary buffer on the qualifying defeat; dial: its size scales with level and Charisma.

rules.statement: When you make an ability check or saving throw, you can add 1d10 after seeing the roll but before its effects occur. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, minimum once, no more than once per roll; all uses return after a Long Rest.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fiend Patron — Dark One’s Own Luck, p. 76 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow a limited, rest-recharged roll adjustment; dial: the number of uses follows Charisma, reflecting the patron’s limited aid.

rules.statement: After each Short or Long Rest, choose one damage type other than Force; you have Resistance to that type until you choose another using this feature.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fiend Patron — Fiendish Resilience, p. 76 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reduce damage of the selected type through Resistance; dial: the protection adapts only when a rest permits a new choice.

rules.statement: Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll, it must make a Charisma save against your spell save DC or be sent through the Lower Planes until the end of your next turn. A non-Fiend takes 8d10 Psychic damage and the target is Incapacitated until then, after which it returns to its former space or the nearest unoccupied space; regain this feature after a Long Rest, or by expending a Pact Magic spell slot without an action.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fiend Patron — Hurl Through Hell, p. 76 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed save causes temporary planar removal and the stated effects; dial: use is limited by a Long Rest unless a spell-slot resource is spent.

rules.statement: A 10-foot aura prevents spellcasting, Magic actions, and magical effects inside it or affecting things inside it; it also suppresses magic-item properties, blocks effects extending into it, and prevents teleportation and planar travel into or out of it. Portals close temporarily, and ongoing spells are suppressed (except those from an Artifact or deity), with their duration still passing; Dispel Magic does not end the aura.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Antimagic Field, p. 109 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the aura blocks or suppresses the listed magic while Concentration lasts, up to 1 hour; dial: its 10-foot boundary defines the protected space.

rules.statement: A 10-minute casting wards up to 40,000 square feet of floor area to 30 feet high for 1 day, preventing teleportation, portals, and listed planar routes into it. Choose creature types that take 5d10 Radiant or Necrotic damage, chosen at casting, on their first entry each turn or when ending a turn there; a spoken password prevents this damage. Casting it daily at the same site for 30 days makes it last until dispelled and consumes the material component on the final casting.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Forbiddance, p. 134 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: establish the ward for the stated area and duration; dial: repeated costly daily casting can make it permanent until dispelled.

rules.statement: Gate creates a visible, 5-to-20-foot circular portal from a space within 60 feet to a precise location on another plane for up to 1 minute of Concentration; only passage through its front transports anything. Deities and planar rulers can prevent it opening in their presence or domains. Instead, you may name a specific creature on another plane to bring it through; you gain no control over it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Gate, p. 135 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit passage through the open portal; dial: the costly diamond and short Concentration duration constrain access, while powerful planar beings can bar it.

rules.statement: For up to 8 hours, you enter the Border Ethereal and can move in any direction, with each foot of upward or downward travel costing an extra foot. You interact only with the Ethereal Plane and return when the spell ends; if your return space is occupied, you move to the nearest unoccupied space and take Force damage equal to twice the feet moved. The spell ends immediately if cast while already on the Ethereal Plane or on a plane that does not border it.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Etherealness, p. 129 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow travel in the Border Ethereal for the stated duration; dial: vertical movement costs extra and an obstructed return causes damage.

rules.statement: You and up to eight willing creatures project astral forms into the Astral Plane, leaving your bodies Unconscious, ageless, and without need for food or air; each target requires consumed components worth at least 1,100 GP. If an astral form leaves that plane, its body and possessions follow along its silver cord, bringing it into its body on the new plane. If the cord is cut, both forms die; the spell ends for a target whose body or astral form reaches 0 Hit Points, and you can end it for everyone by taking a Magic action.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Astral Projection, p. 111 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: separate projection from the body and allow Astral travel; dial: each target’s costly components and the lethal cord vulnerability make the journey hazardous.

rules.statement: At the end of each of your turns for 1 minute, roll 1d6; on 4–6 you vanish from your plane to the Ethereal Plane, where you can perceive your former plane only in gray and within 60 feet. You return at the start of your next turn or when the spell ends, appearing in a visible unoccupied space within 10 feet of where you vanished, or the nearest unoccupied space if none is available.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Blink, p. 114 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: roll at each turn end to determine temporary planar displacement; dial: the chance is fixed at 3 in 6 and returns are limited by nearby space.

rules.statement: A 1-minute verbal command can compel a creature that understands it if it fails a Wisdom save, giving it the Charmed condition for 30 days. While Charmed, acting directly against the command deals 5d10 Psychic damage, at most once per day; a suicidal command ends the spell, and Remove Curse, Greater Restoration, or Wish also ends it. A 7th- or 8th-level slot extends the duration to 365 days; a 9th-level slot lasts until one of those ending spells is used.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Geas, p. 135 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f01)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: bind the target to a command on a failed save; dial: duration and resistance-breaking damage are bounded, and specific magic can end the binding.

rules.statement: A creature that fails its Charisma save after a one-hour casting is bound to serve for 24 hours; it must follow commands as best it can, though a Hostile creature tries to twist them. Higher-level slots extend service to 10, 30, 180, or 366 days at levels 6 through 9; a summoned or created creature’s other spell is extended to match.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Planar Binding, p. 153 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the service length and task; the caster spends a 1,000+ GP jewel and risks hostile compliance.

rules.statement: A one-hour task costs 1,000 GP per hour, a task measured in minutes costs 100 GP per minute, and a task measured in days costs 10,000 GP per day, up to 10 days. The GM may halve or waive payment for an aligned task, halve it for a nonhazardous one, or require more for a dangerous one; suicidal work is rarely accepted, and failure to agree on a price sends the creature home immediately.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Planar Binding, p. 153 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial payment by duration and circumstances; the bargain costs treasure or a suitably agreed service.

rules.statement: Plane Shift transports you and up to eight willing creatures who link hands to another plane, using a forked metal rod worth 250+ GP attuned to a plane. You arrive at a broadly specified destination as the GM determines, or can target a known teleportation-circle sigil sequence on another plane.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Plane Shift (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial destination precision; planar travel requires a costly, plane-attuned rod and may not land exactly where intended.

rules.statement: After one minute of casting with 50+ GP of consumed rare inks, a portal links your drawn circle to a known permanent circle on the same plane and stays open until the end of your next turn. A caster first learns two Material Plane sequences; a new one can be memorized after one minute of study, and casting at one site daily for 365 days makes a circle permanent.
