locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Teleportation Circle, pp. 168–169 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial network access; travel depends on knowing a destination sequence and consumes rare inks.

rules.statement: A 10-foot-radius, 20-foot-high magic cylinder can bar chosen Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, or Undead from entering nonmagically; entering by teleportation or interplanar travel requires a successful Charisma save. The caster can reverse the effect to bar exit instead, and the circle also impedes attacks and certain mental effects across its boundary.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magic Circle, pp. 145–146 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial which creature types and which direction are barred; the ward costs consumed materials worth 100+ GP and lasts one hour.

rules.statement: A 5-to-100-foot-per-side cube can be warded for 24 hours to block sound, sight through its boundary, divination sensors or targeting, teleportation, and/or planar travel. Recasting it at the same location daily for 365 days makes it last until dispelled.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Private Sanctum, p. 156 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the security properties and area; the spell takes 10 minutes and normally lasts only 24 hours.

rules.statement: A failed Wisdom save imprisons a visible creature until dispelled, preventing aging, eating, drinking, breathing, teleporting, and divination from finding or perceiving it. Choose a prison form and an observable ending trigger likely to occur within a decade; ending it by Dispel Magic requires a level 9 slot and targeting the prison or its creating component.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Imprisonment (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial prison form and trigger; the spell requires a 5,000+ GP statuette and can endure indefinitely if its trigger never occurs.

rules.statement: A 2nd-level spell opens an invisible portal at a touched rope into an extradimensional space that holds up to eight Medium or smaller creatures for one hour. Effects cannot pass through the portal, and everything inside falls out when the spell ends.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rope Trick, p. 159 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial who enters; the shelter is temporary, limited in capacity, and releases its contents when it ends.

rules.statement: A 4th-level spell can hide a touched chest and up to 12 cubic feet of nonliving contents on the Ethereal Plane; touching its miniature replica recalls it, and touching both chest and replica sends it back. After 60 days, the spell has a cumulative 5% chance each day to end; it also ends if recast or if the replica is destroyed, potentially leaving the chest on the Ethereal Plane.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Secret Chest, p. 160 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the storage duration; the chest and replica require costly materials, and the hidden chest can be lost.

rules.statement: A soul residing in the spell’s container can project up to 100 feet to return to its own body or try to possess a visible Humanoid. On a failed Charisma save, the caster controls the host and the host’s soul is trapped in the container; if the host dies, the caster must save against its own spell DC to return to the container or die.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Magic Jar (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial whether possession succeeds; the caster risks its body and life, while a resisting target can block another attempt for 24 hours.

rules.statement: Scrying can target a creature on the same plane or a location the caster has seen; a creature’s Wisdom save is modified by familiarity (+5 secondhand, 0 firsthand, −5 extensive) and connection (−2 likeness, −4 possession, −10 body part). On a failed save an invisible sensor tracks the creature within 10 feet for up to 10 minutes; on a success the target is unaffected and cannot be targeted again for 24 hours.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Scrying, p. 160 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the strength of the connection; the target may resist, and the spell only reaches creatures on the caster’s plane.

rules.statement: A creature that returns from death loses attunement to every magic item it had attuned. A dead creature’s spirit knows who is attempting to revive it and may refuse to return.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dead, p. 181 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial whether the spirit consents; revival can cost existing item bonds and depends on the spirit’s willingness.

rules.statement: While Deafened, a creature cannot hear and automatically fails ability checks that require hearing.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Deafened [Condition], p. 181 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f02)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial duration by its causing effect; the condition imposes a hearing-based penalty while it lasts.

rules.statement: Teleportation moves a creature instantly without crossing intervening space, spending no movement unless the effect says otherwise and provoking no Opportunity Attacks. Its carried and worn equipment travels with it, but a creature it touches does not unless specified; an occupied or blocked destination instead places it in the nearest unoccupied space of its choice.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Teleportation (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial destination precision; blocked destinations redirect rather than stop travel.

rules.statement: While wearing the amulet, the user can take a Magic action to name a familiar location on another plane and make a DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check to use Plane Shift. On a failure, the user and each creature and object within 15 feet travel to a randomly determined destination, with the table weighting the named plane most heavily and also including other planes and the Astral Plane.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Amulet of the Planes (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; risky planar transit; a failed check carries nearby creatures and objects to an uncertain destination.

rules.statement: When first lit, the attuned candle can instead be consumed to cast Gate, creating a portal to an Outer Plane selected by the GM or randomly from the listed table. While it burns, its light also grants Advantage on D20 Tests to creatures within it, and lets Clerics and Druids there cast prepared level 1 spells without spending spell slots.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Candle of Invocation (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; the planar portal costs the candle permanently, while its lesser benefits are limited to its burn time.

rules.statement: The cube has three charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. Spending one charge opens a Gate to the plane keyed to a chosen face; pressing that face twice instead spends one charge to use Plane Shift to transport the targets to that plane.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Cubic Gate (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial destination access; use is constrained by keyed planes and a renewable charge supply.

rules.statement: When a Wizard using the attuned hat tries to cast an eligible level 1 or higher Wizard spell they do not know, they spend a spell slot of that level and make an Intelligence (Arcana) check against DC 10 plus the spell’s level. Success casts the spell and bars another attempt with this property until a Short or Long Rest; failure instead triggers a random table result, ranging from an unintended spell or condition to an object, creature, or temporary portal.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Hat of Many Spells, Unknown Spell (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; uncertain spell use; failure consumes the slot but substitutes a randomly determined outcome.

rules.statement: While attuned, the wearer can try to control the Dragon Orb with a Magic action and a DC 15 Charisma saving throw. Success grants control while attunement continues; failure makes the orb impose Charmed for that duration, prevents voluntarily ending attunement, and lets it cast Suggestion on the wearer at will.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dragon Orb (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; the orb offers powerful use at the risk of enduring coercion and inability to end the bond voluntarily.

rules.statement: The shackles can be applied with a Utilize action to an Incapacitated creature of Small through Large size and prevent its extradimensional movement, including teleportation and planar travel, but not passage through an interdimensional portal. The wearer or a designated creature can remove them with a Utilize action; once every 30 days, the captive can try a DC 30 Strength (Athletics) check to break them.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Dimensional Shackles (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; confinement blocks most dimensional escape, but leaves portals and rare physical escape attempts possible.

rules.statement: An activated mirror can trap a creature that sees its reflection within 30 feet if it fails a DC 15 Charisma save; it and its carried or worn belongings enter one of twelve extradimensional cells. A trapped creature can escape through planar-travel magic or be freed by the mirror’s command; if the mirror is shattered, all prisoners emerge nearby.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mirror of Life Trapping (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; capture depends on reflection and a failed save, while escape otherwise requires magic or outside intervention.

rules.statement: For supernatural fear, the GM typically calls for a Wisdom save with a DC suited to the threat; the examples range from DC 10 to DC 20. A Frightened creature typically repeats the save at the end of each turn, ending the effect on a success, and the GM may add further effects while it lasts.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fear and Mental Stress, Fear Effects (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; fear intensity and optional extra effects depend on the threat and the GM’s judgment.

rules.statement: Intense mental stress is typically represented by Psychic damage resisted with a suitable Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma save; examples pair DCs 10, 15, and 20 with 1d6, 3d6, and 9d6 damage. A successful save may halve damage at the GM’s discretion; prolonged effects can impose a condition for 1d10 minutes, suppressible by Calm Emotions or removable by Lesser Restoration.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Fear and Mental Stress, Mental Stress Effects; Prolonged Effects (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f03)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: dial; damage, save ability, and prolonged consequences vary with the source and severity of stress.

rules.statement: A Portable Hole opens into a 10-foot-deep space on another plane, but it does not create an open passage to that plane. Folding it shut traps its contents; a creature inside can force its way out with an action and a successful DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check, appearing within 5 feet of the hole. The closed space contains enough air for 1 hour divided by the number of breathing creatures inside.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Portable Hole, p. 235 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the air supply and escape check; confinement costs time and can threaten breathing creatures.

rules.statement: Putting a Portable Hole inside an extradimensional space made by a Bag of Holding, Handy Haversack, or similar item destroys both items and opens a one-way gate to a random Astral Plane location. Creatures within 10 feet that lack Total Cover are pulled through; the gate then closes and cannot be reopened.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Portable Hole, p. 235 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the random destination; the cost is destroying both storage items and risking nearby creatures.

rules.statement: A Well of Many Worlds opens a two-way, 6-foot-diameter portal to a world or plane chosen by the GM. A creature within 5 feet can close it by taking a Magic action to fold the cloth; after opening a portal, the item cannot open another for 1d8 hours.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Well of Many Worlds, p. 253 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the destination; access depends on an external destination choice and incurs a recharge delay.

rules.statement: When a Sphere of Annihilation contacts a planar portal or extradimensional space, roll d100: on 1–50 the sphere is destroyed; on 51–85 it passes through; on 86–100 a rift sends the sphere and every creature and object within 180 feet to a random plane.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphere of Annihilation, p. 245 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the d100 outcome; interacting with a portal risks destroying the sphere or displacing a wide area.

rules.statement: While wearing the Robe of Stars, you can take a Magic action to enter the Astral Plane with everything you wear and carry. You remain there until you take a Magic action to return, reappearing in your last space or the nearest unoccupied space if it is occupied.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Robe of Stars, p. 240 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the return location only when the original space is occupied; travel costs actions and may displace you on return.

rules.statement: Before drawing from a Mysterious Deck, declare how many cards you will draw, then draw randomly; each card's magic takes effect immediately, and extra cards beyond the declared number do nothing. Draws must be no more than 1 hour apart; if you fail to complete the declared number, the remaining cards fly out and take effect together. Drawn cards disappear, but most return to the deck; the Fool and Jester do not.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Mysterious Deck, p. 231 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the drawn cards; the cost is committing to a number and accepting uncontrolled effects if the sequence is unfinished.

rules.statement: When the listed d100 effect table is used, its result can trigger a spell or other effect at a chosen point, or redirect an effect onto the user. Results include damage, conditions, a creature appearing, an object vanishing into the Ethereal Plane, or a target turning to stone; the table specifies the individual ranges and durations.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Effect table, p. 252 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the table roll; the cost is surrendering control of the exact effect and sometimes accepting a redirected effect.

rules.statement: A hag holding or carrying her soul bag can use Nightmare Haunting once per day from the Ethereal Plane against a visible Material Plane creature. If the target dies from the Dream spell's damage, its soul is trapped in the bag and it cannot be raised until that soul is released; destroying the bag releases its stored souls, and the hag can make a replacement after 7 days.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Night Hag, p. 311 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the target and bag vulnerability; the hag must possess the bag and reach the Ethereal Plane, while destroying it frees trapped souls.

rules.statement: A Robe of Eyes grants Advantage on sight-based Wisdom (Perception) checks, Darkvision, and Truesight out to 120 feet. A Light spell cast on the robe or a Daylight spell cast within 5 feet blinds its wearer for 1 minute; at the end of each turn, a Constitution save (DC 11 or 15 respectively) can end the condition.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Robe of Eyes, p. 240 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the save DC by spell; enhanced perception carries a specific vulnerability and possible loss of sight.

rules.statement: A Robe of Scintillating Colors has 3 charges and regains 1d3 at dawn. Spending 1 charge makes it shine brightly in a 30-foot radius and dimly for another 30 feet until the end of your next turn; creatures that can see you have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you, and those in the bright light that see the activation must pass a DC 15 Wisdom save or be Stunned until the effect ends.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Robe of Scintillating Colors, p. 240 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial the daily charge recovery; the effect is brief and limited by a finite charge reserve.

rules.statement: A Winged Boot wearer can spend 1 of its 4 charges as a Magic action to gain a 30-foot Fly Speed for 1 hour; charges recover at dawn by 1d4. If flight expires while the wearer is airborne, the wearer descends 30 feet per round until landing.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Winged Boots, p. 253 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial daily charge recovery; flight is time-limited, and an airborne wearer must descend after it ends.

rules.statement: A Sphere of Annihilation destroys matter it passes through, except for Artifacts not susceptible to its damage; anything it touches without being wholly engulfed takes 8d10 Force damage. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by its controlled movement is obliterated, leaving possessions but no physical remains.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphere of Annihilation, p. 245 (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f04)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: default; dial whether an Artifact is susceptible; contact risks massive damage or complete bodily destruction.

rules.statement: A pirate captain can force one creature it can see within 30 feet to make a DC 12 Wisdom save; on a failure, the creature is Charmed until the start of the captain’s next turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Pirate Captain, Enthralling Panache (p. 318) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: brief control lasts only until the captain’s next turn.

rules.statement: A rakshasa automatically succeeds on saves against spells and other magical effects, and spell attack rolls automatically miss it. Without its permission, spells cannot observe it remotely or detect its thoughts, creature type, or alignment.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rakshasa, Greater Magic Resistance (p. 318) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: powerful magical defense is built into the creature; its scope is limited to magical effects and observation.

rules.statement: If a rakshasa dies outside the Nine Hells, its body becomes ichor and it instantly revives at full Hit Points in a new body somewhere in the Nine Hells.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rakshasa, Fiendish Restoration (p. 318) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: death relocates and restores the creature, but only in its designated plane.

rules.statement: A rakshasa’s successful Cursed Touch deals 2d6 + 5 slashing damage and 3d12 necrotic damage; a creature hit is cursed and gains no benefit from finishing a Short or Long Rest while the curse lasts.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rakshasa, Cursed Touch (p. 318) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the curse impairs recovery; the passage gives no duration or removal rule.

rules.statement: On a recharge roll of 5–6, a rakshasa can make each enemy in a 30-foot emanation save against DC 18 Wisdom; a failure deals 8d6 psychic damage and causes Frightened and Incapacitated until the start of the rakshasa’s next turn.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rakshasa, Baleful Command (p. 318) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is limited by a recharge trigger and ends at the rakshasa’s next turn.

rules.statement: A rakshasa can cast Detect Magic, Detect Thoughts, Disguise Self, Mage Hand, or Minor Illusion at will, and can cast Fly, Invisibility, Major Image, or Plane Shift once each per day. These spells require no Material components and use Charisma, with spell save DC 18.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Rakshasa, Spellcasting (p. 318) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: listed spells are constrained by at-will or once-per-day availability; Plane Shift has no further travel procedure here.

rules.statement: A red dragon wyrmling’s Fire Breath recharges on a roll of 5–6; each creature in a 15-foot cone makes a DC 13 Dexterity save, taking 7d6 fire damage on a failure or half as much on a success.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Red Dragon Wyrmling, Fire Breath (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the attack uses a fixed area and damage, with repeat use gated by recharge.

rules.statement: A sphinx of lore can use its reaction twice per day when it or another creature within 30 feet makes an ability check or saving throw, adding 2 to the roll.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphinx of Lore, Burst of Ingenuity (p. 328) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the bonus is small and has a strict daily use limit.

rules.statement: Magic cannot observe a sphinx of lore remotely or detect its thoughts without permission; attempts to judge its intentions or sincerity with Wisdom (Insight) have Disadvantage.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphinx of Lore, Inscrutable (p. 328) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: privacy protection applies to magical observation and imposes a specific penalty on Insight.

rules.statement: A sphinx of lore can spend a legendary action after another creature’s turn to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space it can see and make one Claw attack. It has three legendary-action uses, or four in its lair, and regains expended uses at the start of each of its turns.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphinx of Lore, Legendary Actions (p. 328) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: short-range teleport and attack consume a limited action pool that refreshes each turn.

rules.statement: A sphinx of lore can force one visible creature within 120 feet to make a DC 16 Constitution save; on a failure, it gains one Exhaustion level and appears 3d10 years older while it has any Exhaustion. The sphinx cannot use this action again until the start of its next turn, whether the save succeeds or fails.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphinx of Lore, Weight of Years (p. 328) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the aging appearance accompanies Exhaustion, while the action has a one-turn lockout.

rules.statement: A sphinx of valor’s magical roar has a different effect each time it roars, with the sequence resetting after a Long Rest; it can roar three times per day. The passage gives the first roar’s effect: each enemy in a 500-foot emanation makes a DC 20 Wisdom save or becomes Frightened.
locators: D&D 5.2.1 SRD: Sphinx of Valor, Roar (p. 328) (dnd-srd-5.2.1#f05)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effects are sequenced and reset by rest, but only the first effect is specified in this passage.
